sourceText: AlloyDB is a fully managed relational database service that offers high performance, seamless integration, and impressive scalability. AlloyDB is 100% compatible with PostgreSQL. Extend your database application to build AI-powered experiences leveraging AlloyDB’s LlamaIndex integrations. This notebook goes over how to use AlloyDB for PostgreSQL to store vector embeddings with the AlloyDBVectorStore class. Learn more about the package on GitHub. Open In Colab Before you begin To run this notebook, you will need to do the following: - Create a Google Cloud Project - Enable the AlloyDB API - Create a AlloyDB cluster and instance. - Create a AlloyDB database. - Add a User to the database. 🦙 Library Installation Install the integration library, llama-index-alloydb-pg, and the library for the embedding service, llama-index-embeddings-vertex. Colab only: Uncomment the following cell to restart the kernel or use the button to restart the kernel. For Vertex AI Workbench you can restart the terminal using the button on top. 🔐 Authentication Authenticate to Google Cloud as the IAM user logged into this notebook in order to access your Google Cloud Project. - If you are using Colab to run this notebook, use the cell below and continue. - If you are using Vertex AI Workbench, check out the setup instructions here. ☁ Set Your Google Cloud Project Set your Google Cloud project so that you can leverage Google Cloud resources within this notebook. If you don’t know your project ID, try the following: - Run gcloud config list. - Run gcloud projects list. - See the support page: Locate the project ID. Basic Usage Set AlloyDB database values Find your database values, in the AlloyDB Instances page. AlloyDBEngine Connection Pool One of the requirements and arguments to establish AlloyDB as a vector store is a AlloyDBEngine object. The AlloyDBEngine configures a connection pool to your AlloyDB database, enabling successful connections from your application and following industry best practices. To create a AlloyDBEngine using AlloyDBEngine.from instance() you need to provide only 5 things: 1. project id : Project ID of the Google Cloud Project where the AlloyDB instance is located. 2. region : Region where the AlloyDB instance is located. 3. cluster: The name of the AlloyDB cluster. 4. instance : The name of the AlloyDB instance. 5. database : The name of the database to connect to on the AlloyDB instance. By default, IAM database authentication will be used as the method of database authentication. This library uses the IAM principal belonging to the Application Default Credentials (ADC) sourced from the environment. Optionally, built-in database authentication using a username and password to access the AlloyDB database can also be used. Just provide the optional user and password arguments to AlloyDBEngine.from instance(): - user : Database user to use for built-in database authentication and login - password : Database password to use for built-in database authentication and login. Note: This tutorial demonstrates the async interface. All async methods have corresponding sync methods. AlloyDBEngine for AlloyDB Omni To create an AlloyDBEngine for AlloyDB Omni, you will need a connection url. AlloyDBEngine.from connection string first creates an async engine and then turns it into an AlloyDBEngine. Here is an example connection with the asyncpg driver: Initialize a table The AlloyDBVectorStore class requires a database table. The AlloyDBEngine engine has a helper method init vector store table() that can be used to create a table with the proper schema for you. Optional Tip: 💡 You can also specify a schema name by passing schema name wherever you pass table name. Create an embedding class instance You can use any Llama Index embeddings model. You may need to enable Vertex AI API to use VertexTextEmbeddings. We recommend setting the embedding model’s version for production, learn more about the Text embeddings models. Initialize a default AlloyDBVectorStore Download data Load documents Use with VectorStoreIndex Create an index from the vector store by using VectorStoreIndex. Initialize Vector Store with documents The simplest way to use a Vector Store is to load a set of documents and build an index from them using from documents. Query the index Create a custom Vector Store A Vector Store can take advantage of relational data to filter similarity searches. Create a new table with custom metadata columns. You can also re-use an existing table which already has custom columns for a Document’s id, content, embedding, and/or metadata. Add documents with metadata Document metadata can provide the LLM and retrieval process with more information. Learn more about different approaches for extracting and adding metadata. Search for documents with metadata filter You can apply pre-filtering to the search results by specifying a filters argument Add a Index Speed up vector search queries by applying a vector index. Learn more about vector indexes. The ScaNN index creation (only available in AlloyDB Omni) requires sufficient maintenance work memory. You need to set the database flag maintenance work mem by calling set maintenance work mem before applying the index. Re-index Remove an index

sourceText: Baidu VectorDB is a robust, enterprise-level distributed database service, meticulously developed and fully managed by Baidu Intelligent Cloud. It stands out for its exceptional ability to store, retrieve, and analyze multi-dimensional vector data. At its core, VectorDB operates on Baidu’s proprietary “Mochow” vector database kernel, which ensures high performance, availability, and security, alongside remarkable scalability and user-friendliness. This database service supports a diverse range of index types and similarity calculation methods, catering to various use cases. A standout feature of VectorDB is its capacity to manage an immense vector scale of up to 10 billion, while maintaining impressive query performance, supporting millions of queries per second (QPS) with millisecond-level query latency. This notebook shows the basic usage of BaiduVectorDB as a Vector Store in LlamaIndex. To run, you should have a Database instance. Setup If you’re opening this Notebook on colab, you will probably need to install LlamaIndex 🦙. Please provide OpenAI access key In order use embeddings by OpenAI you need to supply an OpenAI API Key: Download Data Creating and populating the Vector Store You will now load some essays by Paul Graham from a local file and store them into the Baidu VectorDB. Initialize the Baidu VectorDB Creation of the vector store entails creation of the underlying database collection if it does not exist yet: Now wrap this store into an index LlamaIndex abstraction for later querying: Note that the above from documents call does several things at once: it splits the input documents into chunks of manageable size (“nodes”), computes embedding vectors for each node, and stores them all in the Baidu VectorDB. Querying the store Basic querying MMR-based queries The MMR (maximal marginal relevance) method is designed to fetch text chunks from the store that are at the same time relevant to the query but as different as possible from each other, with the goal of providing a broader context to the building of the final answer: Connecting to an existing store Since this store is backed by Baidu VectorDB, it is persistent by definition. So, if you want to connect to a store that was created and populated previously, here is how: Metadata filtering The Baidu VectorDB vector store support metadata filtering in the form of exact-match key=value pairs at query time. The following cells, which work on a brand new collection, demonstrate this feature. In this demo, for the sake of brevity, a single source document is loaded (the ../data/paul graham/paul graham essay.txt text file). Nevertheless, you will attach some custom metadata to the document to illustrate how you can can restrict queries with conditions on the metadata attached to the documents.

text: Apache Cassandra 是一個 NoSQL、行式、高度可擴展且高可用性的資料庫。從 5.0 版本開始，該資料庫就具備了 向量搜尋 功能。 DataStax Astra DB through CQL 是一個建於 Cassandra 的託管無伺服器資料庫，提供相同的介面和優勢。 本筆筆記展示了在 LlamaIndex 中使用 Cassandra Vector Store 的基本用法。 要執行完整的程式碼，您需要一個配備 Vector Search 功能的運行中的 Cassandra cluster 或一個 DataStax Astra DB 實例。 設定 下一步是使用全局 DB 連線初始化 CassIO：這是針對 Cassandra cluster 和 Astra DB 略有不同的步驟： 初始化 (Cassandra cluster) 此時，您需要先建立一個 cassandra.cluster.Session 物件，如 Cassandra driver documentation 中所述。細節有所不同（例如網路 settings 和驗證），但可能類似於： 初始化 (Astra DB through CQL) 此時，您使用以下連線參數初始化 CassIO： - 資料庫 ID，例如 01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef - Token，例如 AstraCS:6gBhNmsk135…（必須是「Database Administrator」token） - 可選的 Keyspace 名稱（如果省略，將使用資料庫的預設值） OpenAI key 為了使用 OpenAI 的 embeddings，您需要提供一個 OpenAI API Key： 下載資料 建立和填充 Vector Store 您現在將從本地檔案載入 Paul Graham 的一些文章，並將它們儲存到 Cassandra Vector Store 中。 初始化 Cassandra Vector Store 建立 vector store 涉及在尚不存在時建立底層資料庫表： 然後將此 store 包裝成一個 index LlamaIndex 抽象，以便後續查詢： 請注意，上述 from documents 呼叫會同時執行多項操作：它將輸入 documents 分割成可管理的區塊（「nodes」），為每個 node 計算 embedding vectors，並將它們全部儲存在 Cassandra Vector Store 中。 查詢 store 基本查詢 基於 MMR 的查詢 MMR (maximal marginal relevance) 方法旨在從 store 中擷取同時與查詢相關，但彼此之間差異最大的文本區塊，目的是為最終答案的建構提供更廣泛的上下文： 連接到現有的 store 由於此 store 由 Cassandra 支援，它在定義上是持久性的。因此，如果您想連接到先前建立和填充過的 store，請按以下方式操作： 從索引中移除 documents 首先，從由索引生成的 Retriever 中取得 document 的明確清單，或「nodes」： 但請注意！在使用 vector store 時，您應該將 document 視為應刪除的合理單元，而不是屬於它的任何單個 node。在這個案例中，您只插入了一個單一的文字檔案，因此所有 nodes 都具有相同的 ref doc id： 現在假設您需要移除您上傳的文字檔案： 重複完全相同的查詢並檢查結果。您應該會看到 沒有結果 被找到： Metadata 篩選Cassandra 向量資料庫支援在查詢時以精確匹配的 key=value 對的方式進行元資料過濾。以下儲存格將在一個全新的 Cassandra 表格上展示此功能。 在此示範中，為了簡潔起見，載入單一來源 document（../data/paul graham/paul graham essay.txt 文字檔案）。儘管如此，您仍可以將自訂元資料附加到 document，以說明如何根據附加到 documents 的元資料來限制查詢。 就是這樣：您現在可以在查詢引擎中新增過濾條件： 為了測試過濾功能，嘗試將其更改為僅使用 "dinos" documents……這次將不會有答案 :)
sourceText: Apache Cassandra® is a NoSQL, row-oriented, highly scalable and highly available database. Starting with version 5.0, the database ships with vector search capabilities. DataStax Astra DB through CQL is a managed serverless database built on Cassandra, offering the same interface and strengths. This notebook shows the basic usage of the Cassandra Vector Store in LlamaIndex. To run the full code you need either a running Cassandra cluster equipped with Vector Search capabilities or a DataStax Astra DB instance. Setup The next step is to initialize CassIO with a global DB connection: this is the only step that is done slightly differently for a Cassandra cluster and Astra DB: Initialization (Cassandra cluster) In this case, you first need to create a cassandra.cluster.Session object, as described in the Cassandra driver documentation. The details vary (e.g. with network settings and authentication), but this might be something like: Initialization (Astra DB through CQL) In this case you initialize CassIO with the following connection parameters: - the Database ID, e.g. 01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef - the Token, e.g. AstraCS:6gBhNmsk135… (it must be a “Database Administrator” token) - Optionally a Keyspace name (if omitted, the default one for the database will be used) OpenAI key In order to use embeddings by OpenAI you need to supply an OpenAI API Key: Download data Creating and populating the Vector Store You will now load some essays by Paul Graham from a local file and store them into the Cassandra Vector Store. Initialize the Cassandra Vector Store Creation of the vector store entails creation of the underlying database table if it does not exist yet: Now wrap this store into an index LlamaIndex abstraction for later querying: Note that the above from documents call does several things at once: it splits the input documents into chunks of manageable size (“nodes”), computes embedding vectors for each node, and stores them all in the Cassandra Vector Store. Querying the store Basic querying MMR-based queries The MMR (maximal marginal relevance) method is designed to fetch text chunks from the store that are at the same time relevant to the query but as different as possible from each other, with the goal of providing a broader context to the building of the final answer: Connecting to an existing store Since this store is backed by Cassandra, it is persistent by definition. So, if you want to connect to a store that was created and populated previously, here is how: Removing documents from the index First get an explicit list of pieces of a document, or “nodes”, from a Retriever spawned from the index: But wait! When using the vector store, you should consider the document as the sensible unit to delete, and not any individual node belonging to it. Well, in this case, you just inserted a single text file, so all nodes will have the same ref doc id: Now let’s say you need to remove the text file you uploaded: Repeat the very same query and check the results now. You should see no results being found: Metadata filtering The Cassandra vector store support metadata filtering in the form of exact-match key=value pairs at query time. The following cells, which work on a brand new Cassandra table, demonstrate this feature. In this demo, for the sake of brevity, a single source document is loaded (the ../data/paul graham/paul graham essay.txt text file). Nevertheless, you will attach some custom metadata to the document to illustrate how you can can restrict queries with conditions on the metadata attached to the documents. That’s it: you can now add filtering to your query engine: To test that the filtering is at play, try to change it to use only "dinos" documents… there will be no answer this time :)

text: 此範例取自 ChromaIndex 範例，以及如何使用 Nomic 的 Matryoshka embedding 搭配 Fireworks.ai。 Chroma Chroma 是一個專注於開發者生產力和幸福感的 AI 原生開源向量資料庫。Chroma 依 Apache 2.0 授權。 Discord License Integration Tests - Website - Documentation - Twitter - Discord Chroma 完整型別、完整測試和完整文件。 使用以下方式安裝 Chroma： 終端機視窗 Chroma 以各種模式運行。請參閱下方每個整合與 LangChain 的範例。 - in-memory - 在 python 腳本或 jupyter notebook 中 - in-memory with persistence - 在腳本或 notebook 中並儲存/載入到磁碟 - in a docker container - 作為伺服器運行您的本機機器或在雲端 像任何其他資料庫一樣，您可以： - .add - .get - .update - .upsert - .delete - .peek - 以及 .query 運行相似度搜尋。 在 文件 查看完整文件。 Nomic Nomic 發布了新的 embedding model nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5，它能夠根據您對成本的敏感度返回可變的 embedding size。欲了解更多資訊，請查看他們的模型 此處 和他們的網站 此處。 Fireworks.ai Fireworks 是領先的 OSS model inference provider。在本次範例中，我們將使用 Fireworks 來運行 nomic 模型以及 mixtral-8x7b-instruct 模型作為 query engine。欲了解更多關於 fireworks 的資訊，請查看他們的網站 此處。 基本範例 在這個基本範例中，我們取了 Paul Graham 的文章，將其分割成區塊，使用開源 embedding model 進行 embedding，將其載入到 Chroma 中，然後進行查詢。 如果您在 colab 上開啟此 Notebook，您可能需要安裝 LlamaIndex 🦙。 建立一個 Chroma Index 下載資料 作者在成長過程中主要從事寫作和編程。他開始寫短篇故事，承認它們並不好，並在九年級嘗試在 IBM 1401 上編程。然而，由於缺乏輸入資料，他發現這很令人困惑，因為他無法弄清楚該做什麼。他第一次重要的編程經驗是微電腦的出現，他可以在桌上使用並立即收到回應。他自己建了一個微電腦，後來說服他的父親購買了一台 TRS-80。他編寫了簡單的遊戲、一個預測火箭飛行的程式和一個文字處理器。儘管對編程有興趣，他最初計劃在大學學習哲學，但最終轉向 AI。 基本範例（包含儲存到磁碟）和可調整大小的 embedding 擴展前一個範例，如果您想儲存到磁碟，只需初始化 Chroma client 並將您希望儲存資料的目錄傳遞給它。 Caution: Chroma 會盡力自動將資料儲存到磁碟，然而多個記憶體中的 client 會互相干擾。作為最佳實踐，在任何給定時間點，每個路徑只保留一個 client。 我們還將 embedding 縮小到 128 維度。這對於在資料庫方面注重成本的情況很有幫助。 作者在童年和青少年時期，在學校以外的兩方面進行了工作：寫作和程式設計。他們最初開始寫短篇故事，這些故事的劇情很少，更側重於具有強烈情感的角色。他們在國中時，在地下室的 IBM 1401 電腦上開始進行程式設計，當時他們使用早期版本的 Fortran 編寫程式，並使用 punch cards 執行。然而，由於缺乏輸入資料和有限的數學知識，他們覺得這很有挑戰性。微型電腦的出現顯著改變了他們對程式設計的體驗，使其變得更具互動性和吸引力。他們獲得了一台 TRS-80 微型電腦，並編寫了簡單的遊戲、一個預測模型火箭飛行的程式，以及一個文字處理器。儘管對程式設計有興趣，他們最初計劃在大學學習哲學，然後轉向 AI。 您可以看到兩者的結果是相同的，因此您可以自行實驗維度大小，然後再自行實驗成本與品質的權衡。

Caution: Chroma makes a best-effort to automatically save data to disk, however multiple in-memory clients can stomp each other’s work. title: 從向量資料庫自動檢索
text: 本指南說明如何在 LlamaIndex 中執行 auto-retrieval 。 許多流行的 vector dbs 除了查詢字串外，還支援一組 metadata filters 用於 semantic search。對於自然語言查詢，我們首先使用 LLM 推斷一組 metadata filters 以及應傳遞給 vector db 的正確查詢字串（此查詢字串也可以是空白的）。然後，這個整體查詢組合會對 vector db 執行。 這使得我們能夠實現超越 top-k semantic search 的更動態、更具表達性的檢索方式。給定查詢的相關上下文可能僅需要對 metadata tag 進行過濾，或者需要對過濾後的集合進行 filtering + semantic search 的組合，或者僅僅是原始的 semantic search。 我們以 Chroma 為例進行演示，但 auto-retrieval 也已實作於許多其他 vector dbs（例如 Pinecone、Weaviate 等）。 設定 我們首先定義 imports 並定義一個空的 Chroma collection。 如果您在 colab 上開啟此 Notebook，您可能需要安裝 LlamaIndex 🦙。 定義一些範例資料 我們將一些包含文字區塊的範例 nodes 插入到 vector database 中。請注意，每個 TextNode 不僅包含文字，還包含 metadata，例如 category 和 country。這些 metadata 欄位將在底層 vector db 中被轉換/儲存為此格式。 使用 Chroma Vector Store 建構 Vector Index 在這裡，我們將資料載入到 vector store 中。如上所述，每個 node 的文字和 metadata 都會被轉換成 Chroma 中的對應表示。現在我們可以在 Chroma 中對此資料執行 semantic 查詢和 metadata filtering。 定義 VectorIndexAutoRetriever 我們定義我們的核心 VectorIndexAutoRetriever 模組。該模組接收 VectorStoreInfo，其中包含 vector store collection 的結構化描述及其支援的 metadata filters。此資訊將用於 auto-retrieval prompt 中，其中 LLM 推斷 metadata filters。 對一些範例資料進行運行 我們嘗試對一些範例資料進行運行。請注意 metadata filters 是如何被推斷的——這有助於更精確的檢索！
sourceText: This guide shows how to perform auto-retrieval in LlamaIndex. Many popular vector dbs support a set of metadata filters in addition to a query string for semantic search. Given a natural language query, we first use the LLM to infer a set of metadata filters as well as the right query string to pass to the vector db (either can also be blank). This overall query bundle is then executed against the vector db. This allows for more dynamic, expressive forms of retrieval beyond top-k semantic search. The relevant context for a given query may only require filtering on a metadata tag, or require a joint combination of filtering + semantic search within the filtered set, or just raw semantic search. We demonstrate an example with Chroma, but auto-retrieval is also implemented with many other vector dbs (e.g. Pinecone, Weaviate, and more). Setup We first define imports and define an empty Chroma collection. If you’re opening this Notebook on colab, you will probably need to install LlamaIndex 🦙. Defining Some Sample Data We insert some sample nodes containing text chunks into the vector database. Note that each TextNode not only contains the text, but also metadata e.g. category and country. These metadata fields will get converted/stored as such in the underlying vector db. Build Vector Index with Chroma Vector Store Here we load the data into the vector store. As mentioned above, both the text and metadata for each node will get converted into corresponding representations in Chroma. We can now run semantic queries and also metadata filtering on this data from Chroma. Define VectorIndexAutoRetriever We define our core VectorIndexAutoRetriever module. The module takes in VectorStoreInfo, which contains a structured description of the vector store collection and the metadata filters it supports. This information will then be used in the auto-retrieval prompt where the LLM infers metadata filters. Running over some sample data We try running over some sample data. Note how metadata filters are inferred - this helps with more precise retrieval!

title: Google Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL - `PostgresVectorStore`
text: Cloud SQL 是一個完全託管的關聯式資料庫服務，提供高性能、無縫整合和令人印象深刻的可擴展性。它提供 MySQL、PostgreSQL 和 SQL Server 資料庫引擎。擴展您的資料庫應用程式，利用 Cloud SQL 的 LlamaIndex 整合來建立 AI 驅動的體驗。 本筆筆記將介紹如何使用 Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 來使用 PostgresVectorStore 類別來儲存 vector embeddings。 在 GitHub 上了解更多關於此套件的資訊。 Open In Colab 開始之前 要執行本筆記，您需要完成以下操作： - 建立一個 Google Cloud Project - 啟用 Cloud SQL Admin API。 - 建立一個 Cloud SQL instance。 - 建立一個 Cloud SQL database。 - 向資料庫新增一個使用者。 🦙 函式庫安裝 安裝整合函式庫 llama-index-cloud-sql-pg，以及用於 embedding 服務的函式庫 llama-index-embeddings-vertex。 僅限 Colab： 取消註解以下儲存格以重新啟動核心，或使用按鈕重新啟動核心。對於 Vertex AI Workbench，您可以使用頂部的按鈕重新啟動終端機。 🔐 驗證 以登入本筆記的 IAM 使用者身份驗證 Google Cloud，以便存取您的 Google Cloud Project。 - 如果您使用 Colab 執行本筆記，請使用下面的儲存格並繼續。 - 如果您使用 Vertex AI Workbench，請參閱設定說明 這裡。 ☁ 設定您的 Google Cloud Project 設定您的 Google Cloud Project，以便在本筆記中利用 Google Cloud 資源。 如果您不知道您的專案 ID，請嘗試以下操作： - 執行 gcloud config list。 - 執行 gcloud projects list。 - 查看支援頁面：尋找專案 ID。 基本用法 設定 Cloud SQL 資料庫值 請在 Cloud SQL Instances 頁面 中找到您的資料庫值。 PostgresEngine Connection Pool 建立 Cloud SQL 作為 vector store 的要求和參數之一是 PostgresEngine 物件。PostgresEngine 會為您的 Cloud SQL 資料庫配置一個 connection pool，從而實現應用程式的成功連線並遵循產業最佳實踐。 要使用 PostgresEngine.from instance() 建立一個 PostgresEngine，您只需要提供以下 4 件事： 1. project id：Cloud SQL instance 所在的 Google Cloud Project 的 Project ID。 2. region：Cloud SQL instance 所在的區域 (Region)。 3. instance：Cloud SQL instance 的名稱。 4. database：在 Cloud SQL instance 上要連線的資料庫名稱。 預設情況下，IAM database authentication 將作為資料庫驗證的方法。此函式庫使用從環境中取得的 Application Default Credentials (ADC) 所屬的 IAM principal。 有關 IAM database authentication 的更多資訊，請參閱： - 設定一個用於 IAM database authentication 的 instance - 使用 IAM database authentication 管理使用者 可選地，也可以使用使用使用者名稱和密碼的 built-in database authentication 來存取 Cloud SQL 資料庫。只需向 PostgresEngine.from instance() 提供可選的 user 和 password 參數： - sourceText: Cloud SQL is a fully managed relational database service that offers high performance, seamless integration, and impressive scalability. It offers MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server database engines. Extend your database application to build AI-powered experiences leveraging Cloud SQL’s LlamaIndex integrations. This notebook goes over how to use Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL to store vector embeddings with the PostgresVectorStore class. Learn more about the package on GitHub. Open In Colab Before you begin To run this notebook, you will need to do the following: - Create a Google Cloud Project - Enable the Cloud SQL Admin API. - Create a Cloud SQL instance. - Create a Cloud SQL database. - Add a User to the database. 🦙 Library Installation Install the integration library, llama-index-cloud-sql-pg, and the library for the embedding service, llama-index-embeddings-vertex. Colab only: Uncomment the following cell to restart the kernel or use the button to restart the kernel. For Vertex AI Workbench you can restart the terminal using the button on top. 🔐 Authentication Authenticate to Google Cloud as the IAM user logged into this notebook in order to access your Google Cloud Project. - If you are using Colab to run this notebook, use the cell below and continue. - If you are using Vertex AI Workbench, check out the setup instructions here. ☁ Set Your Google Cloud Project Set your Google Cloud project so that you can leverage Google Cloud resources within this notebook. If you don’t know your project ID, try the following: - Run gcloud config list. - Run gcloud projects list. - See the support page: Locate the project ID. Basic Usage Set Cloud SQL database values Find your database values, in the Cloud SQL Instances page. PostgresEngine Connection Pool One of the requirements and arguments to establish Cloud SQL as a vector store is a PostgresEngine object. The PostgresEngine configures a connection pool to your Cloud SQL database, enabling successful connections from your application and following industry best practices. To create a PostgresEngine using PostgresEngine.from instance() you need to provide only 4 things: 1. project id : Project ID of the Google Cloud Project where the Cloud SQL instance is located. 2. region : Region where the Cloud SQL instance is located. 3. instance : The name of the Cloud SQL instance. 4. database : The name of the database to connect to on the Cloud SQL instance. By default, IAM database authentication will be used as the method of database authentication. This library uses the IAM principal belonging to the Application Default Credentials (ADC) sourced from the envionment. For more informatin on IAM database authentication please see: - Configure an instance for IAM database authentication - Manage users with IAM database authentication Optionally, built-in database authentication using a username and password to access the Cloud SQL database can also be used. Just provide the optional user and password arguments to PostgresEngine.from instance(): - user : Database user to use for built-in database authentication and login - password : Database password to use for built-in database authentication and login. Note: This tutorial demonstrates the async interface. All async methods have corresponding sync methods. Initialize a table The PostgresVectorStore class requires a database table. The PostgresEngine engine has a helper method init vector store table() that can be used to create a table with the proper schema for you. Optional Tip: 💡 You can also specify a schema name by passing schema name wherever you pass table name. Create an embedding class instance You can use any Llama Index embeddings model. You may need to enable Vertex AI API to use VertexTextEmbeddings. We recommend setting the embedding model’s version for production, learn more about the Text embeddings models. Initialize a default PostgresVectorStore Download data Load documents Use with VectorStoreIndex Create an index from the vector store by using VectorStoreIndex. Initialize Vector Store with documents The simplest way to use a Vector Store is to load a set of documents and build an index from them using from documents. Query the index Create a custom Vector Store A Vector Store can take advantage of relational data to filter similarity searches. Create a new table with custom metadata columns. You can also re-use an existing table which already has custom columns for a Document’s id, content, embedding, and/or metadata. Add documents with metadata Document metadata can provide the LLM and retrieval process with more information. Learn more about different approaches for extracting and adding metadata. Search for documents with metadata filter You can apply pre-filtering to the search results by specifying a filters argument Add a Index Speed up vector search queries by applying a vector index. Learn more about vector indexes. Re-index Remove an index

title: Couchbase Vector Store
text: Couchbase 是一款屢獲殊榮的分散式 NoSQL cloud 資料庫，為您的所有 cloud、mobile、AI 和 edge computing 應用程式提供無與倫比的多功能性、效能、可擴展性及財務價值。Couchbase 透過為開發人員提供程式碼輔助 AI，並為應用程式提供 vector search。 Vector Search 是 Couchbase 中的 全文 搜尋服務（Search Service）的一部分。 本教學說明如何在 Couchbase 中使用 Vector Search。您可以同時使用 Couchbase Capella 和您自管理的 Couchbase Server。 安裝 如果您在 colab 上開啟此 Notebook，您可能需要安裝 LlamaIndex 🦙。 建立 Couchbase 連線 我們首先建立與 Couchbase cluster 的連線，然後將 cluster 物件傳遞給 Vector Store。 在這裡，我們使用使用者名稱和密碼進行連線。您也可以使用任何其他支援的方式連線到您的 cluster。 有關連線到 Couchbase cluster 的更多資訊，請查閱 Python SDK 文件。 建立搜尋索引 目前，Search index 需要從 Couchbase Capella 或 Server UI 或使用 REST interface 建立。 讓我們在 testing bucket 上定義一個名為 vector-index 的 Search index。 對於此範例，我們在 UI 的 Search Service 上使用 Import Index 功能。 我們在測試 bucket 的 default scope 上，對 default collection 建立一個 index，將 vector field 設定為 embedding，維度為 1536，將 text field 設定為 text。我們還將所有欄位在 document 下的 metadata 中建立為 dynamic mapping，以應對不同的 document 結構。相似度指標設定為 dot product。 如何將索引匯入 Full Text Search service？ - Couchbase Server - 點擊 Search - Add Index - Import - 在 Import 畫面中複製以下 Index 定義 - 點擊 Create Index 建立索引。 - Couchbase Capella - 將索引定義複製到新的檔案 index.json - 按照文件中的說明在 Capella 中匯入該檔案。 - 點擊 Create Index 建立索引。 索引定義 現在我們在 Couchbase cluster 中設定我們想要用於 Vector Search 的 bucket、scope 和 collection 名稱。 對於此範例，我們使用預設的 scope 和 collections。 對於本教學，我們將使用 OpenAI embeddings 下載資料 載入 documents 基本範例 我們向查詢引擎詢問關於我們剛才建立索引的文章的問題。 Metadata 篩選器 我們將建立一些帶有 metadata 的範例 documents，以便我們可以看到如何根據 metadata 篩選 documents。 自訂篩選器與覆蓋查詢 Couchbase 目前僅透過 LlamaIndex 支援 ExactMatchFilters。Couchbase 支援多種篩選器，包括 range filters、geospatial filters 等。要使用這些篩選器，您可以將它們作為一個字典列表傳遞給 cb search options parameter。關於 search\ options 的不同搜尋/查詢可能性，請參閱 這裡。
sourceText: Couchbase is an award-winning distributed NoSQL cloud database that delivers unmatched versatility, performance, scalability, and financial value for all of your cloud, mobile, AI, and edge computing applications. Couchbase embraces AI with coding assistance for developers and vector search for their applications. Vector Search is a part of the Full Text Search Service (Search Service) in Couchbase. This tutorial explains how to use Vector Search in Couchbase. You can work with both Couchbase Capella and your self-managed Couchbase Server. Installation If you’re opening this Notebook on colab, you will probably need to install LlamaIndex 🦙. Creating Couchbase Connection We create a connection to the Couchbase cluster initially and then pass the cluster object to the Vector Store. Here, we are connecting using the username and password. You can also connect using any other supported way to your cluster. For more information on connecting to the Couchbase cluster, please check the Python SDK documentation. Creating the Search Index Currently, the Search index needs to be created from the Couchbase Capella or Server UI or using the REST interface. Let us define a Search index with the name vector-index on the testing bucket For this example, let us use the Import Index feature on the Search Service on the UI. We are defining an index on the testing bucket’s default scope on the default collection with the vector field set to embedding with 1536 dimensions and the text field set to text. We are also indexing and storing all the fields under metadata in the document as a dynamic mapping to account for varying document structures. The similarity metric is set to dot product. How to Import an Index to the Full Text Search service? - Couchbase Server - Click on Search - Add Index - Import - Copy the following Index definition in the Import screen - Click on Create Index to create the index. - Couchbase Capella - Copy the index definition to a new file index.json - Import the file in Capella using the instructions in the documentation. - Click on Create Index to create the index. Index Definition We will now set the bucket, scope, and collection names in the Couchbase cluster that we want to use for Vector Search. For this example, we are using the default scope & collections. For this tutorial, we will use OpenAI embeddings Download Data Load the documents Basic Example We will ask the query engine a question about the essay we just indexed. Metadata Filters We will create some example documents with metadata so that we can see how to filter documents based on metadata. Custom Filters and overriding Query Couchbase supports ExactMatchFilters only at the moment via LlamaIndex. Couchbase supports a wide range of filters, including range filters, geospatial filters, and more. To use these filters, you can pass them in as a list of dictionaries to the cb search options parameter. The different search/query possibilities for the search\ options can be found here.

sourceText: In this notebook we are going to show a quick demo of using the Dragonfly with Vector Store. If you’re opening this Notebook on colab, you will probably need to install LlamaIndex 🦙. Start Dragonfly The easiest way to start Dragonfly is using the Dragonfly docker image or quickly signing up for a Dragonfly Cloud demo instance. To follow every step of this tutorial, launch the image as follows: Terminal window Setup OpenAI Lets first begin by adding the openai api key. This will allow us to access openai for embeddings and to use chatgpt. Download Data Read in a dataset Here we will use a set of Paul Graham essays to provide the text to turn into embeddings, store in a vector store and query to find context for our LLM QnA loop. Initialize the default vector store Now we have our documents prepared, we can initialize the vector store with default settings. This will allow us to store our vectors in Dragonfly and create an index for real-time search. Query the default vector store Now that we have our data stored in the index, we can ask questions against the index. The index will use the data as the knowledge base for an LLM. The default setting for as\ query\ engine() utilizes OpenAI embeddings and GPT as the language model. Therefore, an OpenAI key is required unless you opt for a customized or local language model. Below we will test searches against out index and then full RAG with an LLM. Use a custom index schema In most use cases, you need the ability to customize the underling index configuration and specification. For example, this is handy in order to define specific metadata filters you wish to enable. With Dragonfly, this is as simple as defining an index schema object (from file or dict) and passing it through to the vector store client wrapper. For this example, we will: 1. switch the embedding model to Cohere 2. add an additional metadata field for the document updated at timestamp 3. index the existing file name metadata field Query the vector store and filter on metadata Now that we have additional metadata indexed in Dragonfly, let’s try some queries with filters. Deleting documents or index completely Sometimes it may be useful to delete documents or the entire index. This can be done using the delete and delete index methods. However, the index still exists (with no associated documents).

sourceText: Elasticsearch is a distributed, RESTful search and analytics engine built on top of Apache Lucene. It offers different retrieval options including dense vector retrieval, sparse vector retrieval, keyword search and hybrid search. Sign up for a free trial of Elastic Cloud or run a local server like described below. Requires Elasticsearch 8.9.0 or higher and AIOHTTP. Running and connecting to Elasticsearch Two ways to setup an Elasticsearch instance for use with: Elastic Cloud Elastic Cloud is a managed Elasticsearch service. Sign up for a free trial. Locally Get started with Elasticsearch by running it locally. The easiest way is to use the official Elasticsearch Docker image. See the Elasticsearch Docker documentation for more information. Terminal window Configuring ElasticsearchStore The ElasticsearchStore class is used to connect to an Elasticsearch instance. It requires the following parameters: Example: Connecting locally Example: Connecting to Elastic Cloud with username and password Example: Connecting to Elastic Cloud with API Key Example data Retrieval Examples This section shows the different retrieval options available through the ElasticsearchStore and make use of them via a VectorStoreIndex. We first define a helper function to retrieve and print results for user query input: Dense retrieval Here we use embeddings from OpenAI to search. This is also the default retrieval strategy: Sparse retrieval For this example you first need to deploy the ELSER model version two in your Elasticsearch deployment. Keyword retrieval To use classic full-text search, you can use the BM25 strategy. Hybrid retrieval Combining dense retrieval and keyword search for hybrid retrieval can be enabled by setting a flag. Metadata Filters We can also apply filters to the query engine based on the metadata of our documents. Custom Filters and overriding Query The elastic search implementation only supports ExactMatchFilters provided from LlamaIndex at the moment. Elasticsearch itself supports a wide range of filters, including range filters, geo filters, and more. To use these filters, you can pass them in as a list of dictionaries to the es filter parameter.

text: 本指南將介紹如何在 LlamaIndex 中執行 auto-retrieval 。 許多流行的 vector dbs 除了查詢字串外，還支援一組 metadata 篩選器用於語義搜尋。對於自然語言查詢，我們首先使用 LLM 來推斷一組 metadata 篩選器以及應傳遞給 vector db 的正確查詢字串（此查詢字串也可以是空白的）。然後，這個總體查詢組合會對 vector db 執行。 這使得我們能夠實現超越 top-k semantic search 的更動態、更具表達力的檢索方式。給定一個查詢的相關上下文可能只需要對一個 metadata tag 進行篩選，或者需要在篩選後的集合內進行篩選與 semantic search 的組合，或者僅僅是原始的 semantic search。 我們以 Elasticsearch 為例進行演示，但 auto-retrieval 也已實作於許多其他 vector dbs（例如 Pinecone、Weaviate 等）。 設定 我們首先定義導入。 如果您在 colab 上開啟此 Notebook，您可能需要安裝 LlamaIndex 🦙。 定義一些範例資料 我們將一些包含文字區塊的範例 nodes 插入到 vector database 中。請注意，每個 TextNode 不僅包含文字，還包含 metadata，例如 category 和 country。這些 metadata 欄位將在底層 vector db 中被轉換/儲存為此形式。 使用 Elasticsearch Vector Store 建構 Vector Index 在這裡，我們將資料載入到 vector store 中。如上所述，每個 node 的文字和 metadata 都會被轉換成 Elasticsearch 中的對應表示。現在我們可以在 Elasticsearch 中對此資料執行 semantic 查詢和 metadata 篩選。 定義 VectorIndexAutoRetriever 我們定義核心的 VectorIndexAutoRetriever 模組。該模組接收 VectorStoreInfo，其中包含 vector store collection 的結構化描述及其支援的 metadata 篩選器。此資訊將用於 auto-retrieval prompt 中，其中 LLM 推斷 metadata 篩選器。 對一些範例資料進行運行 我們嘗試對一些範例資料進行運行。請注意 metadata 篩選器是如何被推斷的——這有助於更精確的檢索！
sourceText: This guide shows how to perform auto-retrieval in LlamaIndex. Many popular vector dbs support a set of metadata filters in addition to a query string for semantic search. Given a natural language query, we first use the LLM to infer a set of metadata filters as well as the right query string to pass to the vector db (either can also be blank). This overall query bundle is then executed against the vector db. This allows for more dynamic, expressive forms of retrieval beyond top-k semantic search. The relevant context for a given query may only require filtering on a metadata tag, or require a joint combination of filtering + semantic search within the filtered set, or just raw semantic search. We demonstrate an example with Elasticsearch, but auto-retrieval is also implemented with many other vector dbs (e.g. Pinecone, Weaviate, and more). Setup We first define imports. If you’re opening this Notebook on colab, you will probably need to install LlamaIndex 🦙. Defining Some Sample Data We insert some sample nodes containing text chunks into the vector database. Note that each TextNode not only contains the text, but also metadata e.g. category and country. These metadata fields will get converted/stored as such in the underlying vector db. Build Vector Index with Elasticsearch Vector Store Here we load the data into the vector store. As mentioned above, both the text and metadata for each node will get converted into corresponding representation in Elasticsearch. We can now run semantic queries and also metadata filtering on this data from Elasticsearch. Define VectorIndexAutoRetriever We define our core VectorIndexAutoRetriever module. The module takes in VectorStoreInfo, which contains a structured description of the vector store collection and the metadata filters it supports. This information will then be used in the auto-retrieval prompt where the LLM infers metadata filters. Running over some sample data We try running over some sample data. Note how metadata filters are inferred - this helps with more precise retrieval!

text: 在本筆筆記中，我們將展示如何使用 Epsilla 在 LlamaIndex 中執行向量搜尋。 作為先決條件，您需要有一個正在運行的 Epsilla 向量資料庫（例如，透過我們的 docker 映像檔），並安裝 pyepsilla 套件。請參閱完整的文件 文件。 如果您在 colab 上開啟此 Notebook，您可能需要安裝 LlamaIndex 🦙。 設定 OpenAI 我們先從新增 openai api key 開始。它將用於為載入到索引中的 documents 建立 embeddings。 下載資料 載入 documents 使用 SimpleDirectoryReader 載入儲存在 /data/paul graham 資料夾中的 documents。 建立索引 在這裡，我們使用先前載入的 documents 建立一個由 Epsilla 支援的索引。EpsillaVectorStore 接受幾個參數。 - client (Any): 用於連接的 Epsilla client。 - collection\ name (str, optional): 要使用的 collection。預設為 “llama\ collection”。 - db\ path (str, optional): 資料庫將被持久化的路徑。預設為 “/tmp/langchain-epsilla”。 - db\ name (str, optional): 為載入的資料庫命名。預設為 “langchain\ store”。 - dimension (int, optional): embeddings 的維度。如果未提供，集合建立將在首次插入時完成。預設為 None。 - overwrite (bool, optional): 是否用相同名稱的現有集合覆蓋。預設為 False。 Epsilla vectordb 使用預設主機 “localhost” 和連接埠 “8888” 運行。 查詢資料 現在我們在索引中有了我們的 document，我們可以對索引提出問題。 接下來，讓我們嘗試覆蓋先前的資料。 接下來，讓我們向現有集合新增更多資料。
sourceText: In this notebook we are going to show how to use Epsilla to perform vector searches in LlamaIndex. As a prerequisite, you need to have a running Epsilla vector database (for example, through our docker image), and install the pyepsilla package. View full docs at docs If you’re opening this Notebook on colab, you will probably need to install LlamaIndex 🦙. Setup OpenAI Lets first begin by adding the openai api key. It will be used to created embeddings for the documents loaded into the index. Download Data Loading documents Load documents stored in the /data/paul graham folder using the SimpleDirectoryReader. Create the index Here we create an index backed by Epsilla using the documents loaded previously. EpsillaVectorStore takes a few arguments. - client (Any): Epsilla client to connect to. - collection\ name (str, optional): Which collection to use. Defaults to “llama\ collection”. - db\ path (str, optional): The path where the database will be persisted. Defaults to “/tmp/langchain-epsilla”. - db\ name (str, optional): Give a name to the loaded database. Defaults to “langchain\ store”. - dimension (int, optional): The dimension of the embeddings. If not provided, collection creation will be done on first insert. Defaults to None. - overwrite (bool, optional): Whether to overwrite existing collection with same name. Defaults to False. title: Jaguar Vector Store
text: 此 document 示範 llama\ index 如何與 Jaguar vector store 協作。 - 它是一個可以儲存大量向量的分布式 vector database。 - ZeroMove 功能可實現即時水平擴展。 - 它支援 embeddings、text、images、videos、PDFs、audio、time series 和 spatial data。 - all-master 架構允許並行讀取和寫入。 - 它的 anomaly detection 能力可以區分資料集中的異常值。 - RAG 支援可以結合 LLMs 和 proprietary 及 real-time data。 - 在多個 vector index 之間共享 metadata 提升了資料一致性。 - 距離度量包括 Euclidean、Cosine、InnerProduct、Manhatten、Chebyshev、Hamming、Jeccard 和 Minkowski。 - 相似度搜尋可以帶有時間截止（time cutoff）和時間衰減（time decay）效果。 先決條件 執行此檔案中的範例需要兩個要求。 您必須安裝並設定 JaguarDB server 及其 HTTP gateway server。請參考 Jaguar Setup 中的說明。 您必須安裝 packages llama-index 和 jaguardb-http-client。 方法一：Docker 方法二：快速設定 (Linux) 匯入 應匯入以下 packages。我們以 OpenAIEmbedding 作為範例。您可以選擇應用程式中的其他 embedding models。 Client Object 我們現在建立一個 jaguar vector store client object。url 是 gateway server 的 http endpoint。url 應替換為您的環境 settings。pod 是 Pod（或 database）的名稱。store 是 vector store 的名稱。一個 pod 可能有多個 store。vector\ index 是 store 中 vector index 的名稱。一個 store 可能有多個 vector indexes。然而，store client object 只綁定到一個 vector index。vector\ type 指定 vector index 的屬性。在字串 “cosine\ fraction\ short” 中，cosine 表示兩個向量之間的距離是使用 cosine distance 計算的。Fraction 表示向量的組成部分是分數數。Short 表示向量組成部分的儲存格式是有符號 16 位元整數的 short integer。儲存格式可以是 32 位元浮點數的 float。它也可以是 8 位元有符號整數的 byte。vector\ dimension 是由提供的 embedding model 生成的向量的維度。 Authentication 為了系統安全和使用者驗證，client 必須登入或連接到 back-end jaguar server。環境變數 JAGUAR\ API\ KEY 或檔案 $HOME/.jagrc 必須包含由您的系統管理員發行的 jaguar api。login() 方法回傳 True 或 False。如果回傳 False，則可能表示您的 jaguar api key 無效，或 http gateway server 未運行，或 jaguar server 沒有正常運行。 Create Vector Store 我們現在建立一個 vector store，具有一個大小為 1024 bytes 的 ‘v:text’ 欄位來儲存文字，以及兩個額外的 metadata 欄位 ‘author’ 和 ‘category’。 Load Documents 以下程式碼開啟範例 Paul Gram documents 並將其讀入記憶體中。 建立索引 準備 storage context、service context 並建立一個 index object。呼叫 from\ documents() 後，vector store 中將儲存 22 個 vectors。 Ask Questions 我們取得一個 query engine 並向引擎提出一些問題。 Pass Query Options 我們可以向 query engine 傳遞額外的參數，以從 jaguar vector store 中選取數據的子集。這可以透過使用 vector store kwargs 參數來實現。參數 day\ cutoff 是文本將被忽略的天數。day\ decay\ rate 是相似度分數的每日衰減率。 Cleanup and Logout所有向量和向量資料在 vector store 中都可以被刪除，並且可以完全移除 vector store 以完成測試。登出呼叫會確保客戶端使用的資源被釋放。
sourceText: This document demonstrates llama\ index working with Jaguar vector store. - It is a distributed vector database that can store large number of vectors. - The ZeroMove feature enables instant horizontal scaling. - It supports embeddings, text, images, videos, PDFs, audio, time series, and spatial data. - The all-master architecture allows both parallel reads and writes. - Its anomaly detection capabilities can distinguish outliers in the dataset. - The RAG support can combine LLMs and proprietary and real-time data. - Sharing of metadata across multiple vector indexes improves data consistency. - Distance metrics include Euclidean, Cosine, InnerProduct, Manhatten, Chebyshev, Hamming, Jeccard, and Minkowski. - Similarity search can be performed with time cutoff and time decay effects. Prerequisites There are two requirements for running the examples in this file. You must install and set up the JaguarDB server and its HTTP gateway server. Please follow the instructions in Jaguar Setup as a reference. You must install packages llama-index and jaguardb-http-client. Method One : Docker Method Two: Quick Setup(Linux) Imports The following packages should be imported. We use the OpenAIEmbedding as an example. You could choose other embedding models in your application. Client Object We now instantiate a jaguar vector store client object. The url is the http endpoint of the gateway server. The url should be replaced with your environment settings. The pod is the Pod (or database) name. The store is the name of the vector store. A pod may have multiple stores. The vector\ index is the name of the vector index in the store. A store may have multiple vector indexes. The store client object is, however, bound to one vector index only. The vector\ type specifies the attributes of the vector index. In the string “cosine\ fraction\ short”, cosine means that the distance between two vectors is computed with the cosine distance. Fraction means the vector components are fractional numbers. Short means the storage format of the vector components is a short integer of signed 16-bits integers. Storage format could be float of 32-bit floating point numbers. It can also be a byte of 8-bit signed integers. The vector\ dimension is the dimension of the vector generated by the provided embedding model. Authentication The client must login or connect to back-end jaguar server for system security and user authentication. Environment variable JAGUAR\ API\ KEY or file $HOME/.jagrc file must contain the jaguar api ke issued by your system administrator. The login() method returns True or False. If it returns False, then it may mean that your jaguar api key is invalid, or the http gateway server is not running, or the jaguar server is not running properly. Create Vector Store We now create a vector store with a field ‘v:text’ of size 1024 bytes to hold text, and two additional metadata fields ‘author’ and ‘category’. Load Documents The following code opens the example Paul Gram documents and read them into memory Make Index Prepare storage context, service context, and make an index object. After the call of from\ documents(), there will be 22 vectors saved in the vector store. Ask Questions We get a query engine and ask some questions to the engine. Pass Query Options We can pass extra arguments to the query engine to select only a subset of data from the jaguar vector store. This can be achieved by using the vector store kwargs argument. Parameter day\ cutoff is number of days beyond which text will be ignored. day\ decay\ rate is rate of daily decay for similarity scores. Cleanup and Logout All vectors and related data in the vector store can be deleted and the vector store can be removed completely to finish the test. Logout call makes sure resources used by the client are released.

sourceText: Note: This example requires a KDB.AI endpoint and API key. Sign up for a free KDB.AI account. KDB.AI is a powerful knowledge-based vector database and search engine that allows you to build scalable, reliable AI applications, using real-time data, by providing advanced search, recommendation and personalization. This example demonstrates how to use KDB.AI to run semantic search, summarization and analysis of financial regulations around some specific moment in time. To access your end point and API keys, sign up to KDB.AI here. To set up your development environment, follow the instructions on the KDB.AI pre-requisites page. The following examples demonstrate some of the ways you can interact with KDB.AI through LlamaIndex. Install dependencies with Pip In order to successfully run this sample, note the following steps depending on where you are running this notebook: - Run Locally / Private Environment: The Setup steps in the repository’s README.md will guide you on prerequisites and how to run this with Jupyter. - Colab / Hosted Environment: Open this notebook in Colab and run through the cells. Import dependencies Set OpenAI API key and choose the LLM and Embedding model to use: Create KDB.AI session and table Option 1. KDB.AI Cloud To use KDB.AI Cloud, you will need two session details - a URL endpoint and an API key. To get these you can sign up for free here. You can connect to a KDB.AI Cloud session using kdbai.Session and passing the session URL endpoint and API key details from your KDB.AI Cloud portal. If the environment variables KDBAI ENDPOINTS and KDBAI API KEY exist on your system containing your KDB.AI Cloud portal details, these variables will automatically be used to connect. If these do not exist, it will prompt you to enter your KDB.AI Cloud portal session URL endpoint and API key details. Option 2. KDB.AI Server To use KDB.AI Server, you will need download and run your own container. To do this, you will first need to sign up for free here. You will receive an email with the required license file and bearer token needed to download your instance. Follow instructions in the signup email to get your session up and running. Once the setup steps are complete you can then connect to your KDB.AI Server session using kdbai.Session and passing your local endpoint. Create the schema for your KDB.AI table !!! Note: The ‘dims’ parameter in the embedding column must reflect the output dimensions of the embedding model you choose. - OpenAI ‘text-embedding-3-small’ outputs 1536 dimensions. title: LanceDB 向量資料庫
text: 在本筆筆記中，我們將展示如何使用 LanceDB 在 LlamaIndex 中執行向量搜尋。 如果您在 Colab 上開啟此 Notebook，您可能需要安裝 LlamaIndex 🦙。 設定 OpenAI 第一步是設定 openai key。它將用於為載入到索引中的 documents 建立 embeddings。 下載資料 載入 documents 使用 SimpleDirectoryReader 載入儲存在 data/paul graham/ 中的 documents。 建立索引 在這裡，我們使用先前載入的 documents 建立一個由 LanceDB 支援的索引。LanceDBVectorStore 接受幾個參數。 - uri (str, required)：LanceDB 將儲存檔案的位置。 - table\ name (str, optional)：嵌入將儲存在哪個表格中。預設為 “vectors”。 - nprobes (int, optional)：使用的探測次數。較高的數字會使搜尋更準確，但也更慢。預設為 20。 - refine\ factor: (int, optional)：透過讀取額外元素並在記憶體中重新排序來精煉結果。預設為 None 更多詳細資訊請參閱 LanceDB docs。 對於 LanceDB cloud： python vector store = LanceDBVectorStore( uri="./lancedb", mode="overwrite", query type="hybrid" ) storage context = StorageContext.from defaults(vector store=vector store) index = VectorStoreIndex.from documents( documents, storage context=storage context ) from llama index.core.vector stores import ( MetadataFilters, FilterOperator, FilterCondition, MetadataFilter, ) from datetime import datetime query filters = MetadataFilters( filters=[ MetadataFilter( key="creation date", operator=FilterOperator.EQ, value=datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), ), MetadataFilter( key="file size", value=75040, operator=FilterOperator.GT ), ], condition=FilterCondition.AND, ) ! pip install -U torch transformers tantivy@git+https://github.com/quickwit-oss/tantivy-py 164adc87e1a033117001cf70e38c82a53014d985 from lancedb.rerankers import ColbertReranker reranker = ColbertReranker() vector store = LanceDBVectorStore(uri="./lancedb", reranker=reranker, mode="overwrite") import lancedb from lancedb.rerankers import ColbertReranker reranker = ColbertReranker() vector store. add reranker(reranker) query engine = index.as query engine( filters=query filters, vector store kwargs={ "query type": "fts", }, ) response = query engine.query("How much did Viaweb charge per month?") print(response) print("metadata -", response.metadata) Viaweb charged $100 a month for a small store and $300 a month for a big one. metadata - {'65ed5f07-5b8a-4143-a939-e8764884828e': {'file path': '/Users/raghavdixit/Desktop/open source/llama index lance/docs/examples/vector stores/data/paul graham/paul graham essay.txt', 'file name': 'paul graham essay.txt', 'file type': 'text/plain', 'file size': 75042, 'creation date': '2024-06-11', 'last modified date': '2024-06-11'}, 'be231827-20b8-4988-ac75-94fa79b3c22e': {'file path': '/Users/raghavdixit/Desktop/open source/llama index lance/docs/examples/vector stores/data/paul graham/paul graham essay.txt', 'file name': 'paul graham essay.txt', 'file type': 'text/plain', 'file size': 75042, 'creation date': '2024-06-11', 'last modified date': '2024-06-11'}} lance filter = "metadata.file name = 'paul graham essay.txt' " retriever = index.as retriever(vector store kwargs={"where": lance filter}) response = retriever.retrieve("What did the author do growing up?") print(response[0].get content()) print("metadata -", response[0].metadata) What I Worked On February 2021 Before college the two main things I worked on, outside of school, were writing and programming. I didn't write essays. I wrote what beginning writers were supposed to write then, and probably still are: short stories. My stories were awful. They had hardly any plot, just characters with strong feelings, which I imagined made them deep. The first programs I tried writing were on the IBM 1401 that our school district used for what was then called "data processing." This was in 9th grade, so I was 13 or 14. The school district's 1401 happened to be in the basement of our junior high school, and my friend Rich Draves and I got permission to use it. It was like a mini Bond villain's lair down there, with all these alien-looking machines — CPU, disk drives, printer, card reader — sitting up on a raised floor under bright fluorescent lights. The language we used was an early version of Fortran. You had to type programs on punch cards, then stack them in the card reader and press a button to load the program into memory and run it. The result would ordinarily be to print something on the spectacularly loud printer. I was puzzled by the 1401. I couldn't figure out what to do with it. And in retrospect there's not much I could have done with it. The only form of input to programs was data stored on punched cards, and I didn't have any data stored on punched cards. The only other option was to do things that didn't rely on any input, like calculate approximations of pi, but I didn't know enough math to do anything interesting of that type. So I'm not surprised I can't remember any programs I wrote, because they can't have done much. My clearest memory is of the moment I learned it was possible for programs not to terminate, when one of mine didn't. On a machine without time-sharing, this was a social as well as a technical error, as the data center manager's expression made clear. With microcomputers, everything changed. Now you could have a computer sitting right in front of you, on a desk, that could respond to your keystrokes as it was running instead of just churning through a stack of punch cards and then stopping. [1] The first of my friends to get a microcomputer built it himself. It was sold as a kit by Heathkit. I remember vividly how impressed and envious I felt watching him sitting in front of it, typing programs right into the computer. Computers were expensive in those days and it took me years of nagging before I convinced my father to buy one, a TRS-80, in about 1980. The gold standard then was the Apple II, but a TRS-80 was good enough. This was when I really started programming. I wrote simple games, a program to predict how high my model rockets would fly, and a word processor that my father used to write at least one book. There was only room in memory for about 2 pages of text, so he'd write 2 pages at a time and then print them out, but it was a lot better than a typewriter. Though I liked programming, I didn't plan to study it in college. In college I was going to study philosophy, which sounded much more powerful. It seemed, to my naive high school self, to be the study of the ultimate truths, compared to which the things studied in other fields would be mere domain knowledge. What I discovered when I got to college was that the other fields took up so much of the space of ideas that there wasn't much left for these supposed ultimate truths. All that seemed left for philosophy were edge cases that people in other fields felt could safely be ignored. I couldn't have put this into words when I was 18. All I knew at the time was that I kept taking philosophy courses and they kept being boring. So I decided to switch to AI. AI was in the air in the mid 1980s, but there were two things especially that made me want to work on it: a novel by Heinlein called The Moon is a Harsh Mistress, which featured an intelligent computer called Mike, and a PBS documentary that showed Terry Winograd using SHRDLU. I haven't tried rereading The Moon is a Harsh Mistress, so I don't know how well it has aged, but when I read it I was drawn entirely into its world. metadata - {'file path': '/Users/raghavdixit/Desktop/open source/llama index lance/docs/examples/vector stores/data/paul graham/paul graham essay.txt', 'file name': 'paul graham essay.txt', 'file type': 'text/plain', 'file size': 75042, 'creation date': '2024-06-11', 'last modified date': '2024-06-11'} nodes = [node.node for node in response] del index index = VectorStoreIndex.from documents( [Document(text="The sky is purple in Portland, Maine")], uri="/tmp/new dataset", ) index.insert nodes(nodes) query engine = index.as query engine() response = query engine.query("Where is the sky purple?") print(textwrap.fill(str(response), 100)) Portland, Maine del index vec store = LanceDBVectorStore.from table(vector store. table) index = VectorStoreIndex.from vector store(vec store) query engine = index.as query engine() response = query engine.query("What companies did the author start?") print(textwrap.fill(str(response), 100)) The author started Viaweb and Aspra. `

On a machine without time-sharing, this was a social as well as a technical error, as the data center manager's expression made clear. With microcomputers, everything changed. Now you could have a computer sitting right in front of you, on a desk, that could respond to your keystrokes as it was running instead of just churning through a stack of punch cards and then stopping. [1] The first of my friends to get a microcomputer built it himself. It was sold as a kit by Heathkit. I remember vividly how impressed and envious I felt watching him sitting in front of it, typing programs right into the computer. Computers were expensive in those days and it took me years of nagging before I convinced my father to buy one, a TRS-80, in about 1980. The gold standard then was the Apple II, but a TRS-80 was good enough. This was when I really started programming. I wrote simple games, a program to predict how high my model rockets would fly, and a word processor that my father used to write at least one book. There was only room in memory for about 2 pages of text, so he'd write 2 pages at a time and then print them out, but it was a lot better than a typewriter. Though I liked programming, I didn't plan to study it in college. In college I was going to study philosophy, which sounded much more powerful. It seemed, to my naive high school self, to be the study of the ultimate truths, compared to which the things studied in other fields would be mere domain knowledge. What I discovered when I got to college was that the other fields took up so much of the space of ideas that there wasn't much left for these supposed ultimate truths. All that seemed left for philosophy were edge cases that people in other fields felt could safely be ignored. I couldn't have put this into words when I was 18. All I knew at the time was that I kept taking philosophy courses and they kept being boring. So I decided to switch to AI. AI was in the air in the mid 1980s, but there were two things especially that made me want to work on it: a novel by Heinlein called The Moon is a Harsh Mistress, which featured an intelligent computer called Mike, and a PBS documentary that showed Terry Winograd using SHRDLU. text: 本指南說明如何在 LlamaIndex 中執行 auto-retrieval 。 許多流行的 vector DBs 除了查詢字串外，還支援一組 metadata 篩選器用於語義搜尋。對於自然語言查詢，我們首先使用 LLM 來推斷一組 metadata 篩選器以及應傳遞給 vector DB 的正確查詢字串（此查詢字串也可以是空白的）。然後，這個總體查詢組合會對 vector DB 執行。 這使得我們能夠進行超越 top-k semantic search 的更動態、更具表達力的檢索方式。給定查詢的相關上下文可能只需要對 metadata tag 進行篩選，或者需要在篩選後的集合內進行篩選 + semantic search 的組合，或者僅僅是原始的 semantic search。 我們以 Lantern 為例進行演示，但 auto-retrieval 也已實作於許多其他 vector DB 中（例如 Pinecone、Chroma、Weaviate 等）。 如果您在 colab 上開啟此 Notebook，您可能需要安裝 LlamaIndex 🦙。 建置 搭配以下內容的向量索引： Lantern Vector Store 在這裡，我們將資料載入到 vector store 中。如上所述，每個 node 的文字和 metadata 都會轉換成 Lantern 中的對應表示。現在我們可以在 Lantern 的資料上執行 semantic 查詢和 metadata 篩選。 Define VectorIndexAutoRetriever 我們定義核心的 VectorIndexAutoRetriever 模組。該模組接收 VectorStoreInfo，其中包含 vector store collection 的結構化描述及其支援的 metadata 篩選器。此資訊將用於 auto-retrieval prompt 中，其中 LLM 推斷 metadata 篩選器。 Running 處理一些範例資料 我們嘗試對一些範例資料進行運行。注意 metadata 篩選器是如何被推斷的——這有助於更精確的檢索！
sourceText: This guide shows how to perform auto-retrieval in LlamaIndex. Many popular vector DBs support a set of metadata filters in addition to a query string for semantic search. Given a natural language query, we first use the LLM to infer a set of metadata filters as well as the right query string to pass to the vector DB (either can also be blank). This overall query bundle is then executed against the vector DB. This allows for more dynamic, expressive forms of retrieval beyond top-k semantic search. The relevant context for a given query may only require filtering on a metadata tag, or require a joint combination of filtering + semantic search within the filtered set, or just raw semantic search. We demonstrate an example with Lantern, but auto-retrieval is also implemented with many other vector DBs (e.g. Pinecone, Chroma, Weaviate, and more). If you’re opening this Notebook on colab, you will probably need to install LlamaIndex 🦙. Build Vector Index with Lantern Vector Store Here we load the data into the vector store. As mentioned above, both the text and metadata for each node will get converted into corresponding representations in Lantern. We can now run semantic queries and also metadata filtering on this data from Lantern. Define VectorIndexAutoRetriever We define our core VectorIndexAutoRetriever module. The module takes in VectorStoreInfo, which contains a structured description of the vector store collection and the metadata filters it supports. This information will then be used in the auto-retrieval prompt where the LLM infers metadata filters. Running over some sample data We try running over some sample data. Note how metadata filters are inferred - this helps with more precise retrieval!

sourceText: In this notebook we are going to show how to use Postgresql and Lantern to perform vector searches in LlamaIndex If you’re opening this Notebook on colab, you will probably need to install LlamaIndex 🦙. Setup OpenAI The first step is to configure the openai key. It will be used to created embeddings for the documents loaded into the index Download Data Loading documents Load the documents stored in the data/paul graham/ using the SimpleDirectoryReader Create the Database Using an existing postgres running at localhost, create the database we’ll be using. Create the index Here we create an index backed by Postgres using the documents loaded previously. LanternVectorStore takes a few arguments. Query the index We can now ask questions using our index. Querying existing index Hybrid Search To enable hybrid search, you need to: 1. pass in hybrid search=True when constructing the LanternVectorStore (and optionally configure text search config with the desired language) 2. pass in vector store query mode="hybrid" when constructing the query engine (this config is passed to the retriever under the hood). You can also optionally set the sparse top k to configure how many results we should obtain from sparse text search (default is using the same value as similarity top k).

text: 本教學示範如何搭配 LlamaIndex 與 Milvus 建立用於 RAG 的非同步文件處理流程。LlamaIndex 可協助處理文件，並將文件儲存在 Milvus 等向量資料庫中。透過 LlamaIndex 與 Milvus Python 用戶端程式庫的非同步 API，我們可以提高流程的吞吐量，有效率地處理並建立大量資料的索引。 本教學會先從高層次介紹如何使用 LlamaIndex 和 Milvus 的非同步方法建構 RAG，接著再介紹較低階的方法，並比較同步與非同步處理的效能。 開始之前 本頁的程式碼片段需要 pymilvus 和 llamaindex 相依套件。您可以使用以下指令安裝： 如果您使用 Google Colab，為了啟用剛安裝的相依套件，可能需要 重新啟動執行階段 （點選畫面上方的「Runtime」選單，再從下拉式選單選擇「Restart session」）。 我們會使用 OpenAI 的模型。請先取得API 金鑰，並將 OPENAI API KEY 設為環境變數。 如果您使用 Jupyter Notebook，請在執行非同步程式碼前先執行這一行程式碼。 準備資料 您可以使用以下指令下載範例資料： 使用非同步處理建構 RAG 本節說明如何建構可非同步處理文件的 RAG 系統。 匯入必要的程式庫，並定義 Milvus URI 和嵌入向量的維度。 - 如果資料量很大，您可以透過 Docker 或 Kubernetes 部署效能良好的 Milvus 伺服器。此設定請使用伺服器 URI（例如 http://localhost:19530）作為 uri。 - 若要使用 Zilliz Cloud 這項全代管的 Milvus 雲端服務，請調整 uri 和 token；它們對應至 Zilliz Cloud 中的公開端點與 API 金鑰。 - 對於網路通訊等複雜系統，相較於同步處理，非同步處理能提升效能。因此，我們認為 Milvus-Lite 不適合使用非同步介面，因為它的使用情境並不適合。 定義一個初始化函式，之後可再次使用它來重建 Milvus 集合。 使用 SimpleDirectoryReader，從 paul graham essay.txt 檔案建立 LlamaIndex 文件物件。 在本機初始化 Hugging Face 嵌入模型，可避免非同步插入資料時觸及 API 速率限制；並行 API 請求可能迅速累積，耗盡公開 API 的配額。不過，如果您的速率限制較高，也可以改用遠端模型服務。 建立索引並插入文件。 我們將 use async 設為 True，以啟用非同步插入模式。 初始化 LLM。 建立查詢引擎時，也可以將 use async 參數設為 True，以啟用非同步搜尋。 探索非同步 API 本節將介紹較低階的 API 用法，並比較同步與非同步執行的效能。 非同步新增 重新初始化向量儲存庫。 接著定義一個產生 node 的函式，供索引產生大量測試 nodes。 定義一個異步函式來將 documents 添加到 vector store 中。我們在 Milvus vector store instance 中使用 async add() 函式。 取得 event loop。 異步地將 documents 添加到 vector store。 與同步添加比較 定義一個 sync add 函式。然後在相同條件下測量執行時間。 結果顯示同步添加過程比異步過程慢得多。 異步搜尋 在執行搜尋前，重新初始化 vector store 並添加一些 documents。 定義一個 async search 函式。我們在 Milvus vector store instance 中使用 aquery() 函式。 從 Milvus store 異步搜尋。 與同步搜尋比較 定義一個 sync search 函式。然後在相同條件下測量執行時間。 結果顯示同步搜尋過程比異步過程慢得多。
sourceText: This tutorial demonstrates how to use LlamaIndex with Milvus to build asynchronous document processing pipeline for RAG. LlamaIndex provides a way to process documents and store in vector db like Milvus. By leveraging the async API of LlamaIndex and Milvus Python client library, we can increase the throughput of the pipeline to efficiently process and index large volumes of data. In this tutorial, we will first introduce the use of asynchronous methods to build a RAG with LlamaIndex and Milvus from a high level, and then introduce the use of low level methods and the performance comparison of synchronous and asynchronous. Before you begin Code snippets on this page require pymilvus and llamaindex dependencies. You can install them using the following commands: If you are using Google Colab, to enable dependencies just installed, you may need to restart the runtime (click on the “Runtime” menu at the top of the screen, and select “Restart session” from the dropdown menu). We will use the models from OpenAI. You should prepare the api key OPENAI API KEY as an environment variable. If you are using Jupyter Notebook, you need to run this line of code before running the asynchronous code. Prepare data You can download sample data with the following commands: Build RAG with Asynchronous Processing This section show how to build a RAG system that can process docs in asynchronous manner. Import the necessary libraries and define Milvus URI and the dimension of the embedding. - If you have large scale of data, you can set up a performant Milvus server on docker or kubernetes. In this setup, please use the server uri, e.g.http://localhost:19530, as your uri. - If you want to use Zilliz Cloud, the fully managed cloud service for Milvus, adjust the uri and token, which correspond to the Public Endpoint and Api key in Zilliz Cloud. - In the case of complex systems (such as network communication), asynchronous processing can bring performance improvement compared to synchronization. So we think Milvus-Lite is not suitable for using asynchronous interfaces because the scenarios used are not suitable. Define an initialization function that we can use again to rebuild the Milvus collection. Use SimpleDirectoryReader to wrap a LlamaIndex document object from the file paul graham essay.txt. Instantiate a Hugging Face embedding model locally. Using a local model avoids the risk of reaching API rate limits during asynchronous data insertion, as concurrent API requests can quickly add up and use up your budget in public API. However, if you have a high rate limit, you may opt to use a remote model service instead. Create an index and insert the document. We set the use async to True to enable async insert mode. Initialize the LLM. When building the query engine, you can also set the use async parameter to True to enable asynchronous search. Explore the Async API In this section, we’ll introduce lower level API usage and compare the performance of synchronous and asynchronous runs. Async add Re-initialize the vector store. Let’s define a node producing function, which will be used to generate large number of test nodes for the index. Define a aync function to add documents to the vector store. We use the async add() function in Milvus vector store instance. Get the event loop. Asynchronously add documents to the vector store. Compare with synchronous add Define a sync add function. Then measure the running time under the same condition. The result shows that the sync adding process is much slower than the async one. Async search Re-initialize the vector store and add some documents before running the search. Define an async search function. We use the aquery() function in Milvus vector store instance. Asynchronously search from Milvus store. Compare with synchronous search Define a sync search function. Then measure the running time under the same condition. The result shows that the sync search process is much slower than the async one.

text: 全文檢索 使用精確的關鍵字匹配，通常利用像 BM25 這樣的演算法來根據相關性對 documents 進行排序。在 Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) 系統中，此方法會檢索相關文本以增強 AI 生成的回應。 同時， 語義檢索 (semantic search) 解釋上下文含義以提供更廣泛的結果。結合這兩種方法會創造一種 hybrid search ，以改善資訊檢索——尤其是在單一方法力不從心時。 使用 Milvus 2.5 的 Sparse-BM25 方法，原始文本會自動轉換為 sparse vectors。這消除了手動生成 sparse embedding 的需求，並實現了混合檢索策略，在語義理解和關鍵字相關性之間取得平衡。 在本教學中，您將學習如何使用 LlamaIndex 和 Milvus 來使用全文檢索和混合檢索建立一個 RAG 系統。我們將從單獨實作全文檢索開始，然後透過整合語義檢索來增強它，以獲得更全面的結果。 在繼續本教學之前，請確保您熟悉 全文檢索 以及 使用 Milvus 在 LlamaIndex 中的基本知識。 先決條件 安裝依賴項 在開始之前，請確保已安裝以下依賴項： 如果您使用 Google Colab，您可能需要 重新啟動執行階段 （導航到介面頂部的「Runtime」選單，從下拉選單中選擇「Restart session」）。 設定帳戶 本教學使用 OpenAI 進行文本嵌入和答案生成。您需要準備 OpenAI API key。 要使用 Milvus vector store，請指定您的 Milvus server URI（可選擇性地使用 TOKEN）。要啟動 Milvus server，您可以透過遵循 Milvus 安裝指南 來設定 Milvus server，或直接嘗試 Zilliz Cloud 進行免費試用。 目前，Full-text search 在 Milvus Standalone、Milvus Distributed 和 Zilliz Cloud 中支援，但在 Milvus Lite（計劃在未來實作）中尚未支援。如需更多資訊，請聯繫 。 下載範例資料 執行以下指令將範例 documents 下載到 “data/paul\ graham” 目錄中： 使用全文檢索的 RAG 將全文檢索整合到 RAG 系統中，可以平衡語義檢索與精確且可預測的基於關鍵字的檢索。您也可以選擇僅使用全文檢索，儘管建議將全文檢索與語義檢索結合以獲得更好的檢索結果。為了示範目的，我們將展示單獨的全文檢索和混合檢索。 要開始，使用 SimpleDirectoryReaderLoad 載入 Paul Graham 的文章 “What I Worked On”： 使用 BM25 的全文檢索 LlamaIndex 的 MilvusVectorStore 支援全文檢索，實現了高效的基於關鍵字的檢索。透過將內建函數作為 sparse embedding function，它對搜尋結果應用 BM25 評分來進行排序。 在本節中，我們將演示如何使用 BM25 實作一個使用 BM25 進行全文檢索的 RAG 系統。 上述程式碼將範例 documents 插入到 Milvus 中，並建立一個索引以啟用全文檢索的 BM25 排序。它會禁用 dense embedding 並使用 BM25BuiltInFunction 及其預設參數。 您可以指定 BM25BuiltInFunction 參數中的輸入和輸出欄位： - input field names (str)：輸入文本欄位（預設值: “text”）。它指示 BM25 演算法應用於哪個文本欄位。如果使用您自己的集合並使用不同的文本欄位名稱，請更改此設定。 - output field names (str)：儲存此 BM25 函數輸出的欄位（預設值: “sparse\ embedding”）。一旦向量資料庫設定完成，您可以使用 Milvus 搭配查詢模式 “sparse” 或 “text\ search” 執行全文檢索查詢： 自訂文本分析器 分析器在全文檢索中扮演重要角色，它將句子分解成 tokens 並執行詞彙處理，例如 stemming 和 stop-word removal。它們通常是特定於語言的。欲了解更多詳情，請參閱 Milvus Analyzer Guide。 Milvus 支援兩種分析器： Built-in Analyzers 和 Custom Analyzers 。預設情況下，BM25BuiltInFunction 使用標準的 built-in analyzer，它根據標點符號對文本進行 tokenization。 若要使用不同的分析器或自訂現有的分析器，您可以向 analyzer params 參數傳遞值： 結合 Reranker 的混合檢索 混合檢索系統結合了 semantic search 和 full-text search，在 RAG 系統中優化檢索效能。 以下範例使用 OpenAI embedding 進行 semantic search，並使用 BM25 進行 full-text search： 運作方式 此方法將 documents 儲存在一個 Milvus collection 中，包含兩個向量欄位： - embedding：由 OpenAI embedding model 生成的用於 semantic search 的密集 embedding。 - sparse embedding：使用 BM25BuiltInFunction 計算的用於全文檢索的稀疏 embedding。 此外，我們應用了使用 “RRFRanker” 及其預設參數的 reranking 策略。若要自訂 reranker，您可以依照 Milvus Reranking Guide 配置 hybrid ranker 和 hybrid ranker params。 現在，讓我們使用一個範例查詢來測試 RAG 系統： 這種混合方法透過利用 semantic 和 keyword-based retrieval，在 RAG 系統中確保更準確、更具上下文意識的回應。
sourceText: Full-text search uses exact keyword matching, often leveraging algorithms like BM25 to rank documents by relevance. In Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, this method retrieves pertinent text to enhance AI-generated responses. Meanwhile, semantic search interprets contextual meaning to provide broader results. Combining both approaches creates a hybrid search that improves information retrieval—especially in cases where a single method falls short. With Milvus 2.5’s Sparse-BM25 approach, raw text is automatically converted into sparse vectors. This eliminates the need for manual sparse embedding generation and enables a hybrid search strategy that balances semantic understanding with keyword relevance. In this tutorial, you’ll learn how to use LlamaIndex and Milvus to build a RAG system using full-text search and hybrid search. We’ll start by implementing full-text search alone and then enhance it by integrating semantic search for more comprehensive results. Before proceeding with this tutorial, ensure you are familiar with full-text search and the basics of using Milvus in LlamaIndex. Prerequisites Install dependencies Before getting started, make sure you have the following dependencies installed: If you’re using Google Colab, you may need to restart the runtime (Navigate to the “Runtime” menu at the top of the interface, and select “Restart session” from the dropdown menu.) Set up accounts This tutorial uses OpenAI for text embeddings and answer generation. You need to prepare the OpenAI API key. To use the Milvus vector store, specify your Milvus server URI (and optionally with the TOKEN). To start a Milvus server, you can set up a Milvus server by following the Milvus installation guide or simply trying Zilliz Cloud for free. Full-text search is currently supported in Milvus Standalone, Milvus Distributed, and Zilliz Cloud, but not yet in Milvus Lite (planned for future implementation). Reach out for more information. Download example data Run the following commands to download sample documents into the “data/paul\ graham” directory: RAG with Full-Text Search Integrating full-text search into a RAG system balances semantic search with precise and predictable keyword-based retrieval. You can also choose to only use full text search though it’s recommended to combine full text search with semantic search for better search results. Here for demonstration purpose we will show full text search alone and hybrid search. To get started, use SimpleDirectoryReaderLoad to load the essay “What I Worked On” by Paul Graham: Full-Text Search with BM25 LlamaIndex’s MilvusVectorStore supports full-text search, enabling efficient keyword-based retrieval. By using a built-in function as the sparse embedding function, it applies BM25 scoring to rank search results. In this section, we’ll demonstrate how to implement a RAG system using BM25 for full-text search. The above code inserts example documents into Milvus and builds an index to enable BM25 ranking for full-text search. It disables dense embedding and utilizes BM25BuiltInFunction with default parameters. You can specify the input and output fields in the BM25BuiltInFunction parameters: - input field names (str): The input text field (default: “text”). It indicates which text field the BM25 algorithm applied to. Change this if using your own collection with a different text field name. - output field names (str): The field where outputs of this BM25 function are stored (default: “sparse\ embedding”). Once the vector store is set up, you can perform full-text search queries using Milvus with query mode “sparse” or “text\ search”: Customize text analyzer Analyzers play a vital role in full-text search by breaking sentences into tokens and performing lexical processing, such as stemming and stop-word removal. They are typically language-specific. For more details, refer to Milvus Analyzer Guide. Milvus supports two types of analyzers: Built-in Analyzers and Custom Analyzers . By default, the BM25BuiltInFunction uses the standard built-in analyzer, which tokenizes text based on punctuation. To use a different analyzer or customize the existing one, you can pass value to the analyzer params argument: Hybrid Search with Reranker A hybrid search system combines semantic search and full-text search, optimizing retrieval performance in a RAG system. The following example uses OpenAI embedding for semantic search and BM25 for full-text search: How it works This approach stores documents in a Milvus collection with both vector fields: - embedding: Dense embeddings generated by OpenAI embedding model for semantic search. - sparse embedding: Sparse embeddings computed using BM25BuiltInFunction for full-text search. In addition, we have applied a reranking strategy using “RRFRanker” with its default parameters. To customize reranker, you are able to configure hybrid ranker and hybrid ranker params following the Milvus Reranking Guide. Now, let’s test the RAG system with a sample query: This hybrid approach ensures more accurate, context-aware responses in a RAG system by leveraging both semantic and keyword-based retrieval.
