text: Rockset 作為即時搜尋與分析資料庫，利用 indexing 來提供可擴展且高效的個人化、產品搜尋、semantic search、chatbot 應用程式等功能。由於 Rockset 專為即時設計，您可以基於不斷更新的串流資料建構這些響應式的應用程式。透過將 Rockset 與 LlamaIndex 整合，您可以輕鬆地在您自己的即時資料上使用 LLMs 來建立可投入生產的 vector search 應用程式。 我們將介紹如何將 Rockset 作為 vector store 在 LlamaIndex 中使用。 教學 在這個範例中，我們將使用 OpenAI 的 text-embedding-ada-002 模型來生成 embeddings，並使用 Rockset 作為 vector store 來儲存 embeddings。我們將從檔案中擷取文字並對內容提出問題。 設定環境 1. 在 Rockset console 中，使用 Write API 作為來源，從中建立一個 collection。將您的 collection 名稱為 llamaindex demo。配置以下 ingest transformation 並使用 VECTOR ENFORCE 來定義您的 embeddings field，以利用效能和儲存優化： 2. 在 Rockset console 中建立一個 API key，並設定 ROCKSET API KEY environment variable。找到您的 API server 這裡 並設定 ROCKSET API SERVER environment variable。設定 OPENAI API KEY environment variable。 3. 安裝依賴項。 終端機視窗 4. LlamaIndex 允許您從多種來源擷取資料。在此範例中，我們將讀取名為 constitution.txt 的文字檔案，該檔案是美國憲法的逐字稿，可從 這裡 找到。 資料擷取 使用 LlamaIndex 的 SimpleDirectoryReader class 將文字檔案轉換為 Document 物件的列表。 建立 LLM 和 service context。 建立 vector store 和 storage context。 將 documents 添加到 llamaindex demo collection 中並建立一個 index。 查詢 對您的 document 提出問題並生成回應。 執行程式。 Metadata Filtering Metadata filtering 允許您檢索符合特定篩選條件的相關 documents。 1. 將 nodes 添加到您的 vector store 並建立一個 index。 2. 定義 metadata filters。 3. 檢索符合篩選條件的相關 documents。 從現有 collection 建立 Index 您可以利用現有 collection 的資料建立 index。 從新 collection 建立 Index 您也可以建立一個新的 Rockset collection 作為 vector store。 設定 - collection : 要查詢的 collection 名稱（必填）。 - workspace : 包含該 collection 的 workspace 名稱。預設為 "commons"。 - api\ key : 用於驗證 Rockset 請求的 API key。如果傳入 client，則忽略此項。預設為 ROCKSET API KEY environment variable。 - api\ server : 用於 Rockset 請求的 API server。如果傳入 client，則忽略此項。預設為 ROCKSET API KEY environment variable 或如果 ROCKSET API SERVER 未設定則為 "https://api.use1a1.rockset.com"。 - client : 用於執行 Rockset 請求的 Rockset client 物件。如果未指定，將使用 api key 參數（或 ROCKSET API SERVER environment variable）和 api server 參數（或 ROCKSET API SERVER environment variable）內部建構一個 client 物件。 - embedding\ col : 包含 embeddings 的資料庫欄位名稱。預設為 "embedding"。 - metadata\ col : 包含 node 資料的資料庫欄位名稱。預設為 "metadata"。 - distance\ func : 用於衡量向量關係的指標。預設為 cosine similarity。
sourceText: As a real-time search and analytics database, Rockset uses indexing to deliver scalable and performant personalization, product search, semantic search, chatbot applications, and more. Since Rockset is purpose-built for real-time, you can build these responsive applications on constantly updating, streaming data. By integrating Rockset with LlamaIndex, you can easily use LLMs on your own real-time data for production-ready vector search applications. We’ll walk through a demonstration of how to use Rockset as a vector store in LlamaIndex. Tutorial In this example, we’ll use OpenAI’s text-embedding-ada-002 model to generate embeddings and Rockset as vector store to store embeddings. We’ll ingest text from a file and ask questions about the content. Setting Up Your Environment 1. Create a collection from the Rockset console with the Write API as your source. Name your collection llamaindex demo. Configure the following ingest transformation with VECTOR ENFORCE to define your embeddings field and take advantage of performance and storage optimizations: 2. Create an API key from the Rockset console and set the ROCKSET API KEY environment variable. Find your API server here and set the ROCKSET API SERVER environment variable. Set the OPENAI API KEY environment variable. 3. Install the dependencies. Terminal window 4. LlamaIndex allows you to ingest data from a variety of sources. For this example, we’ll read from a text file named constitution.txt, which is a transcript of the American Constitution, found here. Data ingestion Use LlamaIndex’s SimpleDirectoryReader class to convert the text file to a list of Document objects. Instantiate the LLM and service context. Instantiate the vector store and storage context. Add documents to the llamaindex demo collection and create an index. Querying Ask a question about your document and generate a response. Run the program. Metadata Filtering Metadata filtering allows you to retrieve relevant documents that match specific filters. 1. Add nodes to your vector store and create an index. 2. Define metadata filters. 3. Retrieve relevant documents that satisfy the filters. Creating an Index from an Existing Collection You can create indices with data from existing collections. Creating an Index from a New Collection You can also create a new Rockset collection to use as a vector store. Configuration - collection : Name of the collection to query (required). - workspace : Name of the workspace containing the collection. Defaults to "commons". - api\ key : The API key to use to authenticate Rockset requests. Ignored if client is passed in. Defaults to the ROCKSET API KEY environment variable. - api\ server : The API server to use for Rockset requests. Ignored if client is passed in. Defaults to the ROCKSET API KEY environment variable or "https://api.use1a1.rockset.com" if the ROCKSET API SERVER is not set. - client : Rockset client object to use to execute Rockset requests. If not specified, a client object is internally constructed with the api key parameter (or ROCKSET API SERVER environment variable) and the api server parameter (or ROCKSET API SERVER environment variable). - embedding\ col : The name of the database field containing embeddings. sourceTitle: Simple Vector Stores - Maximum Marginal Relevance Retrieval
text: 此筆筆記探討了 MMR retrieval \[1] 的使用。透過最大邊際相關性 (maximum marginal relevance)，可以迭代地找到與先前結果不相似的 documents。研究顯示這能提升 LLM 的 retrieval 性能 \[2]。 最大邊際相關性演算法如下： $$ \text{{MMR}} = \arg\max\ {d\ i \in D \setminus R} \[ \lambda \cdot Sim\ 1(d\ i, q) - (1 - \lambda) \cdot \max\ {d\ j \in R} Sim\ 2(d\ i, d\ j) ] $$ 其中，$D$ 是所有候選的 documents 集合，$R$ 是已選定的 documents 集合，$q$ 是查詢，$Sim\ 1$ 是 document 與查詢之間的相似度函數，$Sim\ 2$ 是兩個 documents 之間的相似度函數。$d\ i$ 和 $d\ j$ 分別是 $D$ 和 $R$ 中的 documents。 參數 $\lambda$ (mmr\ threshold) 控制著相關性（第一項）與多樣性（第二項）之間的權衡。如果 mmr\ threshold 接近 1，則更側重於相關性；而 mmr\ threshold 接近 0，則更側重於多樣性。 下載資料 llama\ index/docs/examples/data/paul\ graham 請注意，node 的分數會根據 threshold 進行縮放，並會因與先前 nodes 的相似度而受到額外懲罰。當 threshold 增加到 1 時，分數會相等，與先前 nodes 的相似度將被忽略，從而關閉 MMR 的影響。降低 threshold 會讓演算法更傾向於更具多樣性的 documents。 僅檢索演示 sourceText: This notebook explores the use of MMR retrieval \[1]. By using maximum marginal relevance, one can iteratively find documents that are dissimilar to previous results. It has been shown to improve performance for LLM retrievals \[2]. The maximum marginal relevance algorithm is as follows: $$ \text{{MMR}} = \arg\max\ {d\ i \in D \setminus R} \[ \lambda \cdot Sim\ 1(d\ i, q) - (1 - \lambda) \cdot \max\ {d\ j \in R} Sim\ 2(d\ i, d\ j) ] $$ Here, D is the set of all candidate documents, R is the set of already selected documents, q is the query, $Sim\ 1$ is the similarity function between a document and the query, and $Sim\ 2$ is the similarity function between two documents. $d\ i$ and $d\ j$ are documents in D and R respectively. The parameter λ (mmr\ threshold) controls the trade-off between relevance (the first term) and diversity (the second term). If mmr\ threshold is close to 1, more emphasis is put on relevance, while a mmr\ threshold close to 0 puts more emphasis on diversity. Download Data llama\ index/docs/examples/data/paul\ graham Note that the node score will be scaled with the threshold and will additionally be penalized for the similarity to previous nodes. As the threshold goes to 1, the scores will become equal and similarity to previous nodes will be ignored, turning off the impact of MMR. By lowering the threshold, the algorithm will prefer more diverse documents. Retrieval-Only Demonstration By setting a small chunk size and adjusting the “mmr\ threshold” parameter, we can see how the retrieved results change from very diverse (and less relevant) to less diverse (and more relevant/redundant). title: Tencent Cloud VectorDB
text: Tencent Cloud VectorDB 是一個完全託管、自研的企業級分散式資料庫服務，專為儲存、檢索和分析多維度 vector data 而設計。該資料庫支援多種 index type 和相似度計算方法。單一 index 可以支援高達 10 億的 vector 規模，並可支援數百萬的 QPS 和毫秒級的查詢延遲。Tencent Cloud Vector Database 不僅能為大型模型提供外部知識庫以提高大型模型回應的準確性，還可廣泛應用於推薦系統、NLP services、computer vision 和智慧客戶服務等 AI 領域。 本筆筆記展示了如何將 TencentVectorDB 作為 Vector Store 在 LlamaIndex 中使用。 要運行，您需要有 Database instance. 設定 如果您在 colab 上開啟此 Notebook，您可能需要安裝 LlamaIndex 🦙。 請提供 OpenAI access key 為了使用 OpenAI 的 embeddings，您需要提供一個 OpenAI API Key： 下載資料 建立和填充 Vector Store 您現在將從本地檔案載入 Paul Graham 的一些文章，並將它們儲存到 Tencent Cloud VectorDB 中。 初始化 Tencent Cloud VectorDB 建立 vector store 會建立底層資料庫 collection（如果尚不存在）： 現在將此 store 包裝成一個 index LlamaIndex abstraction，以便後續查詢： 請注意，上述 from documents 呼叫會同時執行多個操作：將輸入 documents 拆分成可管理的區塊（“nodes”），計算每個 node 的 embedding vectors，並將它們全部儲存在 Tencent Cloud VectorDB 中。 查詢 store 基本查詢 基於 MMR 的查詢 MMR (maximal marginal relevance) 方法旨在從 store 中檢索同時與查詢相關，但彼此之間差異最大的文本區塊，以在構建最終答案時提供更廣泛的上下文： 連接到現有的 store 由於此 store 由 Tencent Cloud VectorDB 支援，它在定義上是持久性的。因此，如果您想連接到先前建立和填充過的 store，請按以下方式操作： 從 index 中移除 documents 首先，從由 index 生成的 Retriever 中取得 document 的明確列表，或稱 “nodes”： 但請注意！在使用 vector store 時，您應該將 document 視為應刪除的合理單元，而不是屬於它的任何單個 node。在這個案例中，您只插入了一個單一的文字檔案，因此所有 nodes 都具有相同的 ref doc id： 現在假設您需要移除您上傳的文字檔案： 重複完全相同的查詢並檢查結果。您應該會看到 沒有結果 被找到： Metadata 過濾 Tencent Cloud VectorDB vector store 支援在查詢時以精確匹配 key=value 對的形式進行 metadata 過濾。以下單元，它們在一個全新的 collection 上運行，展示了此功能。 在此演示中，為了簡潔起見，載入單一來源 document（即 ../data/paul graham/paul graham essay.txt 文字檔案）。儘管如此，您將為 document 附加一些自訂 metadata，以說明如何根據附加到 documents 的 metadata 來限制查詢條件。 就是這樣：您現在可以為您的查詢引擎添加過濾條件： 要測試過濾器是否生效，請嘗試將其更改為僅使用 "dinos" documents……這次將不會有回覆了 :)
sourceText: Tencent Cloud VectorDB is a fully managed, self-developed, enterprise-level distributed database service designed for storing, retrieving, and analyzing multi-dimensional vector data. The database supports multiple index types and similarity calculation methods. A single index can support a vector scale of up to 1 billion and can support millions of QPS and millisecond-level query latency. Tencent Cloud Vector Database can not only provide an external knowledge base for large models to improve the accuracy of large model responses but can also be widely used in AI fields such as recommendation systems, NLP services, computer vision, and intelligent customer service. This notebook shows the basic usage of TencentVectorDB as a Vector Store in LlamaIndex. To run, you should have a Database instance. Setup If you’re opening this Notebook on colab, you will probably need to install LlamaIndex 🦙. Please provide OpenAI access key In order use embeddings by OpenAI you need to supply an OpenAI API Key: Download Data Creating and populating the Vector Store You will now load some essays by Paul Graham from a local file and store them into the Tencent Cloud VectorDB. Initialize the Tencent Cloud VectorDB Creation of the vector store entails creation of the underlying database collection if it does not exist yet: Now wrap this store into an index LlamaIndex abstraction for later querying: Note that the above from documents call does several things at once: it splits the input documents into chunks of manageable size (“nodes”), computes embedding vectors for each node, and stores them all in the Tencent Cloud VectorDB. Querying the store Basic querying MMR-based queries The MMR (maximal marginal relevance) method is designed to fetch text chunks from the store that are at the same time relevant to the query but as different as possible from each other, with the goal of providing a broader context to the building of the final answer: Connecting to an existing store Since this store is backed by Tencent Cloud VectorDB, it is persistent by definition. So, if you want to connect to a store that was created and populated previously, here is how: Removing documents from the index First get an explicit list of pieces of a document, or “nodes”, from a Retriever spawned from the index: But wait! When using the vector store, you should consider the document as the sensible unit to delete, and not any individual node belonging to it. Well, in this case, you just inserted a single text file, so all nodes will have the same ref doc id: Now let’s say you need to remove the text file you uploaded: Repeat the very same query and check the results now. You should see no results being found: Metadata filtering The Tencent Cloud VectorDB vector store support metadata filtering in the form of exact-match key=value pairs at query time. The following cells, which work on a brand new collection, demonstrate this feature. In this demo, for the sake of brevity, a single source document is loaded (the ../data/paul graham/paul graham essay.txt text file). Nevertheless, you will attach some custom metadata to the document to illustrate how you can can restrict queries with conditions on the metadata attached to the documents. That’s it: you can now add filtering to your query engine: To test that the filtering is at play, try to change it to use only "dinos" documents… there will be no answer this time :)

text: TiDB Cloud 是一個全面的 Database-as-a-Service (DBaaS) 解決方案，提供專用和無伺服器選項。TiDB Serverless 現在將內建的 vector search 整合到 MySQL 領域。透過此增強功能，您無需建立新的資料庫或額外的技術堆疊，即可在 TiDB Serverless 上無縫開發 AI 應用程式。在 處建立一個免費的 TiDB Serverless cluster，並開始使用 vector search 功能。 本筆筆記提供關於在 LlamaIndex 中使用 tidb vector search 的詳細指南。 設定環境 設定您的 OpenAI Key 設定您需要的 TiDB 連線設定。若要連線到您的 TiDB Cloud Cluster，請遵循以下步驟： - 前往您的 TiDB Cloud cluster Console，導航至 Connect 頁面。 - 選擇使用 SQLAlchemy 和 PyMySQL 連線的選項，並複製提供的連線 URL（不含密碼）。 - 將連線 URL 貼到您的程式碼中，替換 tidb connection string template 變數。 - 輸入您的密碼。 準備用於展示的資料 建立 TiDB Vectore Store 以下程式碼片段在 TiDB 中建立一個名為 VECTOR TABLE NAME 的表格，專為 vector 搜尋而優化。成功執行此程式碼後，您將可以直接在您的 TiDB 資料庫環境中查看和存取 VECTOR TABLE NAME 表格。 建立基於 tidb vectore store 的 query engine 注意：如果在此過程中遇到由於 MySQL protocol 的 packet size 限制而發生的錯誤，例如嘗試插入大量向量（例如 2000 行），您可以透過將插入拆分成較小的批次來緩解此問題。例如，您可以將 insert batch size 參數設定為較小的值（例如 1000），以避免超過 packet size 限制，確保您的資料順利插入到 TiDB vector store 中： 語義相似度搜尋 本節重點介紹 vector search 的基本概念以及如何使用 metadata 篩選器來精煉結果。請注意，tidb vector 只支援 Default VectorStoreQueryMode。 使用 metadata 篩選器 使用 metadata 篩選器執行搜尋，以檢索符合所應用篩選器的特定數量最近鄰結果。 再次查詢 刪除 documents 檢查 documents 是否已被刪除

title: Timescale Vector Store (PostgreSQL)
text: 這份筆記說明如何使用 Postgres vector store TimescaleVector 來儲存和查詢 vector embeddings。 什麼是 Timescale Vector？ Timescale Vector 是為 AI 應用程式而設計的 PostgreSQL++。 Timescale Vector 讓您能在 PostgreSQL 中有效率地儲存和查詢數百萬個 vector embeddings。 - 透過 DiskANN 啟發的索引演算法，利用更快速、更準確的相似性搜尋，增強了 pgvector，針對數百萬個 vector 進行搜尋。 - 透過自動的時間基分區和索引，實現快速的時間基 vector 搜尋。 - 提供一個熟悉的 SQL 介面，用於查詢 vector embeddings 和關聯資料。 Timescale Vector 從 POC 到 production 都能與您一起擴展： - 透過在單一資料庫中儲存關聯元資料、vector embeddings 和時間序列資料，簡化了操作。 - 受益於堅實的 PostgreSQL 基礎，具備企業級功能，例如串流備份和複製、高可用性以及行級安全性。 - 讓您在企業級安全性和合規性下享有無憂的體驗。 如何使用 Timescale Vector Timescale Vector 可在 Timescale 的雲端 PostgreSQL 平台上使用。（目前沒有自託管版本。） LlamaIndex 用戶可獲得 Timescale Vector 的 90 天免費試用。 - 要開始使用，請 sign up 到 Timescale，建立一個新的資料庫，並依照本筆記操作！ - 請參閱 Timescale Vector explainer blog 了解更多詳情和效能基準測試。 - 請參閱 installation instructions 了解更多關於在 python 中使用 Timescale Vector 的詳細資訊。 0. 設定 讓我們匯入本筆記所需的一切。 如果您在 colab 上開啟此 Notebook，您可能需要安裝 LlamaIndex 🦙。 設定 OpenAI API Key 為了為載入到索引中的 documents 建立 embeddings，讓我們設定您的 OpenAI API key： 建立一個 PostgreSQL 資料庫並取得 Timescale service URL 您需要一個 service url 來連接到您的 Timescale 資料庫實例。 首先，在 Timescale 中啟動一個新的雲端資料庫（使用上面的連結免費註冊）。 要連接到您的雲端 PostgreSQL 資料庫，您需要您的 service URI，它可以在您建立新資料庫後下載的 cheatsheet 或 .env 文件中找到。 URI 的格式會像這樣： postgres://tsdbadmin: @ .tsdb.cloud.timescale.com: /tsdb?sslmode=require 1. 使用 Timescale Vector 進行簡單相似性搜尋 下載資料 載入 documents 在這個範例中，我們將使用一個 SimpleDirectoryReader 來載入儲存在 paul graham essay 目錄中的 documents。 SimpleDirectoryReader 是 LlamaIndex 最常用的資料連線器之一，用於從目錄中讀取一個或多個檔案。 建立一個帶有 TimescaleVectorStore 的 VectorStore 索引 接下來，為了執行相似性搜尋，我們首先建立一個 TimescaleVector vector store 來儲存我們從文章內容中得到的 vector embeddings。TimescaleVectorStore 需要幾個參數，即我們上面載入的 service url，以及我們將用作儲存 vector 的表格名稱 table name。 然後，我們在由 documents 支援的 documents 上建立一個 Vector Store Index，該索引由 Timescale 支援。 查詢索引 現在我們在 VectorStore 中索引了 documents，我們可以透過使用預設的 query engine 來詢問索引中的 documents。 請注意，您也可以設定查詢引擎來配置返回的 top\ k 最相似的結果數量，以及用於過濾結果的元資料過濾器。請參閱 設定標準查詢設定區段 了解更多詳情。 查詢現有索引 在上面的範例中，我們從 documents 加載了一個新的 Timescale Vector vectorstore 並建立索引。接下來我們將探討如何查詢現有的索引。我們只需要服務 URI 和我們想要存取的資料表名稱。 2. 使用 ANN 搜尋索引來加速查詢 (注意：這些索引是 ANN 索引，與 LlamaIndex 中的索引概念不同) 您可以透過在 embedding 欄位上建立索引來加速相似度查詢。您應該在您已攝取大量資料後才執行此操作。 Timescale Vector 支援以下索引： - timescale\ vector\ index：一種基於 disk-ann 的圖索引，用於快速相似度搜尋（預設）。 - pgvector’s HNSW index：一種分層可導航小世界圖索引，用於快速相似度搜尋。 - pgvector’s IVFFLAT index：一種反向檔案索引，用於快速相似度搜尋。 重要提示：在 PostgreSQL 中，每個資料表只能有一個欄位的索引。因此，如果您想測試不同索引類型的效能，可以透過以下方式進行：(1) 建立具有不同索引的多個資料表，(2) 在同一個資料表中建立多個向量欄位並對每個欄位建立不同的索引，或 (3) 刪除並重新建立同一個欄位的索引並比較結果。 使用不帶額外參數的 create index() 函式將預設建立一個 timescale vector (DiskANN) 索引，使用預設參數。 您也可以指定索引的參數。請參閱 Timescale Vector 文件，以獲取有關不同參數及其對效能影響的完整討論。 Timescale Vector 也支援 HNSW 和 ivfflat 索引： 我們建議一般使用 timescale-vector 或 HNSW 索引。 3. 帶有時間篩選的相似度搜尋 Timescale Vector 的一個關鍵應用場景是高效的時間基向量搜尋。Timescale Vector 透過按時間自動對向量（及相關的 metadata）進行分區來實現這一點。這讓您可以同時根據查詢向量的相似度和時間來高效地查詢向量。 基於時間的向量搜尋功能對以下應用程式很有幫助： - 儲存和檢索 LLM 回應歷史（例如聊天機器人） - 找出與查詢向量相似的最新嵌入（例如最新新聞）。 - 將相似度搜尋限制在相關的時間範圍內（例如對知識庫提出基於時間的問題）。 為了說明如何使用 TimescaleVector 的時間基向量搜尋功能，我們將使用 TimescaleDB 的 git log 歷史作為範例資料集並對其提出問題。每個 git commit 條目都有一個相關的時間戳記，以及自然語言訊息和其他 metadata（例如作者、commit hash 等）。 我們將說明如何使用 TimescaleVector 的 vectorstore 來建立帶有時間 UUID 的 nodes，並使用時間範圍篩選器執行相似度搜尋。 從 git log CSV 檔案中提取內容和 metadata 首先，將 git log csv 檔案載入到我們 PostgreSQL 資料庫中的一個新集合，命名為 timescale commits。 注意：由於這是一個示範，我們只會處理前 1000 筆記錄。在實際應用中，您可以載入任意數量的記錄。 我們將定義一個輔助函式，根據時間為 node 和相關的向量嵌入建立一個 uuid。我們將使用此函式為每個 git log 條目建立一個 uuid。 重要提示：如果您正在處理 documents/nodes 並希望將當前日期和時間與向量關聯起來以進行時間基搜尋，您可以跳過此步驟。當 nodes 被預設新增到 Timescale Vector 的資料表中時，uuid 將會自動生成。在我們的案例中，因為我們希望 uuid 基於過去的時間戳記，所以我們需要手動建立 uuid。 接著，我們將定義一個函式來為每個 git log 條目建立一個 TextNode。我們將使用上面定義的輔助函式 create uuid() 來根據其 timestampe 為每個 node 建立一個 uuid。我們將使用上面提到的輔助函式 create date() 和 split name() 從 git log 條目中提取相關的 metadata 並將其新增到 node 中。 接下來，我們將為每個 node 的內容建立 vector embeddings，以便我們可以在每個 node 相關的文字上執行 similarity search。我們將使用 OpenAIEmbedding 模型來建立這些 embeddings。 讓我們檢視一下我們集合中的第一個 node 看它長什麼樣子。 將 documents 和 metadata 載入到 TimescaleVector vectorstore 現在我們已經準備好 nodes 並將 embeddings 添加到它們，讓我們將它們新增到我們的 TimescaleVector vectorstore 中。 我們將從我們建立的 nodes 列表中建立一個 Timescale Vector instance。 首先，我們將定義一個 collection name，這將是我們在 PostgreSQL 資料庫中的表格名稱。 我們還將定義一個 time delta，我們將其傳遞給 time partition interval 的參數，它將用作按時間對資料進行分區的間隔。每個 partition 都將包含指定時間長度的資料。為了簡化，我們使用 7 天，但您可以選擇任何對您的使用案例有意義的值——例如，如果您經常查詢最近的 vectors，您可能希望使用較小的 time delta，如 1 天；或者如果您查詢跨越十年的時間範圍的 vectors，則可能希望使用較大的 time delta，如 6 個月或 1 年。 然後我們將 nodes 添加到 Timescale Vector vectorstore 中。 依時間和相似度查詢 vectors 現在我們已經將 documents 載入到 TimescaleVector 中，我們可以依時間和相似度查詢它們。 TimescaleVector 提供多種方法來透過進行帶有時間過濾的 similarity search 來查詢 vectors。讓我們看一下每個方法。 首先，我們定義一個 query string 並獲取 query string 的 vector embedding。 然後我們設定一些變數，我們將在我們的時間過濾器中使用它們。 方法 1：在提供的開始日期和結束日期範圍內過濾。 讓我們檢查一下從 similarity search 返回的 nodes： 注意查詢只返回指定日期範圍內的結果。 方法 2：在提供的開始日期之後的時間 delta 範圍內過濾。 再次注意，只有在開始日期（8 月 1 日）和定義的時間 delta 後（7 天後）之間的 nodes 被返回。 方法 3：在提供的結束日期之前和一個時間 delta 範圍內過濾。 主要重點是，在每個結果中，只會返回在指定時間範圍內的 vectors。這些查詢非常有效率，因為它們只需要搜尋相關的分區。 4. 將 TimescaleVector store 作為一個 Retriever 和查詢引擎使用 現在我們已經探索了基本的 similarity search 和帶有時間過濾的 similarity search，讓我們看看如何使用 Timescale Vector 及其在 LLamaIndex 中的 retriever 和查詢引擎的功能。 首先，我們將看看如何將 TimescaleVector 用作一個 retriever，特別是作為一個 Vector Store Retriever。 為了限制檢索到的 nodes 範圍在相關的時間範圍內，我們可以利用 TimescaleVector 的時間過濾器。在建立 retriever 時，我們只需將時間過濾參數作為 vector strored kwargs 傳遞即可。 接下來我們將看看如何將 TimescaleVector 用作一個 query engine。我們再次使用 TimescaleVector 的時間過濾器，透過在建立查詢引擎時傳遞我們的時間過濾參數作為 vector strored kwargs，來將搜尋範圍限制在相關的時間區間內。
sourceText: This notebook shows how to use the Postgres vector store TimescaleVector to store and query vector embeddings. What is Timescale Vector? Timescale Vector is PostgreSQL++ for AI applications. Timescale Vector enables you to efficiently store and query millions of vector embeddings in PostgreSQL. - Enhances pgvector with faster and more accurate similarity search on millions of vectors via DiskANN inspired indexing algorithm. - Enables fast time-based vector search via automatic time-based partitioning and indexing. - Provides a familiar SQL interface for querying vector embeddings and relational data. Timescale Vector scales with you from POC to production: - Simplifies operations by enabling you to store relational metadata, vector embeddings, and time-series data in a single database. - Benefits from rock-solid PostgreSQL foundation with enterprise-grade feature liked streaming backups and replication, high-availability and row-level security. - Enables a worry-free experience with enterprise-grade security and compliance. How to use Timescale Vector Timescale Vector is available on Timescale, the cloud PostgreSQL platform. (There is no self-hosted version at this time.) LlamaIndex users get a 90-day free trial for Timescale Vector. - To get started, signup to Timescale, create a new database and follow this notebook! - See the Timescale Vector explainer blog for details and performance benchmarks. - See the installation instructions for more details on using Timescale Vector in python. 0. Setup Let’s import everything we’ll need for this notebook. If you’re opening this Notebook on colab, you will probably need to install LlamaIndex 🦙. Setup OpenAI API Key To create embeddings for documents loaded into the index, let’s configure your OpenAI API key: Create a PostgreSQL database and get a Timescale service URL You need a service url to connect to your Timescale database instance. First, launch a new cloud database in Timescale (sign up for free using the link above). To connect to your cloud PostgreSQL database, you’ll need your service URI, which can be found in the cheatsheet or .env file you downloaded after creating a new database. The URI will look something like this: postgres://tsdbadmin: @ .tsdb.cloud.timescale.com: /tsdb?sslmode=require 1. Simple Similarity Search with Timescale Vector Download Data Loading documents For this example, we’ll use a SimpleDirectoryReader to load the documents stored in the paul graham essay directory. The SimpleDirectoryReader is one of LlamaIndex’s most commonly used data connectors to read one or multiple files from a directory. Create a VectorStore Index with the TimescaleVectorStore Next, to perform a similarity search, we first create a TimescaleVector vector store to store our vector embeddings from the essay content. TimescaleVectorStore takes a few arguments, namely the service url which we loaded above, along with a table name which we will be the name of the table that the vectors are stored in. Then we create a Vector Store Index on the documents backed by Timescale using the previously documents. Query the index Now that we’ve indexed the documents in our VectorStore, we can ask questions about our documents in the index by using the default query engine. Note you can also configure the query engine to configure the top\ k most similar results returned, as well as metadata filters to filter the results by. See the configure standard query setting section for more details. Querying existing index In the example above, we created a new Timescale Vector vectorstore and index from documents we loaded. Next we’ll look at how to query an existing index. All we need is the service URI and the table name we want to access. 2. Using ANN search indexes to speed up queries (Note: These indexes are ANN indexes, and differ from the index concept in LlamaIndex) You can speed up similarity queries by creating an index on the embedding column. You should only do this once you have ingested a large part of your data. Timescale Vector supports the following indexes: - timescale\ vector\ index: a disk-ann inspired graph index for fast similarity search (default). - pgvector’s HNSW index: a hierarchical navigable small world graph index for fast similarity search. - pgvector’s IVFFLAT index: an inverted file index for fast similarity search. Important note: In PostgreSQL, each table can only have one index on a particular column. So if you’d like to test the performance of different index types, you can do so either by (1) creating multiple tables with different indexes, (2) creating multiple vector columns in the same table and creating different indexes on each column, or (3) by dropping and recreating the index on the same column and comparing results. Using the create index() function without additional arguments will create a timescale vector (DiskANN) index by default, using the default parameters. You can also specify the parameters for the index. See the Timescale Vector documentation for a full discussion of the different parameters and their effects on performance. Timescale Vector also supports HNSW and ivfflat indexes: We recommend using timescale-vector or HNSW indexes in general. 3. Similarity Search with time-based filtering A key use case for Timescale Vector is efficient time-based vector search. Timescale Vector enables this by automatically partitioning vectors (and associated metadata) by time. This allows you to efficiently query vectors by both similarity to a query vector and time. Time-based vector search functionality is helpful for applications like: - Storing and retrieving LLM response history (e.g. chatbots) - Finding the most recent embeddings that are similar to a query vector (e.g recent news). - Constraining similarity search to a relevant time range (e.g asking time-based questions about a knowledge base) To illustrate how to use TimescaleVector’s time-based vector search functionality, we’ll use the git log history for TimescaleDB as a sample dataset and ask questions about it. Each git commit entry has a timestamp associated with it, as well as natural language message and other metadata (e.g author, commit hash etc). We’ll illustrate how to create nodes with a time-based uuid and how run similarity searches with time range filters using the TimescaleVector vectorstore. Extract content and metadata from git log CSV file First lets load in the git log csv file into a new collection in our PostgreSQL database named timescale commits. Note: Since this is a demo, we will only work with the first 1000 records. In practice, you can load as many records as you want. We’ll define a helper funciton to create a uuid for a node and associated vector embedding based on its timestamp. We’ll use this function to create a uuid for each git log entry. Important note: If you are working with documents/nodes and want the current date and time associated with vector for time-based search, you can skip this step. A uuid will be automatically generated when the nodes are added to the table in Timescale Vector by default. In our case, because we want the uuid to be based on the timestamp in the past, we need to create the uuids manually. Next, we’ll define a function to create a TextNode for each git log entry. We’ll use the helper function create uuid() we defined above to create a uuid for each node based on its timestampe. And we’ll use the helper functions create date() and split name() above to extract relevant metadata from the git log entry and add them to the node. Next we’ll create vector embeddings of the content of each node so that we can perform similarity search on the text associated with each node. We’ll use the OpenAIEmbedding model to create the embeddings. Let’s examine the first node in our collection to see what it looks like. Load documents and metadata into TimescaleVector vectorstore Now that we have prepared our nodes and added embeddings to them, let’s add them into our TimescaleVector vectorstore. We’ll create a Timescale Vector instance from the list of nodes we created. First, we’ll define a collection name, which will be the name of our table in the PostgreSQL database. We’ll also define a time delta, which we pass to the time partition interval argument, which will be used to as the interval for partitioning the data by time. Each partition will consist of data for the specified length of time. We’ll use 7 days for simplicity, but you can pick whatever value make sense for your use case — for example if you query recent vectors frequently you might want to use a smaller time delta like 1 day, or if you query vectors over a decade long time period then you might want to use a larger time delta like 6 months or 1 year. Then we’ll add the nodes to the Timescale Vector vectorstore. Querying vectors by time and similarity Now that we have loaded our documents into TimescaleVector, we can query them by time and similarity. TimescaleVector provides multiple methods for querying vectors by doing similarity search with time-based filtering Let’s take a look at each method below. First we define a query string and get the vector embedding for the query string. Then we set some variables which we’ll use in our time filters. Method 1: Filter within a provided start date and end date. Let’s inspect the nodes that were returned from the similarity search: Note how the query only returns results within the specified date range. Method 2: Filter within a provided start date, and a time delta later. Once again, notice how only nodes between the start date (1 August) and the defined time delta later (7 days later) are returned. Method 3: Filter within a provided end date and a time delta earlier. The main takeaway is that in each result above, only vectors within the specified time range are returned. These queries are very efficient as they only need to search the relevant partitions. 4. Using TimescaleVector store as a Retriever and Query engine Now that we’ve explored basic similarity search and similarity search with time-based filters, let’s look at how to these features of Timescale Vector with LLamaIndex’s retriever and query engine. First we’ll look at how to use TimescaleVector as a retriever, specifically a Vector Store Retriever. To constrain the nodes retrieved to a relevant time-range, we can use TimescaleVector’s time filters. We simply pass the time filter parameters as vector strored kwargs when creating the retriever. Next we’ll look at how to use TimescaleVector as a query engine. Once again, we use TimescaleVector’s time filters to constrain the search to a relevant time range by passing our time filter parameters as vector strored kwargs when creating the query engine.

text: 此筆記示範如何使用與 Google Cloud Vertex AI Vector Search vector database 相關的功能。 Google Vertex AI 向量 搜尋，以前稱為 Vertex AI Matching Engine，提供業界領先的高擴展性低延遲 vector database。這些 vector database 通常被稱為 vector similarity-matching 或 approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) service。 注意 ：LlamaIndex 需要 Vertex AI Vector Search endpoint，且已建立部署的 index。建立一個空的 index 可能需要長達一分鐘，將 index 部署到 endpoint 可能需要長達 30 分鐘。 要查看如何建立 index，請參閱 建立 Index 並將其部署至 Endpoint 部分。 如果您已經有部署的 index，請跳至 Create VectorStore from texts。 安裝 如果您在 colab 中開啟此 Notebook，您可能需要安裝 LlamaIndex 🦙。 建立 Index 並部署到 Endpoint - 此部分示範如何建立新的 index 並將其部署到 endpoint。 建立 Cloud Storage bucket 建立一個空的 Index 注意： 在建立 index 時，您應該指定一個 “index\ update\ method”——BATCH UPDATE 或 STREAM UPDATE。 Batch index 用於當您想批次更新您的 index，包含在一段時間內儲存的資料，例如每週或每月處理的系統。 Streaming index 是當您希望 index 資料隨著新資料添加到您的 datastore 而更新，例如，如果您有一家書店並希望盡快在網路上顯示新的庫存。 您選擇哪種類型很重要，因為設定和要求是不同的。 請參閱 Official Documentation 和 API reference 以獲取有關配置 index 的更多詳細資訊。 建立 Endpoint 要使用 index，您需要建立一個 index endpoint。它作為一個伺服器實例，接收您 index 的查詢請求。endpoint 可以是 public endpoint 或 private endpoint。 讓我們建立一個 public endpoint。 將 Index 部署到 Endpoint 使用 index endpoint，您可以透過指定一個唯一的 deployed index ID 來部署 index。 注意：此操作可能需要長達 30 分鐘。 從文本建立 Vector Store 注意：如果您已經有現有的 Vertex AI Vector Search Index 和 Endpoints，您可以使用以下程式碼將它們指派： 從純文字建立一個簡單的 vector store，不帶 metadata 篩選器 使用 Vertex AI Embeddings 作為 embeddings model 向您的 vectore store 添加 vectors 和 mapped text chunks 執行相似度搜尋 添加 documents 及其 metadata 屬性並使用 filters 使用 filters 執行相似度搜尋 使用 Vertex AI Vector Search 和 Gemini Pro 解析、建立索引和查詢 PDF --- 清理 請在執行實驗後刪除 Vertex AI Vector Search Index 和 Index Endpoint，以避免產生額外費用。請注意，只要 endpoint 正在運行，您將會被收取費用。 ⚠️ 注意：啟用 \CLEANUP\ RESOURCES\ 標誌會刪除 Vector Search Index、Index Endpoint 和 Cloud Storage bucket。請謹慎使用。 - 停用 index 並刪除 index endpoint - 刪除 index - 刪除 Cloud Storage bucket 中的內容
sourceText: This notebook shows how to use functionality related to the Google Cloud Vertex AI Vector Search vector database. Google Vertex AI Vector Search, formerly known as Vertex AI Matching Engine, provides the industry’s leading high-scale low latency vector database. These vector databases are commonly referred to as vector similarity-matching or an approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) service. Note : LlamaIndex expects Vertex AI Vector Search endpoint and deployed index is already created. An empty index creation time take upto a minute and deploying an index to the endpoint can take upto 30 min. To see how to create an index refer to the section Create Index and deploy it to an Endpoint\ If you already have an index deployed , skip to Create VectorStore from texts Installation If you’re opening this Notebook on colab, you will probably need to install LlamaIndex 🦙. Create Index and deploy it to an Endpoint - This section demonstrates creating a new index and deploying it to an endpoint. Create Cloud Storage bucket Create an empty Index Note : While creating an index you should specify an “index\ update\ method” - BATCH UPDATE or STREAM UPDATE A batch index is for when you want to update your index in a batch, with data which has been stored over a set amount of time, like systems which are processed weekly or monthly. A streaming index is when you want index data to be updated as new data is added to your datastore, for instance, if you have a bookstore and want to show new inventory online as soon as possible. Which type you choose is important, since setup and requirements are different. Refer Official Documentation and API reference for more details on configuring indexes Create an Endpoint To use the index, you need to create an index endpoint. It works as a server instance accepting query requests for your index. An endpoint can be a public endpoint or a private endpoint. Let’s create a public endpoint. Deploy Index to the Endpoint With the index endpoint, deploy the index by specifying a unique deployed index ID. NOTE : This operation can take upto 30 minutes. Create Vector Store from texts NOTE : If you have existing Vertex AI Vector Search Index and Endpoints, you can assign them using following code: Create a simple vector store from plain text without metadata filters Use Vertex AI Embeddings as the embeddings model Add vectors and mapped text chunks to your vectore store Running a similarity search Add documents with metadata attributes and use filters Running a similarity search with filters Parse, Index and Query PDFs using Vertex AI Vector Search and Gemini Pro --- Clean Up Please delete Vertex AI Vector Search Index and Index Endpoint after running your experiments to avoid incurring additional charges. Please note that you will be charged as long as the endpoint is running. ⚠️ NOTE: Enabling \CLEANUP\ RESOURCES\ flag deletes Vector Search Index, Index Endpoint and Cloud Storage bucket. Please run it with caution. - Undeploy indexes and Delete index endpoint - Delete index - Delete contents from the Cloud Storage bucket

sourceText: This notebook demonstrates how to use Vertex AI Vector Search v2.0 with LlamaIndex. Vertex AI Vector Search v2.0 introduces a simplified collection-based architecture that eliminates the need for separate index creation and endpoint deployment. v2.0 vs v1.0 Feature v1.0 v2.0 ------------- --------------------------------- ----------------- Architecture Index + Endpoint Collection Setup Steps Create index → Deploy to endpoint Create collection GCS Bucket Required for batch updates Not needed Hybrid Search Not supported Supported Note : For v1.0 usage, see VertexAIVectorSearchDemo.ipynb Install Dependencies Install LlamaIndex with v2 support: Note : V2 support requires llama-index-vector-stores-vertexaivectorsearch version that supports Vertex AI Vector Search v2.0 API. Authentication (if using Colab): Configuration Set your Google Cloud project details: Create a v2 Collection Unlike v1.0 which requires creating an index and deploying it to an endpoint, v2.0 only requires creating a collection. Important for Hybrid Search: The collection schema below is configured to support all hybrid search features: - Text Search : String fields (text, category, color) can be searched with keywords - Semantic Search : The vertex embedding config enables auto-embeddings for SEMANTIC HYBRID mode - Filtering : Numeric (price) and string fields support metadata filtering Set Up LlamaIndex Components Create v2 Vector Store Creating a v2 vector store is simple - just specify api version="v2" and your collection id: Add Documents Simple Text Nodes Nodes with Metadata Add nodes with metadata for filtering and hybrid search: Query the Vector Store Simple Similarity Search Search with Metadata Filters RAG Query with LLM Use the vector store with an LLM for retrieval-augmented generation: v2-Only Features Delete Specific Nodes Clear All Data (v2 only) v2 supports clearing all data from a collection - this is NOT available in v1: Hybrid Search (v2 Only) v2 supports hybrid search , combining vector similarity with text-based search for improved retrieval quality. This is particularly useful when you want to leverage both semantic understanding (vectors) and exact keyword matching (text search). Supported Query Modes Mode Description Use Case ----------------- ------------------------------ ------------------------------ DEFAULT Dense vector similarity search Standard semantic search TEXT SEARCH Full-text keyword search Exact keyword matching HYBRID Vector + Text with RRF fusion Best of both worlds SEMANTIC HYBRID Vector + Semantic search Auto-embedding semantic search Ranker Options Ranker Description --------------- ------------------------------------------- rrf (default) Reciprocal Rank Fusion with alpha weighting vertex AI-powered semantic ranking via Vertex AI Create Hybrid-Enabled Vector Store To enable hybrid search, set enable hybrid=True and specify which fields to use for text search: TEXT\ SEARCH Mode - Keyword Search Use TEXT SEARCH mode for full-text keyword matching. This is useful when you want exact keyword matches rather than semantic similarity: HYBRID Mode - Vector + Text Search Use HYBRID mode to combine vector similarity with text search. The alpha parameter controls the balance: - alpha=1.0 - Pure vector search - alpha=0.5 - Balanced - alpha=0.0 - Pure text search SEMANTIC\ HYBRID Mode SEMANTIC HYBRID combines your dense vector search with Vertex AI’s built-in semantic search. This requires the collection to have vertex embedding config configured for auto-embeddings. Using VertexRanker Instead of RRF, you can use Vertex AI’s semantic ranker for AI-powered result ranking: Hybrid Search with Query Engine (RAG) You can also use hybrid search with the standard LlamaIndex query engine for RAG applications: Hybrid Search Parameters Reference Parameter Type Default Description ----------------------------- ----------- ---------------------------------- ------------------------------------- enable hybrid bool False Enable hybrid search modes text search fields List[str] None Data fields for text search embedding field str "embedding" Vector field name default hybrid alpha float 0.5 Default RRF weight (0=text, 1=vector) hybrid ranker str "rrf" Ranker: “rrf” or “vertex” semantic task type str "RETRIEVAL QUERY" Task type for SemanticSearch vertex ranker model str "semantic-ranker-default@latest" VertexRanker model vertex ranker title field str None Title field for VertexRanker vertex ranker content field str None Content field for VertexRanker Clean Up Delete the collection when done to avoid charges: Summary This notebook demonstrated: 1. Simple Setup : v2 only requires a collection - no index/endpoint deployment 2. Easy Integration : Just add api version="v2" to use the new API 3. Same Interface : All LlamaIndex operations (add, query, delete) work the same 4. New Features : v2 adds clear() method not available in v1 5. Hybrid Search : Combine vector and text search for better retrieval: - TEXT SEARCH - Full-text keyword search - HYBRID - Vector + text with RRF fusion - SEMANTIC HYBRID - Vector + semantic search - VertexRanker for AI-powered ranking Migration from v1 For detailed migration instructions, see V2\ MIGRATION.md

text: 本指南說明如何在 LlamaIndex 中使用 Weaviate 進行 auto-retrieval 。 Weaviate vector database 除了用於語義搜尋的查詢字串外，還支援一組 metadata filters。對於自然語言查詢，我們會先使用大型語言模型 (LLM) 來推斷一組 metadata filters 以及應傳遞給 vector database 的正確查詢字串（此查詢字串也可以是空白的）。然後，這個整體查詢組合會對 vector database 執行。 這使得我們能夠進行比 top-k 語義搜尋更動態、更具表達性的檢索方式。給定查詢的相關上下文可能僅需要對 metadata tag 進行過濾，或者需要對過濾後的集合進行 filtering + semantic search 的組合，或者僅僅是原始的 semantic search。 設定 我們首先定義 imports 並定義一個空的 Weaviate collection。 如果您在 Colab 上開啟此 Notebook，您可能需要安裝 LlamaIndex 🦙。 我們將使用 GPT-4 及其推理能力來推斷 metadata filters。根據您的使用情境，"gpt-3.5-turbo" 也可以使用。 此 Notebook 在 Embedded mode 中使用 Weaviate，此模式支援 Linux 和 macOS。 如果您希望嘗試 Weaviate 的完全託管服務 Weaviate Cloud Services (WCS)，您可以啟用註釋中的程式碼。 定義一些範例資料 我們將一些包含文字區塊的範例 nodes 插入到 vector database 中。請注意，每個 TextNode 不僅包含文字，還包含 metadata，例如 category 和 country。這些 metadata 欄位將在底層 vector db 中被轉換/儲存為此格式。 使用 Weaviate Vector Store 建構 Vector Index 在這裡，我們將資料載入到 vector store 中。如上所述，每個 node 的文字和 metadata 都會被轉換成 Weaviate 中的對應表示。現在我們可以在 Weaviate 的資料上執行 semantic 查詢和 metadata filtering。 定義 VectorIndexAutoRetriever 我們定義核心的 VectorIndexAutoRetriever 模組。該模組接收 VectorStoreInfo，其中包含 vector store collection 的結構化描述及其支援的 metadata filters。此資訊將用於 auto-retrieval prompt 中，讓 LLM 推斷 metadata filters。 對一些範例資料進行運行 我們嘗試對一些範例資料進行運行。請注意 metadata filters 是如何被推斷的——這有助於更精確的檢索！
sourceText: This guide shows how to perform auto-retrieval in LlamaIndex with Weaviate. The Weaviate vector database supports a set of metadata filters in addition to a query string for semantic search. Given a natural language query, we first use a Large Language Model (LLM) to infer a set of metadata filters as well as the right query string to pass to the vector database (either can also be blank). This overall query bundle is then executed against the vector database. This allows for more dynamic, expressive forms of retrieval beyond top-k semantic search. The relevant context for a given query may only require filtering on a metadata tag, or require a joint combination of filtering + semantic search within the filtered set, or just raw semantic search. Setup We first define imports and define an empty Weaviate collection. If you’re opening this Notebook on Colab, you will probably need to install LlamaIndex 🦙. We will be using GPT-4 for its reasoning capabilities to infer the metadata filters. Depending on your use case, "gpt-3.5-turbo" can work as well. This Notebook uses Weaviate in Embedded mode, which is supported on Linux and macOS. If you prefer to try out Weaviate’s fully managed service, Weaviate Cloud Services (WCS), you can enable the code in the comments. Defining Some Sample Data We insert some sample nodes containing text chunks into the vector database. Note that each TextNode not only contains the text, but also metadata e.g. category and country. These metadata fields will get converted/stored as such in the underlying vector db. Build Vector Index with Weaviate Vector Store Here we load the data into the vector store. As mentioned above, both the text and metadata for each node will get converted into corresponding representations in Weaviate. We can now run semantic queries and also metadata filtering on this data from Weaviate. Define VectorIndexAutoRetriever We define our core VectorIndexAutoRetriever module. The module takes in VectorStoreInfo, which contains a structured description of the vector store collection and the metadata filters it supports. This information will then be used in the auto-retrieval prompt where the LLM infers metadata filters. Running over some sample data We try running over some sample data. Note how metadata filters are inferred - this helps with more precise retrieval!

text: 簡介 本腳本演示如何爬取產品網站，擷取相關資訊，建立一個適合 SEO 的知識圖譜（Knowledge Graph，即 PDPs 和 PLPs 的結構化表示），並利用它來改善搜尋和使用者體驗。 主要功能與函式庫： - 網路爬取 (Advertools) - 建立產品詳情頁 (PDPs) 和產品列表頁 (PLPs) 的知識圖譜 - WordLift - 產品推薦 (WordLift Neural Search) - 建立購物助理 (WordLift + LlamaIndex 🦙) 此方法能提升電子商務網站的 SEO 表現和使用者參與度。 瞭解更多相關資訊請點擊這裡： - - -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- [](https://wordlift.io) 由 Andrea Volpini 和 David Riccitelli MIT License 最後更新時間： 2024 年 7 月 31 日 設定 使用 Advertools 爬取網站 使用 WordLift 建立 KG 🕸 執行展示 現在使用 GraphQL 在 KG 中查詢產品 利用知識圖譜 現在我們已成功為電子商務網站建立了一個包含產品嵌入 (product embeddings) 的知識圖譜，我們可以利用它來提升使用者體驗和功能。為每個產品生成的嵌入，使我們能夠執行語義相似性搜尋並建立更智慧的系統。 為您的網頁新增結構化資料 在本節中，我們將對 WordLift 的資料 API 進行簡單測試。此 API 用於將來自知識圖譜 (KG) 的結構化資料標記注入到您的網頁中。結構化資料有助於搜尋引擎更好地理解您的內容，可能在搜尋結果中帶來豐富片段 (rich snippets) 和提升 SEO。 對於本筆筆記，我們正在使用一個預先配置好的 KG 在一個示範電子商務網站上。我們將參考一個虛構的 URL：https://data-science-with-python-for-seo.wordlift.dev。 當呼叫 WordLift 的資料 API 時，我們只需傳入一個 URL，即可收到對應的 JSON-LD (JavaScript 物件表示法 for Linked Data)。此結構化資料通常包含電子商務網站所需的產品詳情、價格和可用性等資訊。 下方的 get json ld from url() 函式演示了此過程。它以 URL 作為輸入，並回傳以 JSON-LD 格式的結構化資料，可供注入到您的網頁中。 使用 WordLift Neural Search 生成相似產品連結 有了產品嵌入，我們現在可以利用 WordLift 的 Neural Search 功能向使用者推薦相似產品。此功能顯著提升使用者參與度，並能透過根據語義相似性展示相關產品來潛在地提升銷售額。 與傳統的關鍵字匹配不同，語義相似性會考慮產品描述的上下文和意義。這種方法允許提供更細緻、更準確的推薦，即使產品沒有相同的精確關鍵字。 我們先前定義的 get top k similar urls 函式實作了此功能。它以產品 URL 作為輸入，回傳一個按相似度分數排序的語義相似產品列表。舉例來說，如果使用者正在查看一件紅色棉質 T 恤，此功能可能會推薦其他不同顏色的棉質 T 恤，或由不同材質製成的相似風格上衣。這為使用者創造了更直觀、更吸引人的購物體驗。 透過實作這個 Neural Search 功能，我們能夠創造更個人化、更高效的購物體驗，有助於提高使用者滿意度及轉換率。 使用 LlamaIndex 建立電子商務網站的聊天機器人 🦙 我們建立的 Knowledge Graph 為建立智慧聊天機器人提供了完美的基礎。LlamaIndex（前身為 GPT Index）是一個強大的資料框架，允許我們將私有或特定領域的資料輸入、結構化並存取在大型語言模型 (LLMs) 中。透過 LlamaIndex，我們可以建立一個具有情境感知能力的聊天機器人，它能理解我們的產品目錄並有效協助客戶。 透過結合 LlamaIndex 與我們的 Knowledge Graph，我們可以開發一個能回應直接查詢的聊天機器人。這個聊天機器人將理解產品目錄，使其能夠： 1. 回答有關產品規格、供應情況和價格的問題 2. 根據客戶偏好提供個人化的產品推薦 3. 提供相似產品的比較 這種方法能帶來更自然、更有幫助的客戶互動，提升他們的購物體驗。聊天機器人可以利用我們 Knowledge Graph 中的結構化資料，使用 LlamaIndex 來有效檢索並透過 LLM 呈現相關資訊。 在後續的章節中，我們將介紹如何使用我們的 Knowledge Graph 資料設定 LlamaIndex，並建立一個能智慧協助我們電子商務客戶的聊天機器人。 安裝 LlamaIndex 和 WordLiftVectorStore 💪 設定 NomicEmbeddings 給我們的 Query Engine Nomic 發布了 v1.5 🪆🪆🪆 的 embedding model，這為文字 embedding 能力帶來了顯著的改進。Embeddings 是捕捉文字語義的數值表示，讓我們的系統能夠理解和比較查詢的內容及 documents。 Nomic v1.5 的主要功能包括： - 尺寸可變的 embeddings，維度在 64 到 768 之間 - Matryoshka learning，允許巢狀表示 - 擴展的上下文大小為 8192 tokens 我們在 WordLift 中使用 NomicEmbeddings 是因為這些進階功能，現在我們也正在設定 LlamaIndex 使用它來編碼使用者查詢。在我們的堆疊中保持 embedding model 的一致性，確保了我們的 Knowledge Graph 與查詢理解過程之間的更好對齊。 NomicEmbeddings 的更多資訊可以在 此處 找到。 前往 獲取您的免費金鑰。 我們將使用 OpenAI 作為生成回應的預設 LLM。當然也可以使用任何其他可用的 LLM。 現在讓我們使用我們 Knowledge Graph 的資料設定 WordliftVectorStore。
sourceText: Introduction This script demonstrates how to crawl a product website, extract relevant information, build an SEO-friendly Knowledge Graph (a structured representation of PDPs and PLPs), and leverage it for improved search and user experience. Key Features & Libraries: - Web scraping (Advertools) - Knowledge Graph creation for Product Detail Pages (PDPs) and Product Listing Pages (PLPs) - WordLift - Product recommendations (WordLift Neural Search) - Shopping assistant creation (WordLift + LlamaIndex 🦙) This approach enhances SEO performance and user engagement for e-commerce sites. Learn more about how it works here: - - -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- [](https://wordlift.io) by Andrea Volpini and David Riccitelli MIT License Last updated: Jul 31st, 2024 Setup Crawl the Website w/ Advertools Build the KG w/ WordLift 🕸 Run the show Let’s query products in the KG now using GraphQL Leveraging the Knowledge Graph Now that we have successfully created a Knowledge Graph for our e-commerce website, complete with product embeddings, we can take advantage of it to enhance user experience and functionality. The embeddings we’ve generated for each product allow us to perform semantic similarity searches and build more intelligent systems. Adding Structured Data to your Web Pages In this section, we will perform a simple test of WordLift’s data API. This API is used to inject structured data markup from the Knowledge Graph (KG) into your webpages. Structured data helps search engines better understand your content, potentially leading to rich snippets in search results and improved SEO. For this notebook, we’re using a pre-configured KG on a demo e-commerce website. We’ll be referencing a fictitious URL: https://data-science-with-python-for-seo.wordlift.dev. When calling WordLift’s data API, we simply pass a URL and receive the corresponding JSON-LD (JavaScript Object Notation for Linked Data). This structured data typically includes information such as product details, pricing, and availability for e-commerce sites. The get json ld from url() function below demonstrates this process. It takes a URL as input and returns the structured data in JSON-LD format, ready to be injected into your webpage. Generating Links of Similar Products using WordLift Neural Search With our product embeddings in place, we can now leverage WordLift’s Neural Search capabilities to recommend similar products to users. This feature significantly enhances user engagement and can potentially boost sales by showcasing relevant products based on semantic similarity. Unlike traditional keyword matching, semantic similarity considers the context and meaning of product descriptions. This approach allows for more nuanced and accurate recommendations, even when products don’t share exact keywords. The get top k similar urls function we’ve defined earlier implements this functionality. It takes a product URL and returns a list of semantically similar products, ranked by their similarity scores. For example, if a user is viewing a red cotton t-shirt, this feature might recommend other cotton t-shirts in different colors, or similar style tops made from different materials. This creates a more intuitive and engaging shopping experience for the user. By implementing this Neural Search feature, we’re able to create a more personalized and efficient shopping experience, potentially leading to increased user satisfaction and higher conversion rates. Building a Chatbot for the E-commerce Website using LlamaIndex 🦙 The Knowledge Graph we’ve created serves as a perfect foundation for building an intelligent chatbot. LlamaIndex (formerly GPT Index) is a powerful data framework that allows us to ingest, structure, and access private or domain-specific data in Large Language Models (LLMs). With LlamaIndex, we can create a context-aware chatbot that understands our product catalog and can assist customers effectively. By leveraging LlamaIndex in conjunction with our Knowledge Graph, we can develop a chatbot that responds to direct queries. This chatbot will have an understanding of the product catalog, enabling it to: 1. Answer questions about product specifications, availability, and pricing 2. Make personalized product recommendations based on customer preferences 3. Provide comparisons between similar products This approach leads to more natural and helpful interactions with customers, enhancing their shopping experience. The chatbot can draw upon the structured data in our Knowledge Graph, using LlamaIndex to efficiently retrieve and present relevant information through the LLM. In the following sections, we’ll walk through the process of setting up LlamaIndex with our Knowledge Graph data and creating a chatbot that can intelligently assist our e-commerce customers. Installing LlamaIndex and WordLiftVectorStore 💪 Setting NomicEmbeddings for our Query Engine Nomic has released v1.5 🪆🪆🪆 of their embedding model, which brings significant improvements to text embedding capabilities. Embeddings are numerical representations of text that capture semantic meaning, allowing our system to understand and compare the content of queries and documents. Key features of Nomic v1.5 include: - Variable-sized embeddings with dimensions between 64 and 768 - Matryoshka learning, which allows for nested representations - An expanded context size of 8192 tokens We use NomicEmbeddings in WordLift due to these advanced features, and now we’re configuring LlamaIndex to use it as well when encoding user queries. This consistency in embedding models across our stack ensures better alignment between our Knowledge Graph and the query understanding process. More information on NomicEmbeddings can be found here. Go here to get your free key. We will use OpenAI as default LLM for generating response. We could of course use any other available LLM. Let’s setup now WordliftVectorStore using data from our Knowledge Graph.

title: 記憶體
text: 概念 記憶體是 Agent 系統的核心元件，可儲存並取回過去的資訊。 在 LlamaIndex 中，你通常可以使用現有的 BaseMemory 類別自訂記憶體，或自行建立自訂實作。 Agent 執行期間會呼叫 memory.put() 儲存資訊，並呼叫 memory.get() 取回資訊。 注意： ChatMemoryBuffer 已棄用。未來版本會以 Memory 類別取代預設實作；這個類別更具彈性，也支援更複雜的記憶體設定。本節範例都會使用 Memory 類別。目前整個 framework 預設仍使用 ChatMemoryBuffer，建立基本的對話紀錄緩衝區，讓 Agent 取得符合 token 上限的最近 X 則訊息。Memory 類別的運作方式相近，但更具彈性，也能支援更複雜的記憶體設定。 使用方式 使用 Memory 類別可以建立同時包含短期記憶（也就是 FIFO 訊息佇列）與可選長期記憶（也就是隨時間擷取資訊）的記憶體。 為 Agent 設定 Memory 將記憶體傳入 run() 方法，即可為 Agent 設定記憶體： 手動管理 Memory 你也可以直接呼叫 memory.put messages() 和 memory.get()，並傳入對話紀錄，手動管理記憶體。 從 Agent 取得最新記憶 你可以從 Agent 的 context 取得最新記憶： 自訂 Memory 短期記憶 Memory 類別預設會在 token 上限內保留最近的 X 則訊息。你可以透過 token limit 和 chat history token ratio 引數傳給 Memory 類別，自訂其設定。 - token limit（預設值：30000）：短期與長期記憶可儲存的 token 數上限。 - chat history token ratio（預設值：0.7）：短期對話紀錄所占的 token 比例上限。如果對話紀錄超過這個比例，且已啟用長期記憶，最舊的訊息就會移入長期記憶。 - token flush size（預設值：3000）：對話紀錄超過 token 上限時，要移入長期記憶的 token 數。 長期記憶 長期記憶以 Memory Block 物件表示。這些物件會接收從短期記憶移出的訊息，也可以處理訊息以擷取資訊。取回記憶時，系統會合併短期與長期記憶。 目前預先定義了三種記憶區塊： - StaticMemoryBlock：儲存固定資訊的記憶區塊。 - FactExtractionMemoryBlock：從對話紀錄擷取事實的記憶區塊。 - VectorMemoryBlock：透過向量資料庫儲存及取回多批對話訊息的記憶區塊。 預設會根據 insert method 引數，將記憶區塊插入 system message 或最新的 user message。 這聽起來有點複雜，其實很簡單。來看一個範例： 這裡設定了三個記憶區塊： - core info：靜態記憶區塊，用來保存使用者的基本資訊。靜態內容可以是字串，也可以是 ContentBlock 物件清單，例如 TextBlock、ImageBlock 等。這些資訊會一直保留在記憶體中。 - extracted info：事實擷取記憶區塊，會從對話紀錄擷取資訊。這裡傳入 llm，用來從移出的對話訊息擷取事實，並將 max facts 設為 50。若擷取的事實超過上限，系統會自動摘要並縮減 max facts，為新資訊騰出空間。 - vector memory：向量記憶區塊，會透過向量資料庫儲存及取回多批對話訊息。每一批都是一組已移出的對話訊息。這裡傳入 vector store 和 embed model，用來儲存及取回訊息。 你也會看到我們為每個區塊設定了 priority。當記憶區塊內容（也就是長期記憶）加上短期記憶超過 Memory 物件的 token 上限時，系統會依此決定如何處理。 記憶區塊過長時會自動「截斷」。預設做法是先從記憶體移除內容，直到騰出足夠空間。你也可以建立子類別並實作自己的截斷邏輯。 - priority=0：此區塊永遠保留在記憶體中。 - priority=1, 2, 3, etc：記憶體超過 token 上限時，這個值決定記憶區塊的截斷順序，讓短期與長期記憶的總內容不超過 token limit。 現在把這些區塊傳入 Memory： 使用記憶體的過程中，短期記憶會逐漸填滿。超過 chat history token ratio 後，系統會將符合 token flush size 的最舊訊息移出，交由各記憶區塊處理。 取回記憶時，短期與長期記憶會合併。Memory 物件會確保兩者的總內容不超過 token limit；如果超過，就會呼叫記憶區塊的 .truncate() 方法，並依 priority 決定截斷順序。 提示 預設使用 tiktoken 計算 token 數。若要自訂計算方式，可以將 tokenizer fn 設為自訂 callable；它會接收字串並回傳清單，再以清單長度計算 token 數。 記憶體累積足夠資訊後，可能會呈現如下內容： 輸出內容會類似這樣： 此處將記憶插入 system message，並為每個記憶區塊提供專屬區段。 自訂記憶區塊 除了預先定義的記憶區塊，你也可以建立自己的自訂記憶區塊。 這裡定義了一個計算使用者提及特定名稱次數的記憶區塊。 它的 truncate 方法很簡單，只會回傳空字串。 遠端記憶體 Memory 預設使用記憶體內的 SQLite 資料庫。你可以變更 database URI，改用任何遠端資料庫。 你可以自訂資料表名稱，也可以直接傳入 async engine。這對自行管理 connection pool 很有幫助。 自訂 Chat Store 如果 SQLAlchemy 不符合你的基礎架構需求，可以實作 AsyncDBChatStore 介面，並將實作作為 chat store 傳入。SQL 專用引數（table name、async database uri、async engine、db schema）會在提供 chat store 時忽略。 Memory 與 Workflow Context 閱讀到這裡，你可能已經遇過使用 Workflow，並將 Context 物件序列化以儲存及恢復特定 Workflow 狀態的情況。Workflow 的 Context 是複合物件，包含 Workflow 的執行階段資訊，以及供不同 Workflow 步驟共用的 key/value 配對。 相較之下，Memory 物件較為精簡，只保存 ChatMessage 物件，以及可選的 MemoryBlock 清單以提供長期記憶。 在多數實際情境中，兩者會一起使用。如果你沒有自訂記憶體，序列化 Context 物件就足以保存所需狀態。 在其他情況下，例如使用 FunctionAgent、AgentWorkflow 或 ReActAgent 時，如果你自訂了記憶體，就需要將它做為獨立的 runtime argument 傳入（特別是使用超出預設設定的功能時，Memory 物件便無法序列化）。 最後，有些情況（例如人在迴圈中的流程）需要同時提供 Context（用來恢復 Workflow）與 Memory（用來保存對話紀錄）。 （已棄用）記憶體類型 在 llama index.core.memory 中，我們提供幾種不同的記憶體類型： - ChatMemoryBuffer：基本的記憶體緩衝區，會保存符合 token 上限的最近 X 則訊息。 - ChatSummaryMemoryBuffer：記憶體緩衝區，會保存符合 token 上限的最近 X 則訊息；對話變得太長時，也會定期摘要。 - VectorMemory：透過向量資料庫儲存及取回對話訊息。它不保證訊息順序，並會回傳與最新使用者訊息最相似的內容。 - SimpleComposableMemory：將多個記憶體組合在一起，通常用來搭配 VectorMemory 與 ChatMemoryBuffer 或 ChatSummaryMemoryBuffer。 範例 以下提供幾個記憶體的實際使用範例： - 記憶體 - 執行期間操作記憶體 - 使用自訂記憶體減少多輪對話混淆 注意： 以下範例已棄用： - Chat 記憶體緩衝區 - Chat 摘要記憶體緩衝區 - 可組合記憶體 - 向量記憶體 - Mem0 記憶體
sourceText: Concept Memory is a core component of agentic systems. It allows you to store and retrieve information from the past. In LlamaIndex, you can typically customize memory by using an existing BaseMemory class, or by creating a custom one. As the agent runs, it will make calls to memory.put() to store information, and memory.get() to retrieve information. NOTE: The ChatMemoryBuffer is deprecated. In a future release, the default will be replaced with the Memory class, which is more flexible and allows for more complex memory configurations. Examples in this section will use the Memory class. By default, the ChatMemoryBuffer is used across the framework, to create a basic buffer of chat history, which gives the agent the last X messages that fit into a token limit. The Memory class operates similarly, but is more flexible and allows for more complex memory configurations. Usage Using the Memory class, you can create a memory that has both short-term memory (i.e. a FIFO queue of messages) and optionally long-term memory (i.e. extracting information over time). Configuring Memory for an Agent You can set the memory for an agent by passing it into the run() method: Managing the Memory Manually You can also manage the memory manually by calling memory.put messages() and memory.get() directly, and passing in the chat history. Retrieving the Latest Memory from an Agent You can get the latest memory from an agent by grabbing it from the agent context: Customizing Memory Short-Term Memory By default, the Memory class will store the last X messages that fit into a token limit. You can customize this by passing in token limit and chat history token ratio arguments to the Memory class. - token limit (default: 30000): The maximum number of short-term and long-term tokens to store. - chat history token ratio (default: 0.7): The ratio of tokens in the short-term chat history to the total token limit. If the chat history exceeds this ratio, the oldest messages will be flushed into long-term memory (if long-term memory is enabled). - token flush size (default: 3000): The number of tokens to flush into long-term memory when the chat history exceeds the token limit. Long-Term Memory Long-term memory is represented as Memory Block objects. These objects receive the messages that are flushed from short-term memory, and optionally process them to extract information. Then when memory is retrieved, the short-term and long-term memories are merged together. Currently, there are three predefined memory blocks: - StaticMemoryBlock: A memory block that stores a static piece of information. - FactExtractionMemoryBlock: A memory block that extracts facts from the chat history. - VectorMemoryBlock: A memory block that stores and retrieves batches of chat messages from a vector database. By default, depending on the insert method argument, the memory blocks will be inserted into the system message or the latest user message. This sounds a bit complicated, but it’s actually quite simple. Let’s look at an example: Here, we’ve setup three memory blocks: - core info: A static memory block that stores some core information about the user. The static content can either be a string or a list of ContentBlock objects like TextBlock, ImageBlock, etc. This information will always be inserted into the memory. - extracted info: An extracted memory block that will extract information from the chat history. Here we’ve passed in the llm to use to extract facts from the flushed chat history, and set the max facts to 50. If the number of extracted facts exceeds this limit, the max facts will be automatically summarized and reduced to leave room for new information. - vector memory: A vector memory block that will store and retrieve batches of chat messages from a vector database. Each batch is a list of the flushed chat messages. Here we’ve passed in the vector store and embed model to use to store and retrieve the chat messages. You’ll also notice that we’ve set the priority for each block. This is used to determine the handling when the memory blocks content (i.e. long-term memory) + short-term memory exceeds the token limit on the Memory object. When memory blocks get too long, they are automatically “truncated”. By default, this just means they are removed from memory until there is room again. This can be customized with subclasses of memory blocks that implement their own truncation logic. - priority=0: This block will always be kept in memory. - priority=1, 2, 3, etc: This determines the order in which memory blocks are truncated when the memory exceeds the token limit, to help the overall short-term memory + long-term memory content be less than or equal to the token limit. Now, let’s pass these blocks into the Memory class: As the memory is used, the short-term memory will fill up. Once the short-term memory exceeds the chat history token ratio, the oldest messages that fit into the token flush size will be flushed and sent to each memory block for processing. When memory is retrieved, the short-term and long-term memories are merged together. The Memory object will ensure that the short-term memory + long-term memory content is less than or equal to the token limit. If it is longer, the .truncate() method will be called on the memory blocks, using the priority to determine the truncation order. Tip By default, tokens are counted using tiktoken. To customize this, you can set the tokenizer fn argument to a custom callable that given a string, returns a list. The length of the list is then used to determine the token count. Once the memory has collected enough information, we might see something like this from the memory: Which will print something like this: Here, the memory was inserted into the system message, with specific sections for each memory block. Customizing Memory Blocks While predefined memory blocks are available, you can also create your own custom memory blocks. Here, we’ve defined a memory block that counts the number of times a user mentions a specific name. Its truncate method is basic, just returning an empty string. Remote Memory By default, the Memory class is using an in-memory SQLite database. You can plug in any remote database by changing the database URI. You can customize the table name, and also optionally pass in an async engine directly. This is useful for managing your own connection pool. Custom Chat Store If SQLAlchemy isn’t a fit for your infrastructure, implement the AsyncDBChatStore interface and pass it as chat store. The SQL-specific arguments (table name, async database uri, async engine, db schema) are ignored when a chat store is given. Memory vs. Workflow Context At this point in the documentation, you may have encountered cases where you are using a Workflow and are serializing a Context object to save and resume a specific workflow state. The workflow Context is a complex object that holds runtime information about the workflow, as well as key/value pairs that are shared across workflow steps. In comparison, the Memory object is a simpler object, holding only ChatMessage objects, and optionally a list of MemoryBlock objects for long-term memory. In most practical cases, you will end up using both. If you aren’t customizing the memory, then serializing the Context object will be sufficient. In other cases, like when using FunctionAgent, AgentWorkflow, or ReActAgent, if you customize the memory, then you will want to provide that as a separate runtime argument (especially since beyond the default, the Memory object is not serializable). Lastly, there are cases (like human-in-the-loop) where you will need to provide both the Context (to resume the workflow) and the Memory (to store the chat history). (Deprecated) Memory Types In llama index.core.memory, we offer a few different memory types: - ChatMemoryBuffer: A basic memory buffer that stores the last X messages that fit into a token limit. - ChatSummaryMemoryBuffer: A memory buffer that stores the last X messages that fit into a token limit, and also summarizes the conversation periodically when it gets too long. - VectorMemory: A memory that stores and retrieves chat messages from a vector database. It makes no guarantees about the order of the messages, and returns the most similar messages to the latest user message. - SimpleComposableMemory: A memory that composes multiple memories together. Usually used to combine VectorMemory with ChatMemoryBuffer or ChatSummaryMemoryBuffer. Examples You can find a few examples of memory in action below: - Memory - Manipulating Memory at Runtime - Limiting Multi-Turn Confusion with Custom Memory NOTE: Deprecated examples: - Chat Memory Buffer - Chat Summary Memory Buffer - Composable Memory - Vector Memory - Mem0 Memory

title: 工具
text: 概念 完善的工具抽象是建構 LlamaIndex 代理系統的核心。定義一組工具，與設計任何 API 介面相似；不同之處在於這些工具是供 agent 呼叫，而非供人直接使用。我們支援使用者定義 Tool ，也能定義 ToolSpec ，在底層封裝一系列函式。 使用支援 function calling 的 agent 或 LLM 時，選用哪個工具及為該工具填入哪些引數，很大程度取決於工具的 名稱 與 描述 ，以及對用途和引數的說明。花時間調整這些資訊，可能會大幅影響 LLM 呼叫工具的方式。 Tool 只需實作簡單通用的介面：定義 call ，並回傳基本中繼資料（名稱、描述、函式結構描述）。 我們提供幾種不同類型的工具： - FunctionTool：讓您輕鬆將自訂函式包裝成工具。它也能自動推斷函式結構描述，或讓您自行調整各項設定。 - QueryEngineTool：包裝既有查詢引擎的工具。由於我們的 agent 抽象類別繼承自 BaseQueryEngine，這類工具也能包裝其他 agents。 - 社群貢獻的 ToolSpecs：可為單一服務（例如 Gmail）定義一個或多個工具 - 實用工具：包裝其他工具，處理工具回傳的大量資料 FunctionTool 函式工具是既有函式的簡易包裝器，同時支援同步與非同步函式！ 若要更完整地定義函式，也可以使用 Annotated 型別來指定引數說明。 預設會以函式名稱作為工具名稱，並以 docstring 作為工具描述；您也可以自行覆寫這些值。 QueryEngineTool 使用 QueryEngineTool，即可將任何查詢引擎包裝成工具： Tool 規格 我們也提供豐富的工具與工具規格（Tool Specs），作為獨立的整合套件。 您可以把工具規格想成一組搭配使用的工具，通常會涵蓋同一介面或服務（例如 Gmail）中的實用功能。 若要搭配 agent 使用，請安裝對應的工具規格整合套件： 終端機視窗 接著即可這樣使用： 完整的社群貢獻工具規格清單請參閱 GitHub 上的工具目錄。 實用工具 直接呼叫 API 往往會回傳大量資料，可能超出 LLM 的上下文視窗；即使沒有超出，也可能不必要地增加 token 用量。 為了解決這個問題，我們在工具整合套件中提供一組「實用工具」。這些工具不綁定特定服務（例如 Gmail 或 Notion），而是擴充既有工具的能力。此處的實用工具可協助處理常見模式，例如快取或建立索引，並查詢各種 API 呼叫所回傳的資料。 以下介紹兩種主要的實用工具。 OnDemandLoaderTool 這個工具會將既有的 LlamaIndex 資料載入器（BaseReader 類別）包裝成 agent 可使用的工具。呼叫時，可傳入觸發資料載入器 load data 所需的所有參數，以及自然語言查詢字串。執行時，工具會先載入資料，再建立索引（例如使用向量儲存庫），最後按需查詢；這三個步驟會在單次工具呼叫中完成。 相較於自行處理 API 資料的載入與索引，這種方式往往更方便。雖然自行處理或許有助於重複利用資料，但許多情況下，使用者只需要臨時建立索引，避免 API 回應受提示詞視窗限制。 使用範例如下： 終端機視窗 LoadAndSearchToolSpec LoadAndSearchToolSpec 接收任何既有 Tool 作為輸入。作為工具規格，它實作 to tool list；呼叫此方法時，會回傳兩個工具：load 工具和 search 工具。 執行 load 工具時，會呼叫底層 Tool，並為輸出建立索引（預設使用向量索引）。執行 search 工具時，則會接收查詢字串，並呼叫底層索引進行搜尋。 這適用於預設會回傳大量資料的 API 端點。例如，WikipediaToolSpec 預設會回傳整篇 Wikipedia 頁面，很容易超出多數 LLM 的上下文視窗。 使用範例如下： 終端機視窗 直接回傳 您會看到工具類別的建構子提供 return direct 選項。若將它設為 True，agent 的回應就會直接回傳，不再由 agent 解讀或改寫。這有助於縮短執行時間，也適合用來設計會結束 agent 推理迴圈的工具。 例如，您可以這樣指定工具： 在上例中，系統會呼叫查詢引擎工具，並將工具的回應直接作為最終結果回傳，然後結束執行迴圈。 若設為 return direct=False，agent 會參考聊天記錄中的上下文改寫回應，甚至可能再次呼叫工具。 我們也提供了使用 return direct 的範例筆記本。 偵錯工具 有時，了解實際傳送給 API 的工具定義內容，會很有幫助。 您可以呼叫底層函式取得目前的工具結構描述，查看詳細內容；OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等 API 也會使用這份結構描述。
sourceText: Concept Having proper tool abstractions is at the core of building agentic systems in LlamaIndex. Defining a set of Tools is similar to defining any API interface, with the exception that these Tools are meant for agent rather than human use. We allow users to define both a Tool as well as a ToolSpec containing a series of functions under the hood. When using an agent or LLM with function calling, the tool selected (and the arguments written for that tool) rely strongly on the tool name and description of the tools purpose and arguments. Spending time tuning these parameters can result in larges changes in how the LLM calls these tools. A Tool implements a very generic interface - simply define call and also return some basic metadata (name, description, function schema). We offer a few different types of Tools: - FunctionTool: A function tool allows users to easily convert any user-defined function into a Tool. It can also auto-infer the function schema, or let you customize various aspects. - QueryEngineTool: A tool that wraps an existing query engine. Note: since our agent abstractions inherit from BaseQueryEngine, these tools can also wrap other agents. - Community contributed ToolSpecs that define one or more tools around a single service (like Gmail) - Utility tools for wrapping other tools to handle returning large amounts of data from a tool FunctionTool A function tool is a simple wrapper around any existing function (both sync and async are supported!). For a better function definition, you can also leverage the Annotated type to specify argument descriptions. By default, the tool name will be the function name, and the docstring will be the tool description. But you can also override this. QueryEngineTool Any query engine can be turned into a tool, using QueryEngineTool: Tool Specs We also offer a rich set of Tools and Tool Specs as separate integration packages. You can think of tool specs like bundles of tools meant to be used together. Usually these cover useful tools across a single interface/service, like Gmail. To use with an agent, you can install the specific tool spec integration: Terminal window And then use it: See the tools directory on GitHub for a full list of community contributed tool specs. Utility Tools Oftentimes, directly querying an API can return a massive volume of data, which on its own may overflow the context window of the LLM (or at the very least unnecessarily increase the number of tokens that you are using). To tackle this, we’ve provided an initial set of “utility tools” in our tool integrations - utility tools are not conceptually tied to a given service (e.g. Gmail, Notion), but rather can augment the capabilities of existing Tools. In this particular case, utility tools help to abstract away common patterns of needing to cache/index and query data that’s returned from any API request. Let’s walk through our two main utility tools below. OnDemandLoaderTool This tool turns any existing LlamaIndex data loader ( BaseReader class) into a tool that an agent can use. The tool can be called with all the parameters needed to trigger load data from the data loader, along with a natural language query string. During execution, we first load data from the data loader, index it (for instance with a vector store), and then query it “on-demand”. All three of these steps happen in a single tool call. Oftentimes this can be preferable to figuring out how to load and index API data yourself. While this may allow for data reusability, oftentimes users just need an ad-hoc index to abstract away prompt window limitations for any API call. A usage example is given below: Terminal window LoadAndSearchToolSpec The LoadAndSearchToolSpec takes in any existing Tool as input. As a tool spec, it implements to tool list , and when that function is called, two tools are returned: a load tool and then a search tool. The load Tool execution would call the underlying Tool, and the index the output (by default with a vector index). The search Tool execution would take in a query string as input and call the underlying index. This is helpful for any API endpoint that will by default return large volumes of data - for instance our WikipediaToolSpec will by default return entire Wikipedia pages, which will easily overflow most LLM context windows. Example usage is shown below: Terminal window Return Direct You’ll notice the option return direct in the tool class constructor. If this is set to True, the response from an agent is returned directly, without being interpreted and rewritten by the agent. This can be helpful for decreasing runtime, or designing/specifying tools that will end the agent reasoning loop. For example, say you specify a tool: In the above example, the query engine tool would be invoked, and the response from that tool would be directly returned as the response, and the execution loop would end. If return direct=False was used, then the agent would rewrite the response using the context of the chat history, or even make another tool call. We have also provided an example notebook of using return direct. Debugging Tools Often, it can be useful to debug what exactly the tool definition is that is being sent to APIs. You can get a good peek at this by using the underlying function to get the current tool schema, which is levereged in APIs like OpenAI and Anthropic.

title: Agents
text: 在 LlamaIndex 中，我們將「agent」定義為一種特定的系統，它使用 LLM、memory 和 tools 來處理來自外部使用者的輸入。這與「agentic」一詞形成對比，後者通常指的是 agents 的超類，即任何在過程中具有 LLM 決策能力的系統。 在 LlamaIndex 中建立一個 agent 只需幾行程式碼： 呼叫這個 agent 會啟動一組特定的動作迴圈： - Agent 獲取最新的 message + chat history - tool schemas 和 chat history 會傳送給 API - Agent 會回覆直接回應，或一個 tool calls 的列表 - 每個 tool call 都會被執行 - tool call 的結果會被加入 chat history - Agent 會使用更新後的 history 再次被呼叫，並會直接回應或選擇更多呼叫 FunctionAgent 是一種 agent 的類型，它使用 LLM provider 的 function/tool calling 能力來執行 tools。其他類型的 agents，例如 ReActAgent 和 CodeActAgent，使用不同的 prompting 策略來執行 tools。 您可以造訪 the agents guide 了解更多關於 agents 及其能力。 提示 有些 model 可能不支援 streaming LLM output。雖然 streaming 預設是開啟的，但如果您遇到錯誤，您可以隨時將 FunctionAgent(..., streaming=False) 設定為禁用 streaming。 工具 Tools 可以簡單地定義為 python functions，或使用 FunctionTool 和 QueryEngineTool 等 class 進行進一步自訂。LlamaIndex 也使用名為 Tool Specs 的東西，為常見 API 提供預定義的 tools 集合。 您可以閱讀 tools 指南 以了解更多關於配置 tools 的資訊。 Memory Memory 是建構 agents 時的核心元件。預設情況下，所有 LlamaIndex agents 都使用 ChatMemoryBuffer 來處理 memory。 若要自訂，您可以將其宣告在 agent 外部並傳入： 您可以閱讀 memory guide 以了解更多關於配置 memory 的資訊。 Multi-Modal Agents 某些 LLMs 將支援多種模態，例如圖片和文字。使用帶有 content blocks 的 chat messages，我們可以將圖片傳遞給 agent 進行推理。 例如，想像您有一張 slide from this presentation 的截圖。 您可以將此圖片傳遞給 agent 進行推理，並看到它會讀取圖片並相應地採取行動。 Multi-Agent Systems 您可以將 agents 組合為一個 multi-agent 系統，其中每個 agent 都能將控制權轉移給另一個 agent 來協調完成任務。 這只是建立 multi-agent 系統的一種方法。請繼續閱讀以了解更多關於 multi-agent systems。 Manual Agents 雖然像 FunctionAgent、ReActAgent、CodeActAgent 和 AgentWorkflow 這樣的 agent classes 抽象了許多細節，但有時建立自己的低階 agents 會更理想。 直接使用 LLM 物件，您可以快速實作一個基本的 agent 迴圈，同時對 tool calling 和 error handling 的運作擁有完全的控制權。 Examples / Module Guides 您可以在 module guides page 找到更完整的範例和 module guides 列表。
sourceText: In LlamaIndex, we define an “agent” as a specific system that uses an LLM, memory, and tools, to handle inputs from outside users. Contrast this with the term “agentic”, which generally refers to a superclass of agents, which is any system with LLM decision making in the process. To create an agent in LlamaIndex, it takes only a few lines of code: Calling this agent kicks off a specific loop of actions: - Agent gets the latest message + chat history - The tool schemas and chat history get sent over the API - The Agent responds either with a direct response, or a list of tool calls - Every tool call is executed - The tool call results are added to the chat history - The Agent is invoked again with updated history, and either responds directly or selects more calls The FunctionAgent is a type of agent that uses an LLM provider’s function/tool calling capabilities to execute tools. Other types of agents, such as ReActAgent and CodeActAgent, use different prompting strategies to execute tools. You can visit the agents guide to learn more about agents and their capabilities. Tip Some models might not support streaming LLM output. While streaming is enabled by default, if you encounter an error, you can always set FunctionAgent(..., streaming=False) to disable streaming. Tools Tools can be defined simply as python functions, or further customized using classes like FunctionTool and QueryEngineTool. LlamaIndex also provides sets of pre-defined tools for common APIs using something called Tool Specs. You can read more about configuring tools in the tools guide Memory Memory is a core-component when building agents. By default, all LlamaIndex agents are using a ChatMemoryBuffer for memory. To customize it, you can declare it outside the agent and pass it in: You can read more about configuring memory in the memory guide Multi-Modal Agents Some LLMs will support multiple modalities, such as images and text. Using chat messages with content blocks, we can pass in images to an agent for reasoning. For example, imagine you had a screenshot of the slide from this presentation. You can pass this image to an agent for reasoning, and see that it reads the image and acts accordingly. Multi-Agent Systems You can combine agents into a multi-agent system, where each agent is able to hand off control to another agent to coordinate while completing tasks. This is only one way to build multi-agent systems. Read on to learn more about multi-agent systems. Manual Agents While the agent classes like FunctionAgent, ReActAgent, CodeActAgent, and AgentWorkflow abstract away a lot of details, sometimes its desirable to build your own lower-level agents. Using the LLM objects directly, you can quickly implement a basic agent loop, while having full control over how the tool calling and error handling works. Examples / Module Guides You can find a more complete list of examples and module guides in the module guides page.
