title: 端到端評估
text: End-to-End 評估應該是開發 RAG 應用程式的導向指標 —— 給定資料來源與一組查詢後，我的 workflow 是否能產生正確的回應？ 雖然在初期個別檢查查詢與回應很有幫助，但隨著處理的失敗案例與邊緣案例增加，逐一檢查每個查詢將變得不再可行。相反地，定義一組摘要指標或自動化評估會更有幫助，讓你能直覺地掌握這些指標傳達的訊息，以及哪些部分需要深入分析。 設定評估集 建議先從一組規模小但多樣化的查詢開始，並在發現有問題的查詢或互動時，逐步增加更多範例。 我們開發了一些工具，可以根據一組要查詢的 documents 自動為您產生資料集（請參閱下方範例）。 - Question Generation 未來，我們也將能針對工具自動建立資料集。 評估選項的光譜 當評估的應用程式有正確答案時，定量評估（Quantitative eval）會更有用 —— 例如：驗證在給定計畫的情況下，工具的選擇及其輸入是否正確，或檢索特定的資訊片段，或嘗試產生符合特定 schema 的中間輸出（例如 JSON 欄位）。 當產生旨在「有幫助」但未必需要完全精確的長篇回應時，定性評估（Qualitative eval）則較為適用。 評估選項存在一個光譜，範圍涵蓋指標、較便宜的模型、較昂貴的模型 (GPT4) 以及人工評估。 以下是 evaluation modules 的一些使用範例： - Batch Eval Runner - Correctness Eval - Faithfulness Eval - Guideline Eval - Pairwise Eval - Relevancy Eval - Semantic Similarity Eval 探索 - 敏感度測試 在複雜的 workflow 中，可能很難釐清流程中的哪些部分影響了結果。 敏感度測試（Sensitivity testing）是一個很好的切入點，可用於決定哪些元件需要單獨測試或更深入地調整，或者資料集中的哪些部分（例如查詢）可能產生了有問題的結果。 關於如何使用敏感度測試等方法自動發現問題的更多詳細資訊將於近期推出。 在傳統 ML 領域中，這類工具的範例包括 Giskard。 指標集成 (Metrics Ensembling) 隨著開發集規模擴大，使用 GPT-4 進行評估的成本可能會很高。 指標集成使用一組較弱的訊號（exact match, F1, ROUGE, BLEU, BERT-NLI 和 BERT-similarity）來預測更昂貴且更接近金標籤（人工標記/GPT-4）的評估方法之輸出。 其目的有二： 1. 在開發階段，能快速且低成本地在大型資料集上評估變更。 2. 在生產監控階段，標記出離群值以進行進一步評估（GPT-4 / 人工告警）。 我們也希望指標集成具有可解釋性 —— 相關性與權重分數應能指示哪些指標最能捕捉評估標準。 我們將在未來的更新中詳細討論相關方法論。
sourceText: End-to-End evaluation should be the guiding signal for your RAG application - will my workflow generate the right responses given the data sources and a set of queries? While it helps initially to individually inspect queries and responses, as you deal with more failure and corner cases, it may stop being feasible to look at each query individually, and rather it may help instead to define a set of summary metrics or automated evaluation, and gain an intuition for what they might be telling you and where you might dive deeper. Setting up an Evaluation Set It is helpful to start off with a small but diverse set of queries, and build up more examples as one discovers problematic queries or interactions. We’ve created some tools that automatically generate a dataset for you given a set of documents to query. (See example below). - Question Generation In the future, we will also be able to create datasets automatically against tools. The Spectrum of Evaluation Options Quantitative eval is more useful when evaluating applications where there is a correct answer - for instance, validating that the choice of tools and their inputs are correct given the plan, or retrieving specific pieces of information, or attempting to produce intermediate output of a certain schema (e.g. JSON fields). Qualitative eval is more useful when generating long-form responses that are meant to be helpful but not necessarily completely accurate. There is a spectrum of evaluation options ranging from metrics, cheaper models, more expensive models (GPT4), and human evaluation. Below is some example usage of the evaluation modules: - Batch Eval Runner - Correctness Eval - Faithfulness Eval - Guideline Eval - Pairwise Eval - Relevancy Eval - Semantic Similarity Eval Discovery - Sensitivity Testing With a complex workflow, it may be unclear which parts of the flow are affecting your results. Sensitivity testing can be a good inroad into choosing which components to individually test or tweak more thoroughly, or which parts of your dataset (e.g. queries) may be producing problematic results. More details on how to discover issues automatically with methods such as sensitivity testing will come soon. Examples of this in the more traditional ML domain include Giskard. Metrics Ensembling It may be expensive to use GPT-4 to carry out evaluation especially as your dev set grows large. Metrics ensembling uses an ensemble of weaker signals (exact match, F1, ROUGE, BLEU, BERT-NLI and BERT-similarity) to predict the output of a more expensive evaluation methods that are closer to the gold labels (human-labelled/GPT-4). It is intended for two purposes: 1. Evaluating changes cheaply and quickly across a large dataset during the development stage. 2. Flagging outliers for further evaluation (GPT-4 / human alerting) during the production monitoring stage. We also want the metrics ensembling to be interpretable - the correlation and weighting scores should give an indication of which metrics best capture the evaluation criteria. We will discuss more about the methodology in future updates.

title: 評估
text: 準備工作 LlamaIndex 旨在將您的資料與 LLM 應用程式連結。 有時候，即使透過查看 trace 診斷並修正了 bug，仍需要更細粒度的評估來系統性地診斷問題。 LlamaIndex 旨在提供相關工具，讓識別問題與接收有用的診斷訊號變得簡單。 與評估密切相關的概念還包括實驗（experimentation）與實驗追蹤（experiment tracking）。 通用策略 在開發 LLM 應用程式時，建議先定義端到端（end-to-end）的評估 workflow；一旦您開始收集失敗案例或邊緣案例（corner cases），並對哪些部分運作良好或不良好產生直覺後，可以再深入評估並優化特定元件。 這可以類比為軟體測試中的整合測試（integration tests）與單元測試（unit tests）。當您開始調整個別元件時，應該開始撰寫單元測試。同樣地，判斷各部分是否協作良好的金標準則是整合測試。兩者同樣重要。 - End-to-end Evaluation - Component-Wise Evaluation 以下是現有評估模組的概覽。我們將隨時間增加更多模組與支援。 - Evaluation Overview E2E 或 Component-Wise - 我該從哪個開始？ 如果您想在迭代過程中掌握系統的整體表現，將核心開發迴圈圍繞在 e2e eval 展開是合理的，將其作為整體的 sanity check 或 vibe check。 如果您對開發方向已有明確想法，並希望逐步迭代每個元件、隨進度逐步建構，則可以從 component-wise eval 開始。然而，這可能會面臨過早最佳化（premature optimization）的風險——在未評估整體應用需求的情況下就進行模型選擇或參數設定。在建立最終應用程式時，您可能需要重新審視這些選擇。 深入探討評估 評估是一個具有爭議的話題，隨著 NLP 領域的演進，評估方法也隨之改變。 在強大的基礎模型執行標記（annotation）任務已優於人類標記者的時代，評估的最佳實踐不斷在變動。先前用於啟動與評估現今模型的評估方法（例如 BLEU 或 F1），已被證明與人類判斷的相關性較低，因此需謹慎使用。 通常，以生成為主、開放式的任務，以及需要判斷或觀點的任務，由於其主觀性質，比事實性問題更難自動評估。我們將致力於提供更多指南與案例研究，說明在特定情境下應採取哪些適當的方法。 標準指標 針對標記過的資料集（無論是您自己的資料或學術基準），有幾個建議了解的標準指標： 1. Exact Match (EM)： 回答完全正確的查詢百分比。 2. Recall： 回答正確的查詢百分比，不論回傳的答案數量。 3. Precision： 回答正確的查詢百分比，除以回傳的答案數量。 4. F1： F1 分數是 precision 與 recall 的調和平均數。因此，它能透過單一指標對稱地代表 precision 與 recall，並同時考慮偽陽性（false positives）與偽陰性（false negatives）。 這篇 towardsdatascience 文章 更深入地介紹了 NDCG、MAP 和 MRR 等技術指標。 案例研究與資源 1. (課程) Data-Centric AI (MIT), 2023 2. Scale’s Approach to LLM Testing and Evaluation 3. LLM Patterns by Eugene Yan 資源 - Component-Wise Evaluation - End-to-end Evaluation
sourceText: Setting the Stage LlamaIndex is meant to connect your data to your LLM applications. Sometimes, even after diagnosing and fixing bugs by looking at traces, more fine-grained evaluation is required to systematically diagnose issues. LlamaIndex aims to provide those tools to make identifying issues and receiving useful diagnostic signals easy. Closely tied to evaluation are the concepts of experimentation and experiment tracking. General Strategy When developing your LLM application, it could help to first define an end-to-end evaluation workflow, and then once you’ve started collecting failure or corner cases and getting an intuition for what is or isn’t going well, you may dive deeper into evaluating and improving specific components. The analogy with software testing is integration tests and unit tests. You should probably start writing unit tests once you start fiddling with individual components. Equally, your gold standard on whether things are working well together are integration tests. Both are equally important. - End-to-end Evaluation - Component-Wise Evaluation Here is an overview of the existing modules for evaluation. We will be adding more modules and support over time. - Evaluation Overview E2E or Component-Wise - Which Do I Start With? If you want to get an overall idea of how your system is doing as you iterate upon it, it makes sense to start with centering your core development loop around the e2e eval - as an overall sanity/vibe check. If you have an idea of what you’re doing and want to iterate step by step on each component, building it up as things go - you may want to start with a component-wise eval. However this may run the risk of premature optimization - making model selection or parameter choices without assessing the overall application needs. You may have to revisit these choices when creating your final application. Diving Deeper into Evaluation Evaluation is a controversial topic, and as the field of NLP has evolved, so have the methods of evaluation. In a world where powerful foundation models are now performing annotation tasks better than human annotators, the best practices around evaluation are constantly changing. Previous methods of evaluation which were used to bootstrap and evaluate today’s models such as BLEU or F1 have been shown to have poor correlation with human judgements, and need to be applied prudently. Typically, generation-heavy, open-ended tasks and requiring judgement or opinion and harder to evaluate automatically than factual questions due to their subjective nature. We will aim to provide more guides and case-studies for which methods are appropriate in a given scenario. Standard Metrics Against annotated datasets, whether your own data or an academic benchmark, there are a number of standard metrics that it helps to be aware of: 1. Exact Match (EM): The percentage of queries that are answered exactly correctly. 2. Recall: The percentage of queries that are answered correctly, regardless of the number of answers returned. 3. Precision: The percentage of queries that are answered correctly, divided by the number of answers returned. 4. F1: The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. It thus symmetrically represents both precision and recall in one metric, considering both false positives and false negatives. This towardsdatascience article covers more technical metrics like NDCG, MAP and MRR in greater depth. Case Studies and Resources 1. (Course) Data-Centric AI (MIT), 2023 2. Scale’s Approach to LLM Testing and Evaluation 3. LLM Patterns by Eugene Yan Resources - Component-Wise Evaluation - End-to-end Evaluation

text: 概觀 Finetuning 模型是指透過一組資料來更新模型本身，以在多方面提升模型表現。這包括提高輸出品質、減少 hallucination、更全面地記憶資料，以及降低延遲與成本。 我們工具集的核心圍繞在 in-context learning / retrieval augmentation，這涉及在 inference 模式下使用模型，而非訓練模型本身。 雖然 finetuning 也可以用來利用外部資料來「增強」模型，但 finetuning 能在多方面補足 retrieval augmentation： Embedding Finetuning 的優勢 - Finetuning embedding 模型可以讓模型在特定的訓練資料分佈上產生更有意義的 embedding 表示 $\rightarrow$ 進而提升 retrieval 效能。 LLM Finetuning 的優勢 - 讓模型學習特定資料集的風格 - 讓模型學習在訓練資料中較少出現的 DSL（例如 SQL） - 讓模型修正難以透過 prompt engineering 解決的 hallucination 或錯誤 - 將更強大的模型（例如 GPT-4）distill 到更簡單/便宜的模型中（例如 gpt-3.5, Llama 2） 與 LlamaIndex 的整合 這是一份持續更新的指南，目前有三個與 LlamaIndex 的關鍵整合。請參閱以下章節以了解更多詳情！ - Finetuning embeddings 以提升 retrieval 效能 - Finetuning Llama 2 以提升 text-to-SQL 表現 - Finetuning gpt-3.5-turbo 以 distill gpt-4 Finetuning Embeddings 我們建立了完整的指南，向您展示如何以不同方式 finetune embeddings，無論是對非結構化文本語料庫 finetune 模型本身（在此案例中為 bge），或是針對任何 black-box embedding 使用 adapter。其步驟如下： 1. 使用 LlamaIndex 針對任何非結構化內容生成合成的問答資料集。 2. Finetuning 模型。 3. 評估模型。 Finetuning 可讓 retrieval 評估指標提升 5-10%。接著您可以透過 LlamaIndex 將此 fine-tuned 模型整合到您的 RAG 應用程式中。 - Fine-tuning an Adapter - Embedding Fine-tuning Guide - Router Fine-tuning 舊版 - Embedding Fine-tuning Repo - Embedding Fine-tuning Blog Fine-tuning LLMs Fine-tuning GPT-3.5 以 distill GPT-4 我們提供多份指南，展示如何使用 OpenAI 的 finetuning endpoints 來 fine-tune gpt-3.5-turbo，使其針對 RAG/agents 輸出 GPT-4 等級的回應。 我們使用 GPT-4 從任何非結構化內容中自動生成問題，並使用 GPT-4 query engine flow 來生成「ground-truth」答案。我們的 OpenAIFineTuningHandler callback 會自動將問答記錄到資料集中。 接著我們啟動 finetuning 任務，並獲得一個 distilled model。我們可以使用 Ragas 評估此模型，並與原生 GPT-3.5 workflow 進行基準測試。 - GPT-3.5 微調 Notebook（Colab） - GPT-3.5 微調 Notebook（Notebook 連結） - [\[WIP\] Function Calling 微調](https://developers.llamaindex.ai/python/examples/finetuning/openai fine tuning functions/index.md) 舊版 - GPT-3.5 微調 Notebook（Colab） - GPT-3.5 微調 Notebook（Repo） Fine-tuning 以提升結構化輸出品質 Fine-tuning 的另一個使用場景是讓模型更擅長輸出結構化資料。我們可以針對 OpenAI 和 Llama2 執行此操作。 - OpenAI Function Calling 微調 Fine-tuning Llama 2 以提升 Text-to-SQL 表現 在本教學中，我們將展示如何使用 text-to-SQL 資料集來 finetune Llama 2，然後利用 LlamaIndex 的抽象層，針對任何 SQL 資料庫進行結構化分析。 此技術棧包含：使用 sql-create-context 作為訓練資料集、OpenLLaMa 作為基礎模型、PEFT 進行 finetuning、Modal 提供雲端運算，以及 LlamaIndex 提供 inference 抽象層。- Llama 2 文字轉-SQL Fine-tuning (w/ Modal，Repo) - Llama 2 Text-to-SQL 微調（Modal、Notebook） Fine微調 Evaluator 在這些教學中，我們的目標是將 GPT-4 judge（或 evaluator）的知識蒸餾到 GPT-3.5 judge 中。近期研究觀察到 GPT-4 judges 與人類評估者的一致性很高（例如參閱 ）。 因此，透過 fine-tuning GPT-3.5 judge，我們或許能以更低的成本達到 GPT-4 的水準（進而與人類評估結果達成一致）。 - Finetune Correctness Judge - Finetune LLM Judge Fine-tuning Cross-Encoders 用於 Re-Ranking 透過 fine-tuning cross encoder，我們可以嘗試提升在私有資料上的 re-ranking 效能。 Re-ranking 是進階檢索的關鍵步驟，其流程是使用獨立的模型對從多個來源檢索到的 nodes 重新排序，使最相關的 nodes 排在最前面。 在本範例中，我們使用 sentence-transformers 套件來協助 fine-tune crossencoder 模型，並使用基於 QASPER 資料集產生的資料集。 - Cross-Encoder Finetuning - Finetuning Llama 2 用於 Text-to-SQL - Finetuning GPT-3.5 至 Distill GPT-4 Cohere Custom Reranker 透過使用 CohereAI 訓練 custom reranker，我們可以嘗試提升在私有資料上的 re-ranking 效能。 Re-ranking 是進階檢索流程中的關鍵步驟。此步驟使用獨立的模型來重新整理從初步檢索階段取得的 nodes，目的是確保最相關的 nodes 優先排列在最前面。 在本範例中，我們使用 cohere custom reranker 訓練模組，針對您的領域或特定資料集建立 reranker，以提升檢索效能。 - Cohere Custom Reranker
sourceText: Overview Finetuning a model means updating the model itself over a set of data to improve the model in a variety of ways. This can include improving the quality of outputs, reducing hallucinations, memorizing more data holistically, and reducing latency/cost. The core of our toolkit revolves around in-context learning / retrieval augmentation, which involves using the models in inference mode and not training the models themselves. While finetuning can be also used to “augment” a model with external data, finetuning can complement retrieval augmentation in a variety of ways: Embedding Finetuning Benefits - Finetuning the embedding model can allow for more meaningful embedding representations over a training distribution of data — leads to better retrieval performance. LLM Finetuning Benefits - Allow it to learn a style over a given dataset - Allow it to learn a DSL that might be less represented in the training data (e.g. SQL) - Allow it to correct hallucinations/errors that might be hard to fix through prompt engineering - Allow it to distill a better model (e.g. GPT-4) into a simpler/cheaper model (e.g. gpt-3.5, Llama 2) Integrations with LlamaIndex This is an evolving guide, and there are currently three key integrations with LlamaIndex. Please check out the sections below for more details! - Finetuning embeddings for better retrieval performance - Finetuning Llama 2 for better text-to-SQL - Finetuning gpt-3.5-turbo to distill gpt-4 Finetuning Embeddings We’ve created comprehensive guides showing you how to finetune embeddings in different ways, whether that’s the model itself (in this case, bge) over an unstructured text corpus, or an adapter over any black-box embedding. It consists of the following steps: 1. Generating a synthetic question/answer dataset using LlamaIndex over any unstructured context. 2. Finetuning the model 3. Evaluating the model. Finetuning gives you a 5-10% increase in retrieval evaluation metrics. You can then plug this fine-tuned model into your RAG application with LlamaIndex. - Fine-tuning an Adapter - Embedding Fine-tuning Guide - Router Fine-tuning Old - Embedding Fine-tuning Repo - Embedding Fine-tuning Blog Fine-tuning LLMs Fine-tuning GPT-3.5 to distill GPT-4 We have multiple guides showing how to use OpenAI’s finetuning endpoints to fine-tune gpt-3.5-turbo to output GPT-4 responses for RAG/agents. We use GPT-4 to automatically generate questions from any unstructured context, and use a GPT-4 query engine flow to generate “ground-truth” answers. Our OpenAIFineTuningHandler callback automatically logs questions/answers to a dataset. We then launch a finetuning job, and get back a distilled model. We can evaluate this model with Ragas to benchmark against a naive GPT-3.5 workflow. - GPT-3.5 Fine-tuning Notebook (Colab) - GPT-3.5 Fine-tuning Notebook (Notebook link) - [\[WIP\] Function Calling Fine-tuning](/python/examples/finetuning/openai fine tuning functions/index.md) Old - GPT-3.5 Fine-tuning Notebook (Colab) - GPT-3.5 Fine-tuning Notebook (in Repo) Fine-tuning for Better Structured Outputs Another use case for fine-tuning is to make the model better at outputting structured data. We can do this for both OpenAI and Llama2. - OpenAI Function Calling Fine-tuning Fine-tuning Llama 2 for Better Text-to-SQL In this tutorial, we show you how you can finetune Llama 2 on a text-to-SQL dataset, and then use it for structured analytics against any SQL database using LlamaIndex abstractions. The stack includes sql-create-context as the training dataset, OpenLLaMa as the base model, PEFT for finetuning, Modal for cloud compute, LlamaIndex for inference abstractions. - Llama 2 Text-to-SQL Fine-tuning (w/ Modal, Repo) - Llama 2 Text-to-SQL Fine-tuning (w/ Modal, Notebook) Fine-tuning An Evaluator In these tutorials, we aim to distill a GPT-4 judge (or evaluator) onto a GPT-3.5 judge. It has been recently observed that GPT-4 judges can reach high levels of agreement with human evaluators (e.g., see ). Thus, by fine-tuning a GPT-3.5 judge, we may be able to reach GPT-4 levels (and by proxy, agreement with humans) at a lower cost. - Finetune Correctness Judge - Finetune LLM Judge Fine-tuning Cross-Encoders for Re-Ranking By finetuning a cross encoder, we can attempt to improve re-ranking performance on our own private data. Re-ranking is key step in advanced retrieval, where retrieved nodes from many sources are re-ranked using a separate model, so that the most relevant nodes are first. In this example, we use the sentence-transformers package to help finetune a crossencoder model, using a dataset that is generated based on the QASPER dataset. - Cross-Encoder Finetuning - Finetuning Llama 2 for Text-to-SQL - Finetuning GPT-3.5 to Distill GPT-4 Cohere Custom Reranker By training a custom reranker with CohereAI, we can attempt to improve re-ranking performance on our own private data. Re-ranking is a crucial step in advanced retrieval processes. This step involves using a separate model to re-organize nodes retrieved from initial retrieval phase. The goal is to ensure that the most relevant nodes are prioritized and appear first. In this example, we use the cohere custom reranker training module to create a reranker on your domain or specific dataset to improve retrieval performance. - Cohere Custom Reranker

title: 建構適用於正式環境的高效能 RAG 應用程式
sourceTitle: Building Performant RAG Applications for Production
text: 開發 RAG 應用程式的原型很簡單，但要使其高效、強健且能擴展至大型知識庫則相當困難。 本指南包含多項技巧，旨在提升您的 RAG workflow 效能。我們首先概述一些通用技術，並大致按照從簡單到複雜的順序排列。接著，我們將深入探討每項技術、其解決的應用場景，以及如何使用 LlamaIndex 實作！ 最終目標是優化您的檢索與生成效能，以便在更複雜的資料集上更準確地回答更多查詢，且不產生幻覺。 建構生產級 RAG 的通用技術 以下是建構生產級 RAG 的一些核心考量： - 將用於檢索的 chunks 與用於合成的 chunks 解耦 - 針對較大型 Document 集的結構化檢索 - 根據任務動態檢索 chunks - 對檢索到的 nodes 進行 Reranking 以提升精準度 - 優化 context embeddings 我們在 Production RAG Webinar 中討論了這些內容及更多細節。請參閱 此 Tweet 執行緒 以獲取更多彙整資訊。 將用於檢索的 chunks 與用於合成的 chunks 解耦 提升檢索品質的一項關鍵技術，是將用於檢索的 chunks 與用於合成的 chunks 進行解耦。 動機 用於檢索的最佳 chunk 表示方式，可能與用於合成的最佳考量不同。例如，原始文字 chunk 可能包含 LLM 在針對查詢合成詳細答案時所需的細節；然而，它可能包含填充詞或資訊，進而影響 embedding 的表示，或者因為缺乏全域上下文，導致在收到相關查詢時完全無法被檢索到。 關鍵技術 利用此概念主要有兩種方式： 1. 對 document 摘要進行 Embedding，並將其連結至與該 document 相關的 chunks。 這有助於在檢索 chunks 之前，先在高層級檢索相關的 documents，而非直接檢索 chunks（後者可能會落在不相關的 documents 中）。 資源： - Table Recursive Retrieval - Document Summary Index 2. 對句子進行 Embedding，然後將其連結至該句子周圍的視窗（window）。 這允許對相關上下文進行更細粒度的檢索（Embedding 過大的 chunks 會導致「lost in the middle」問題），同時也能確保 LLM 合成時有足夠的上下文。 資源： - Metadata Replacement Postprocessor 針對較大型 Document 集的結構化檢索 動機 標準 RAG 堆疊（top-k 檢索 + 基礎文字分割）的一個大問題是，當 documents 的數量增加時（例如您有 100 份不同的 PDF），效能會下降。在這種情況下，針對特定查詢，您可能希望利用結構化資訊來協助更精準的檢索；例如，如果您提出的問題僅與兩份 PDF 相關，可以使用結構化資訊來確保這兩份 PDF 被回傳，而非僅依賴 chunks 的原始 embedding 相似度。 關鍵技術 針對生產級 RAG 系統，有幾種執行結構化標記/檢索的方法，每種方法各有優缺點。 1. Metadata Filters + Auto Retrieval 為每個 document 加上 metadata 並儲存在向量資料庫中。在推論時，利用 LLM 推論出正確的 metadata filters，除了語義查詢字串外，同步對向量資料庫進行查詢。 - 優點 ✅：主流向量資料庫均支援。可透過多個維度過濾 document。 - 缺點 🚫：定義正確的標記可能較困難。標記可能不包含足夠的相關資訊以實現更精準的檢索。此外，標記代表的是 document 層級的關鍵字搜尋，不支援語義查找。Resources: 2. Store Document Hierarchies (summaries - raw chunks) + Recursive Retrieval Embed document summaries and map to chunks per document。先在 document 層級進行 Fetch，接著再進入 chunk 層級。 - Pros ✅: 允許在 document 層級進行 semantic lookups。 - Cons 🚫: 不支援透過 structured tags 進行 keyword lookups（這比 semantic search 更精確）。此外，自動產生 summaries 的成本可能較高。 Resources - Chroma Auto-Retrieval - Document Summary Index - Auto-Retriever vs. Recursive Retriever Dynamically Retrieve Chunks Depending 於您的 Task Motivation RAG 不僅僅是針對特定事實進行問答（這是 top-k similarity 所優化的方向）。使用者可能會提出各種不同的查詢。由簡單的 RAG stack 處理的查詢包括詢問特定事實，例如「告訴我這家公司 2023 年的 D\&I 計劃」或「敘述者在 Google 工作期間做了什麼」。但查詢也可能包含摘要，例如「你能給我這個 document 的高階概觀嗎」，或是比較，「你能比較/對比 X 和 Y 嗎」。所有這些使用情境可能需要不同的 retrieval 技術。 關鍵技術 LlamaIndex 提供了一些核心抽象概念來協助您進行特定任務的 retrieval。這包括我們的 router 模組以及 data agent 模組。此外還包括一些進階的 query engine 模組，以及其他將 structured 與 unstructured 資料結合的模組。 您可以使用這些模組來同時進行問答與摘要，甚至將 structured queries 與 unstructured queries 結合使用。 Core Module Resources - Query engine - Agents - Router Detailed Guide Resources - Sub-Question Query Engine - Joint QA-Summary - Router Query Engine - OpenAI Agent Cookbook Reranking Retrieved Nodes for Precision Motivation Dense retrievers 和 hybrid retrievers 是為了 recall 而調校的；它們會回傳在語義上與查詢接近的候選結果，但 top-1 不一定是最相關的。在生產環境中，這會表現為「retrieval 看起來沒錯，但模型回答的問題仍然錯誤」。Reranker 透過對 top-k 候選結果執行更強大但較慢的模型，並在將其傳送到 LLM 之前重新排序，來解決這個問題。 關鍵技術 Retrieve 一組較寬的候選集（例如 similarity top k=10-20），然後 rerank 到較小的 top n (3–5)。選項依成本排序如下： 1. 透過 SentenceTransformerRerank 使用 Local cross-encoder，這是建議的預設選項。不需要 API key，且運行在與 embeddings 相同的基礎設施上。為了速度可使用 cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2，若需要更強的多國語言品質則使用 Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B。 2. Hosted reranker APIs：CohereRerank, JinaRerank, VoyageAIRerank, MixedbreadAIRerank。配置簡單，無需管理基礎設施，但會增加單次查詢的延遲與成本。 3. LLM-as-reranker：LLMRerank, RankGPTRerank, RankLLMRerank。品質最強，成本最高。僅限於準確度優先於成本的生產流程。 請參閱 rerankers overview 查看決策樹，以及 node postprocessors guide 查看完整的整合清單。 Optimize Context Embeddings Motivation 這與上述「將用於 retrieval 與 synthesis 的 chunks 解耦」的動機相關。我們希望確保 embeddings 已針對您的特定資料集進行優化，以實現更好的 retrieval。預訓練模型可能無法捕捉到與您的使用情境相關的關鍵資料特性。 Key Techniques除了上述部分技巧外，我們也可以嘗試對 embedding model 進行微調。事實上，我們可以使用無標記的方式，在非結構化文本語料庫上完成此操作。 請參閱我們的指南： - Embedding 微調指南
sourceText: Prototyping a RAG application is easy, but making it performant, robust, and scalable to a large knowledge corpus is hard. This guide contains a variety of tips and tricks to improve the performance of your RAG workflow. We first outline some general techniques - they are loosely ordered in terms of most straightforward to most challenging. We then dive a bit more deeply into each technique, the use cases that it solves, and how to implement it with LlamaIndex! The end goal is to optimize your retrieval and generation performance to answer more queries over more complex datasets accurately and without hallucinations. General Techniques for Building Production-Grade RAG Here are some top Considerations for Building Production-Grade RAG - Decoupling chunks used for retrieval vs. chunks used for synthesis - Structured Retrieval for Larger Document Sets - Dynamically Retrieve Chunks Depending on your Task - Reranking retrieved nodes for precision - Optimize context embeddings We discussed this and more during our Production RAG Webinar. Check out this Tweet thread for more synthesized details. Decoupling Chunks Used for Retrieval vs. Chunks Used for Synthesis A key technique for better retrieval is to decouple chunks used for retrieval with those that are used for synthesis. Motivation The optimal chunk representation for retrieval might be different than the optimal consideration used for synthesis. For instance, a raw text chunk may contain needed details for the LLM to synthesize a more detailed answer given a query. However, it may contain filler words/info that may bias the embedding representation, or it may lack global context and not be retrieved at all when a relevant query comes in. Key Techniques There’s two main ways to take advantage of this idea: 1. Embed a document summary, which links to chunks associated with the document. This can help retrieve relevant documents at a high-level before retrieving chunks vs. retrieving chunks directly (that might be in irrelevant documents). Resources: - Table Recursive Retrieval - Document Summary Index 2. Embed a sentence, which then links to a window around the sentence. This allows for finer-grained retrieval of relevant context (embedding giant chunks leads to “lost in the middle” problems), but also ensures enough context for LLM synthesis. Resources: - Metadata Replacement Postprocessor Structured Retrieval for Larger Document Sets Motivation A big issue with the standard RAG stack (top-k retrieval + basic text splitting) is that it doesn’t do well as the number of documents scales up - e.g. if you have 100 different PDFs. In this setting, given a query you may want to use structured information to help with more precise retrieval; for instance, if you ask a question that’s only relevant to two PDFs, using structured information to ensure those two PDFs get returned beyond raw embedding similarity with chunks. Key Techniques There’s a few ways of performing more structured tagging/retrieval for production-quality RAG systems, each with their own pros/cons. 1. Metadata Filters + Auto Retrieval Tag each document with metadata and then store in a vector database. During inference time, use the LLM to infer the right metadata filters to query the vector db in addition to the semantic query string. - Pros ✅: Supported in major vector dbs. Can filter document via multiple dimensions. - Cons 🚫: Can be hard to define the right tags. Tags may not contain enough relevant information for more precise retrieval. Also tags represent keyword search at the document-level, doesn’t allow for semantic lookups. Resources: 2. Store Document Hierarchies (summaries - raw chunks) + Recursive Retrieval Embed document summaries and map to chunks per document. Fetch at the document-level first before chunk level. - Pros ✅: Allows for semantic lookups at the document level. - Cons 🚫: Doesn’t allow for keyword lookups by structured tags (can be more precise than semantic search). Also autogenerating summaries can be expensive. Resources - Chroma Auto-Retrieval - Document Summary Index - Auto-Retriever vs. Recursive Retriever Dynamically Retrieve Chunks Depending on your Task Motivation RAG isn’t just about question-answering about specific facts, which top-k similarity is optimized for. There can be a broad range of queries that a user might ask. Queries that are handled by naive RAG stacks include ones that ask about specific facts e.g. “Tell me about the D\&I initiatives for this company in 2023” or “What did the narrator do during his time at Google”. But queries can also include summarization e.g. “Can you give me a high-level overview of this document”, or comparisons “Can you compare/contrast X and Y”. All of these use cases may require different retrieval techniques. Key Techniques LlamaIndex provides some core abstractions to help you do task-specific retrieval. This includes our router module as well as our data agent module. This also includes some advanced query engine modules. This also include other modules that join structured and unstructured data. You can use these modules to do joint question-answering and summarization, or even combine structured queries with unstructured queries. Core Module Resources - Query engine - Agents - Router Detailed Guide Resources - Sub-Question Query Engine - Joint QA-Summary - Router Query Engine - OpenAI Agent Cookbook Reranking Retrieved Nodes for Precision Motivation Dense retrievers and hybrid retrievers are tuned for recall; they’ll return candidates that are semantically close to the query, but the top-1 isn’t always the most relevant. In production, this shows up as “the retrieval looks right, but the model is still answering the wrong question.” A reranker addresses this by running a stronger, slower model over the top-k candidates and reordering them before they reach the LLM. Key Techniques Retrieve a wider candidate set (e.g. similarity top k=10-20) and rerank down to a smaller top n (3–5). Options, in order of cost: 1. Local cross-encoder via SentenceTransformerRerank, the recommended default. No API key, runs on the same infra as your embeddings. Use a model like cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 for speed or Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B for stronger multilingual quality. 2. Hosted reranker APIs: CohereRerank, JinaRerank, VoyageAIRerank, MixedbreadAIRerank. Simple to wire up, no infra to manage, adds per-query latency and cost. 3. LLM-as-reranker: LLMRerank, RankGPTRerank, RankLLMRerank. Strongest quality, most expensive. Reserve for production flows where accuracy dominates cost. See the rerankers overview for a decision tree and the node postprocessors guide for the full list of integrations. Optimize Context Embeddings Motivation This is related to the motivation described above in “decoupling chunks used for retrieval vs. synthesis”. We want to make sure that the embeddings are optimized for better retrieval over your specific data corpus. Pre-trained models may not capture the salient properties of the data relevant to your use case. Key Techniques Beyond some of the techniques listed above, we can also try finetuning the embedding model. We can actually do this over an unstructured text corpus, in a label-free way. Check out our guides here: - Embedding Fine-tuning Guide

title: RAG 故障模式檢查清單
text: 當您的 RAG pipeline 表現不如預期時，很難精確找出根本原因。本檢查清單涵蓋了最常見的失效模式、其症狀以及能讓您恢復正常運作的最小修復方案。 前九個章節側重於單次查詢的行為（檢索、chunking、embeddings、query formulation 以及 synthesis）。後續章節則強調在較大規模或長時間運行的部署中才會出現的系統級問題。 1. 檢索幻覺 發生情況： retriever 回傳的 chunks 看起來相關，但實際上並不包含答案。接著 LLM 會根據不相關的上下文「幻覺」出一個聽起來合理的回答。 症狀： - 回答聽起來很有信心，但事實錯誤 - 檢索到的 chunks 與 query 共享關鍵字，但討論的是不同主題 - 不相關的段落具有高 similarity scores 修復方案： - 加入 reranker （例如 CohereRerank, SentenceTransformerRerank）在初步檢索後過濾掉 false positives - 增加 similarity top k 並讓 reranker 進行剪枝，而非僅依賴向量資料庫的小 top-k - 使用 hybrid search （結合向量 + 關鍵字檢索）以減少語義上的誤匹配 - 透過 node postprocessors 加入 relevance threshold 以捨棄低信心度的 chunks 2. 選到錯誤的文字區塊（分塊方式不佳） 發生情況： 您的 documents 切分方式將關鍵上下文分散在多個 chunks 中，導致沒有單一 chunk 擁有足夠資訊來回答 query。 症狀： - 回答部分缺失或不完整 - 正確資訊存在於您的 corpus 中，但檢索到的 chunks 未能完整包含 - 當您手動提供正確文本時，回答品質大幅提升 修復方案： - 嘗試調整 chunk size and overlap （例如使用 1024+ tokens 的較大 chunks 並搭配 10–20% 的 overlap） - 使用 SentenceSplitter 取代單純的固定大小切分，以保留句子邊界 - 嘗試使用 HierarchicalNodeParser 進行 hierarchical chunking ，以同時捕捉細粒度與廣泛的上下文 - 考慮使用 SentenceWindowNodeParser 檢索單一句子，但利用周圍上下文進行 synthesis 3. 索引碎片化 發生情況： 您的 index 包含重複、過時或衝突的 documents 版本，導致檢索結果不一致或相互矛盾。 症狀： - 同一個問題在不同次執行時得到不同答案 - 檢索到的 chunks 中包含矛盾資訊 - 即使更新了來源 documents，仍會出現舊資料 修復方案： - 實作一套搭配 doc id 追蹤的 document management 策略，並使用 index.refresh ref docs() 更新變更過的 documents - 使用 IngestionPipeline 搭配 docstore 在索引前對 documents 進行去重 - 定期從來源重新構建 index，而非僅僅是 append - 加入 metadata（時間戳記、版本號），並在適用時根據 recency 進行過濾 4. 設定偏移（Embedding 不匹配） 發生情況： 查詢時使用的 embedding model 與索引時使用的不同，或者在索引與查詢之間變更了如 chunk size 等 settings。 症狀： - 程式碼變更或 dependency 更新後，檢索品質突然下降 - 所有查詢的 similarity scores 異常低 - 先前可正常運作的查詢現在回傳不相關結果 修復方案： - 將 embedding model 名稱與 index 一併儲存，並記錄在 metadata 或 config 中 - 固定 embedding model 版本（例如 text-embedding-3-small 或特定的 sentence-transformers model revision） - 如果變更了 embedding model，必須重新構建整個 index，因為 embeddings 無法混用 - 在索引與查詢的程式路徑中一致地使用 Settings.embed model 5. Embedding 模型不匹配（模型不適合使用領域） 發生情況： embedding model 無法理解您領域的術語，導致領域特定查詢的語義相似度表現不佳。 症狀： - 通用知識問題結果良好，但領域特定問題結果不佳 - 您領域中的同義詞或 jargon 無法被有效匹配- 在您的資料集上，關鍵字搜尋的表現優於向量搜尋 解決方案： - 嘗試使用 domain-adapted embedding model （例如針對法律、醫療或程式碼微調的模型） - 將向量搜尋與 關鍵字搜尋 結合（混合模式），以捕捉精確的術語匹配 - 從您的語料庫生成合成 QA 對，並在部署前評估 embedding recall 6. 超出 Context window 發生原因： 檢索到的 chunk 過多，被塞入 LLM 的 prompt 中，導致超過 context window 或因雜訊過多而稀釋了有效訊號。 症狀： - 回答被截斷或中斷 - 出現關於 token 限制的 API 錯誤 - 回答忽略了相關的檢索內容（尤其是位於 context 開頭或中間的內容） - 隨著 similarity top k 增加，品質下降 解決方案： - 使用如 TreeSummarize 或 Refine 的 response synthesizer 代替 CompactAndRefine 以處理大量 context - 減少 similarity top k，並依賴 reranking 僅呈現最相關的 chunk - 設定明確的 max tokens 限制，並使用 callback manager 監控 token 數量 - 考慮使用 summary index 或 recursive retrieval 在 synthesis 前壓縮 context 7. 缺少 Metadata 篩選 發生原因： retriever 在所有 documents 中進行搜尋，但實際上應該將範圍限制在特定子集（例如特定的日期範圍、部門或 document 類型）。 症狀： - 回答從錯誤的 documents 中提取（例如使用者詢問今年，卻抓到去年的報告） - 不同 document 類別之間發生交叉污染 - 使用者回報「系統知道太多」或回傳不相關的內容 解決方案： - 在 ingestion 期間加入結構化 metadata （日期、來源、類別、作者） - 在查詢時使用 MetadataFilters 來限制檢索範圍 - 實作 auto-retrieval ，由 LLM 從使用者查詢中提取篩選參數 - 為邏輯上不同的 document 集合使用獨立的 index 或 namespace 8. 未正確理解查詢 發生原因： 使用者的查詢含糊不清、太短，或其措辭與 documents 中儲存資訊的方式不同。 症狀： - 僅僅對查詢進行簡單的改寫，結果就大幅改變 - 短查詢（一兩個單字）的回傳結果不佳 - 使用者必須「知道正確的關鍵字」才能獲得好的答案 解決方案： - 加入 query transformation 步驟，並使用 HyDEQueryTransform 生成假設性答案來進行搜尋 - 使用 SubQuestionQueryEngine 將複雜查詢分解為較簡單的子查詢 - 使用 LLM 實作 query rewriting 以擴展或改寫查詢 - 加入包含範例查詢的 few-shot prompt 以引導使用者 9. LLM 回答合成失敗 發生原因： retriever 檢索到了正確的 chunk，但 LLM 無法從中合成出良好的答案。 症狀： - 檢索到的 chunk 是正確的（經人工驗證），但答案仍然錯誤 - LLM 忽略提供的 context，而是根據其訓練資料回答 - 儘管有具體的 context 可用，答案卻過於籠統 解決方案： - 使用更強大的 LLM 進行 synthesis（例如使用 GPT-4o 代替 GPT-4o-mini）或微調 temperature - 自定義 QA prompt template ，明確指示 LLM 僅使用提供的 context - 使用 Refine 回應模式，依序處理每個 chunk 而非一次處理全部 - 加入 system prompt，強調 LLM 應僅根據 context 回答 10. Embedding 相似度指標不匹配（Cosine score 不等於實際語意） 發生原因： 用於相似度計算的距離指標或正規化方式，與資料中意義的分布不一致。過長或過於籠統的 chunk 會主導相似度分數，而真正相關的片段在排名中較低。 症狀： - Top-1 的結果明顯錯誤，但相關的 documents 出現在 top-k 列表的較後方- 相關與不相關 chunk 的 similarity scores 過於接近 - 在 documents 中加入通用的 boilerplate text 對 retrieval 行為產生的影響超出預期 - 手動檢查顯示 retrieval 品質對微小的 preprocessing 變更非常敏感 修正方法： - 檢查完整的 top-k 列表，確認相關 chunk 是否有出現但排名過低 - 正規化或修剪過長的 chunk，避免少數巨大的 nodes 主導 similarity - 考慮加入 reranking 階段，使用與基礎 vector store 不同的 scoring function - 在部署前使用標記過的 query 評估 retrieval（在小型測試集上計算 precision / recall），並根據結果調整 similarity top k 與 thresholds 11. Session 與快取記憶中斷 發生情況： 使用者期望系統能記得之前的互動或設定，但底層的 indices、vector stores 或 caches 是 stateless 的，或是 key 設定錯誤。即便資料存在，不同 session 之間的 retrieval 結果仍顯得不穩定。 症狀： - 在不同日期詢問相同問題，回傳的 documents 子集不同 - 在 redeploy 或清除 cache 後，先前穩定的 query 開始出現偏差 - 使用相同 query 手動請求 vector store 時，有時會回傳空結果或結果集大幅縮小 修正方法： - 為 session 與 user keys 定義明確的策略，並確保它們一致地傳遞至應用程式、retrievers 與 stores 中 - 將長期知識與短期暫存空間分開，避免 cache eviction 刪除關鍵資料 - 針對有問題的請求記錄 index versions、cache keys 與 retrieval parameters，並跨 session 進行比較 - 加入 regression test，在每次 deploy 後重播一段短對話或 query 序列以驗證穩定性 12. 可觀測性缺口（黑箱除錯） 發生情況： 你知道答案錯誤，但無法得知 retriever 或 LLM 實際上做了什麼。缺乏基礎的 traces 會導致無法判斷問題出在 retrieval、synthesis 還是 deployment。 症狀： - Bug 回報為「有時回答很奇怪」，但缺乏可重現的 traces - 無法輕鬆檢查針對某個錯誤答案所 retrieval 的 nodes - 未記錄 token counts、prompts 與 index metadata，導致無法重建 production 的執行過程 修正方法： - 為 retrieval、query transforms、prompts 與 responses 開啟 tracing 與 logging（可透過 LlamaIndex callbacks 或自有的 logging stack） - 針對每個錯誤答案，至少擷取：使用者 query、retrieved nodes、similarity scores、index 或 snapshot identifiers，以及最終的 LLM prompt - 在應用程式中加入「debug mode」，將 retrieval 結果與決策印出或儲存以供手動檢查 - 在變更基礎設施前，嘗試僅利用 logs 與 traces 重現失敗；若無法重現，請先提升可觀測性 13. 索引生命週期與部署順序 發生情況： Pipeline 在本地測試正常，但 production 行為隨機，因為 indices 為空、僅部分建立，或與執行中的設定不一致。服務啟動順序錯誤，或指向錯誤的儲存空間。 症狀： - 部署後立即發現部分 query 回傳明顯不完整或空的答案 - Logs 顯示 vector store 包含的 nodes 遠少於預期 - 變更環境變數或 secrets 時，悄悄切換了 query 時使用的 index 或 embedding settings - 在沒有任何程式碼變更的情況下，rollback 或 redeploy 會再次改變答案 修正方法： - 將 index 視為版本化的 artifact，並在 ingestion 與 serving 路徑中追蹤 index version 或 snapshot id - 加入 health check，在 deploy 後執行一個已知正確的 query；若 index 為空、低於最小尺寸或使用錯誤的 embedding config 則判定失敗 - 確保 ingestion 或 refresh jobs 完成後，才將 production traffic 導向新 index - 避免手動執行一次性的 ingestion 步驟；將其編寫成 scripts 或 pipelines 以防止意外遺漏 快速診斷流程圖 請參考此流程以縮小問題範圍： 1. 優先檢查 retrieval： 印出檢索到的 nodes 並手動確認其是否包含答案。 - 若 檢索到的 nodes 錯誤 $\rightarrow$ 請重點檢查上述項目 1–5、7–8。 - 若 檢索到的 nodes 正確 $\rightarrow$ 請重點檢查上述項目 6、9。 2. 測試已知正確的 query： 嘗試一個您明確知道答案位於哪個 document 的 query。 - 若 失敗 $\rightarrow$ 可能是 indexing 或 embedding 問題（項目 3–5、10、13）。 - 若 成功 $\rightarrow$ 問題與特定 query 有關（項目 1、7–8、11）。 3. 檢查 token 數量： 記錄傳送到 LLM 的總 token 數。 - 若 接近上限 $\rightarrow$ Context window 溢位（項目 6）。 - 若 遠低於上限 $\rightarrow$ Synthesis 或 retrieval 品質問題（項目 1–5、8–10、12）。 4. 若問題僅出現在 production 或部署後： - 請重點檢查系統層級問題（項目 11–13），並驗證 index 版本、快取與 trace。 延伸閱讀 - Building Performant RAG Applications for Production - Building RAG from Scratch - Evaluation Guide 本文提及的主要 LlamaIndex 類別 - SentenceSplitter - HierarchicalNodeParser - SentenceWindowNodeParser - CohereRerank - SentenceTransformerRerank - HyDEQueryTransform - SubQuestionQueryEngine - IngestionPipeline - MetadataFilters
sourceText: When your RAG pipeline isn’t performing as expected, it can be difficult to pinpoint the root cause. This checklist covers the most common failure modes, their symptoms, and minimal fixes to get you back on track. The first nine sections focus on single-query behavior (retrieval, chunking, embeddings, query formulation, and synthesis). The later sections highlight system-level issues that often show up only in larger or longer-running deployments. 1. Retrieval Hallucination What happens: The retriever returns chunks that look superficially relevant but don’t actually contain the answer. The LLM then “hallucinates” a plausible-sounding response from irrelevant context. Symptoms: - Answers sound confident but are factually wrong - Retrieved chunks share keywords with the query but discuss a different topic - High similarity scores on irrelevant passages Fixes: - Add a reranker (e.g., CohereRerank, SentenceTransformerRerank) to filter out false positives after initial retrieval - Increase similarity top k and let the reranker prune, rather than relying on a small top-k from the vector store alone - Use hybrid search (combining vector + keyword retrieval) to reduce semantic false matches - Add a relevance threshold via node postprocessors to discard low-confidence chunks 2. Wrong Chunk Selection (Poor Chunking) What happens: Your documents are split in a way that separates critical context across multiple chunks, so no single chunk has enough information to answer the query. Symptoms: - Partial or incomplete answers - The correct information exists in your corpus but the retrieved chunks don’t contain it fully - Answers improve dramatically when you manually provide the right text Fixes: - Experiment with chunk size and overlap (for example, larger chunks such as 1024+ tokens with 10–20% overlap) - Use SentenceSplitter instead of naive fixed-size splitting to preserve sentence boundaries - Try hierarchical chunking with HierarchicalNodeParser to capture both fine-grained and broad context - Consider SentenceWindowNodeParser to retrieve a sentence but synthesize with surrounding context 3. Index Fragmentation What happens: Your index contains duplicate, outdated, or conflicting versions of documents, leading to inconsistent or contradictory retrieval results. Symptoms: - Different answers for the same question across runs - Contradictory information in retrieved chunks - Stale data appearing even after you’ve updated source documents Fixes: - Implement a document management strategy with doc id tracking and use index.refresh ref docs() to update changed documents - Use IngestionPipeline with a docstore to deduplicate documents before indexing - Periodically rebuild your index from source rather than only appending - Add metadata (timestamps, version numbers) and filter on recency when relevant 4. Config Drift (Embedding Mismatch) What happens: The embedding model used at query time differs from the one used at index time, or settings like chunk size changed between indexing and querying. Symptoms: - Sudden drop in retrieval quality after a code change or dependency update - Similarity scores are abnormally low across all queries - Previously working queries now return irrelevant results Fixes: - Store your embedding model name alongside your index and log it in metadata or config - Pin your embedding model version (for example, text-embedding-3-small or a specific sentence-transformers model revision) - If you change the embedding model, rebuild the entire index since you cannot mix embeddings - Use Settings.embed model consistently in both indexing and querying code paths 5. Embedding Model Mismatch (Wrong Model for the Domain) What happens: The embedding model doesn’t understand your domain’s terminology, leading to poor semantic similarity for domain-specific queries. Symptoms: - Good results on general-knowledge questions but poor results on domain-specific ones - Synonyms or jargon in your domain are not matched well - Keyword search outperforms vector search on your dataset Fixes: - Try a domain-adapted embedding model (for example, fine-tuned models for legal, medical, or code) - Combine vector search with keyword search (hybrid mode) to capture exact terminology matches - Generate synthetic QA pairs from your corpus and evaluate embedding recall before deploying 6. Context Window Overflow What happens: Too many retrieved chunks are stuffed into the LLM’s prompt, exceeding the context window or diluting the signal with noise. Symptoms: - Truncated or cut-off responses - API errors about token limits - Answers that ignore relevant retrieved content (especially content at the beginning or middle of the context) - Degraded quality as similarity top k increases Fixes: - Use a response synthesizer like TreeSummarize or Refine instead of CompactAndRefine to handle large amounts of context - Reduce similarity top k and rely on reranking to surface only the most relevant chunks - Set explicit max tokens limits and monitor token counts with callback manager - Consider a summary index or recursive retrieval to compress context before synthesis 7. Missing Metadata Filtering What happens: The retriever searches across all documents when it should be scoped to a specific subset (for example, a certain date range, department, or document type). Symptoms: - Answers pull from wrong documents (for example, last year’s report when the user asks about this year) - Cross-contamination between document categories - Users report “the system knows too much” or returns unrelated content Fixes: - Add structured metadata (date, source, category, author) during ingestion - Use MetadataFilters at query time to scope retrieval - Implement auto-retrieval where the LLM extracts filter parameters from the user query - Use separate indices or namespaces for logically distinct document collections 8. Poor Query Understanding What happens: The user’s query is ambiguous, too short, or phrased differently from how information is stored in your documents. Symptoms: - Simple rephrasing of the query dramatically changes results - Short queries (one or two words) return poor results - Users need to “know the right words” to get good answers Fixes: - Add a query transformation step and use HyDEQueryTransform to generate a hypothetical answer and search with that - Use SubQuestionQueryEngine to break complex queries into simpler sub-queries - Implement query rewriting with an LLM to expand or rephrase the query - Add a few-shot prompt with example queries to guide users 9. LLM Synthesis Failures What happens: The retriever gets the right chunks, but the LLM fails to synthesize a good answer from them. Symptoms: - Retrieved chunks are correct (verified manually) but the answer is still wrong - The LLM ignores provided context and answers from its training data - Answers are overly generic despite specific context being available Fixes: - Use a stronger LLM for synthesis (for example, GPT-4o over GPT-4o-mini) or adjust temperature slightly - Customize the QA prompt template to explicitly instruct the LLM to use only the provided context - Use Refine response mode to process each chunk sequentially rather than all at once - Add a system prompt reinforcing that the LLM should answer based on context only 10. Embedding Metric Mismatch (Cosine Score ≠ True Meaning) What happens: The distance metric or normalization used for similarity does not line up with how meaning is distributed in your data. Very long or very generic chunks dominate similarity scores, while the truly relevant snippets sit lower in the ranking. Symptoms: - The top-1 result is clearly wrong, but relevant documents appear lower in the top-k list - Similarity scores for relevant and irrelevant chunks are tightly clustered together - Adding generic boilerplate text to documents changes retrieval behavior more than expected - Manual inspection shows that retrieval quality is sensitive to small preprocessing changes Fixes: - Inspect the full top-k list and check whether relevant chunks appear but are ranked too low - Normalize or trim overly long chunks so a few large nodes do not dominate similarity - Consider a reranking stage that uses a different scoring function from the base vector store - Evaluate retrieval with labeled queries before deploying (precision / recall on a small test set) and adjust similarity top k and thresholds based on results 11. Session and Cache Memory Breaks What happens: Users expect the system to remember previous interactions or configuration, but the underlying indices, vector stores, or caches are stateless or keyed incorrectly. Retrieval appears flaky across sessions even though the data is present. Symptoms: - The same question asked on different days returns answers from different subsets of documents - After a redeploy or cache clear, previously stable queries start to drift - Manually hitting the vector store with the same query sometimes returns an empty or much smaller result set Fixes: - Define a clear strategy for session and user keys and ensure they are passed consistently through your application, retrievers, and stores - Separate long-term knowledge from short-lived scratch space so cache eviction does not remove critical data - Log index versions, cache keys, and retrieval parameters for problematic requests and compare across sessions - Add a regression test that replays a short conversation or query sequence after each deploy to verify stability 12. Observability Gaps (“Black-Box Debugging”) What happens: You know that answers are wrong, but you cannot see what the retriever or LLM actually did. Without basic traces it becomes impossible to tell whether the issue is retrieval, synthesis, or deployment. Symptoms: - Bugs are reported as “it sometimes answers strangely” without reproducible traces - You cannot easily inspect which nodes were retrieved for a given bad answer - Token counts, prompts, and index metadata are not logged, so production runs cannot be reconstructed Fixes: - Enable tracing and logging for retrieval, query transforms, prompts, and responses (either through LlamaIndex callbacks or your own logging stack) - For each failed answer, capture at least: the user query, retrieved nodes, similarity scores, index or snapshot identifiers, and the final LLM prompt - Add a “debug mode” in your application that prints or stores retrieval results and decisions for manual inspection - Before changing infrastructure, try to reproduce failures using only logs and traces; if you cannot, improve observability first 13. Index Lifecycle and Deployment Ordering What happens: The pipeline works in local tests, but production behaves randomly because indices are empty, half-built, or misaligned with the running configuration. Services may start in the wrong order or point at the wrong storage. Symptoms: - Right after deployment, some queries return obviously incomplete or empty answers - Logs show that the vector store contains far fewer nodes than expected - Changing environment variables or secrets silently switches the index or embedding settings used at query time - Rolling back or redeploying changes answers again without any code changes Fixes: - Treat the index as a versioned artifact and track an index version or snapshot id in both ingestion and serving paths - Add a health check that runs a known-good query after deploy and fails if the index is empty, below a minimum size, or built with the wrong embedding config - Ensure ingestion or refresh jobs complete before routing production traffic to the new index - Avoid manual one-off ingestion steps; encode them in scripts or pipelines so they cannot be skipped accidentally Quick Diagnostic Flowchart Use this to narrow down where the problem is: 1. Check retrieval first: Print retrieved nodes and verify they contain the answer manually. - If retrieved nodes are wrong → Focus on items 1–5, 7–8 above. - If retrieved nodes are correct → Focus on items 6, 9 above. 2. Check a known-good query: Try a query where you know exactly which document contains the answer. - If it fails → Likely an indexing or embedding issue (items 3–5, 10, 13). - If it works → The issue is query-specific (items 1, 7–8, 11). 3. Check token counts: Log the total tokens sent to the LLM. - If near the limit → Context window overflow (item 6). - If well within limits → Synthesis or retrieval quality issue (items 1–5, 8–10, 12). 4. If problems only appear in production or after deploys: - Focus on system-level issues (items 11–13) and verify index versions, caches, and traces. title: 人機協作
text: 工具也可以定義能將人納入迴圈的工具。這對於需要人工輸入的任務很有用，例如確認工具呼叫或提供回饋。 如我們在 Workflows tutorial 中看到的，Workflows 在 AgentWorkflow 的底層運作方式是執行會發出和接收事件的步驟。以下是構成 AgentWorkflow 的步驟（藍色）以及在它們之間傳遞資料的事件（綠色）的圖表。你會認出這些事件，它們是我們在早期輸出流中處理的那些事件。 Workflows diagram 為了將人納入迴圈，我們會讓我們的工具發出一個未被 workflow 中任何其他步驟接收的事件。然後我們會告訴我們的工具等待接收一個特定的「reply」事件。 我們內建了 InputRequiredEvent 和 HumanResponseEvent 事件可用於此目的。如果你想捕捉不同形式的人工輸入，你可以繼承這些事件以符合你自己的偏好。讓我們匯入它們： 接下來，我們將建立一個執行假設危險任務的工具。這裡有幾件新事情發生： - wait for event 用於等待 HumanResponseEvent。 - waiter event 是寫入事件流的事件，讓呼叫者知道我們正在等待回應。 - waiter id 是此特定等待呼叫的唯一識別碼。它有助於確保我們為每個 waiter id 只發送一個 waiter event。 - requirements 參數用於指定我們希望等待具有特定 user name 的 HumanResponseEvent。 我們像往常一樣建立我們的 agent，將我們剛定義的工具傳遞給它： 現在我們可以執行 workflow，像處理任何其他串流事件一樣處理 InputRequiredEvent，並使用 send event 方法回應一個傳入的 HumanResponseEvent： 像往常一樣，你可以看到 this example 的完整程式碼。 你可以做任何你想捕捉的輸入；你可以使用 GUI、音訊輸入，甚至讓另一個獨立的 agent 參與其中。如果你的輸入需要花費時間，或發生在另一個程序中，你可能想 serialize the context 並將其儲存到資料庫或檔案，以便你稍後可以恢復 workflow。 說到讓其他 agents 參與其中，就引導我們進入下一節，詳細說明幾種建立 multi-agent systems 的方法。
sourceText: Tools can also be defined that get a human in the loop. This is useful for tasks that require human input, such as confirming a tool call or providing feedback. As we’ll see in our Workflows tutorial, the way Workflows work under the hood of AgentWorkflow is by running steps which both emit and receive events. Here’s a diagram of the steps (in blue) that make up an AgentWorkflow and the events (in green) that pass data between them. You’ll recognize these events, they’re the same ones we were handling in the output stream earlier. Workflows diagram To get a human in the loop, we’ll get our tool to emit an event that isn’t received by any other step in the workflow. We’ll then tell our tool to wait until it receives a specific “reply” event. We have built-in InputRequiredEvent and HumanResponseEvent events to use for this purpose. If you want to capture different forms of human input, you can subclass these events to match your own preferences. Let’s import them: Next we’ll create a tool that performs a hypothetical dangerous task. There are a couple of new things happening here: - wait for event is used to wait for a HumanResponseEvent. - The waiter event is the event that is written to the event stream, to let the caller know that we’re waiting for a response. - waiter id is a unique identifier for this specific wait call. It helps ensure that we only send one waiter event for each waiter id. - The requirements argument is used to specify that we want to wait for a HumanResponseEvent with a specific user name. We create our agent as usual, passing it the tool we just defined: Now we can run the workflow, handling the InputRequiredEvent just like any other streaming event, and responding with a HumanResponseEvent passed in using the send event method: As usual, you can see the full code of this example. You can do anything you want to capture the input; you could use a GUI, or audio input, or even get another, separate agent involved. If your input is going to take a while, or happen in another process, you might want to serialize the context and save it to a database or file so that you can resume the workflow later. Speaking of getting other agents involved brings us to our next section, detailing several ways to build multi-agent systems.

title: Multi-agent 模式在 LlamaIndex 中
text: 當需要多個專家來解決某個任務時，您在 LlamaIndex 中有幾種選擇，每種方式都在便利性與靈活性之間進行權衡。本文將介紹最常見的三種模式、何時選擇每種模式，並為每種方法提供一個最簡化的程式碼草圖。 1. AgentWorkflow (內建) – 宣告一組 agents，讓 AgentWorkflow 管理任務的交接。 Section 完整 Notebook 2. Orchestrator pattern (內建) – 一個「orchestrator」agent 決定下一個要呼叫哪個子 agent；這些子 agents 會作為 tools 暴露給它。 Section 完整 Notebook 3. Custom planner (DIY) – 您編寫 LLM prompt（通常是 XML / JSON），自行規劃步驟，並在程式碼中命令式地呼叫 agents。 Section 完整 Notebook --- 模式 1 – AgentWorkflow (即線性的「群體」模式) 何時使用 – 您希望即開箱即用地獲得多個 agent 的行為，幾乎不需要額外的程式碼，並且對 AgentWorkflow 附帶的預設交接決策感到滿意。 AgentWorkflow 本身就是一個 Workflow 預先配置好，可以理解 agents、狀態和 tool-calling。您提供一個包含一個或多個 agents 的 array ，告訴它應該從哪一個開始，它將會： 1. 將使用者訊息給 root agent。 2. 執行 agent 選擇的任何 tools。 3. 允許 agent 在決定時將控制權「交接」給另一個 agent。 4. 重複此過程，直到 agent 返回最終答案。 注意 ：在任何時候，當前活躍的 agent 可以選擇將控制權交還給使用者。 以下是 multi-agent 報告生成範例 的精簡版本。三個 agents 協作進行研究、撰寫和審閱報告。（… 表示為簡潔而省略的程式碼。） AgentWorkflow 負責所有的協調工作，並即時串流事件，以便您可以讓使用者了解進度。 --- 模式 2 – Orchestrator agent (子 agents 作為 tools) 何時使用 – 您希望有一個單一的地方決定 每一個 步驟，以便注入自訂邏輯，但您仍然傾向於使用宣告式的 agent as tool 體驗，而不是編寫您自己的規劃器。 在這個模式中，您仍然會建立專家的 agents（ResearchAgent、WriteAgent、ReviewAgent）， 但 您不要求它們彼此之間進行交接。相反地，您將每個 agent 的 run 方法暴露為一個 tool，並將這些 tool 提供給一個新的頂層 agent——即 Orchestrator 。 您可以在 agents\ as\ 工具 notebook 中看到完整的範例。 因為 orchestrator 只是另一個 FunctionAgent，您可以免費獲得串流、tool-calling 和狀態管理——同時您仍能完全控制 agents 的呼叫方式和整體控制流程（tools 始終回傳給 orchestrator）。 --- 模式 3 – Custom planner (DIY prompting + parsing) 何時使用 – 最大的靈活性。您需要強制執行非常特定的規劃格式、與外部排程器整合，或收集前述模式無法即開箱即用提供的額外元數據。 在這裡，想法是您編寫一個 prompt，指示 LLM 輸出一個結構化的計畫（XML / JSON / YAML）。您自己的 Python 程式碼解析該計畫並命令式地執行它。從屬的 agents 可以是任何東西——FunctionAgents、RAG pipelines 或其他服務。 以下是一個可以規劃、執行計畫並檢查是否需要進一步步驟的 workflow 的 最小 草圖。您可以在 自訂\ 多\ 代理人 notebook 中看到完整的範例。 此方法意味著 您 擁有協調迴圈，因此您可以插入所需的任何自訂邏輯、快取或人工介入檢查。 --- 選擇模式 Pattern 行數 彈性 內建串流/事件 :--- :--- :--- :--- AgentWorkflow ⭐ – 最少 ★★ 是 Orchestrator agent ⭐⭐ ★★★ 是 (透過 orchestrator) Custom planner ⭐⭐⭐ ★★★★★ 是 (透過 sub-agents)。頂層由您決定。 如果您需要快速原型設計，請從 AgentWorkflow 開始。當您需要對流程有更多控制時，請切換到 Orchestrator agent 。只有當前兩種模式無法表達您所需流程時，才使用 Custom planner 。 接下來您將學習如何使用 structured output in single and multi-agent workflows
sourceText: When more than one specialist is required to solve a task you have several options in LlamaIndex, each trading off convenience for flexibility. This page walks through the three most common patterns, when to choose each one, and provides a minimal code sketch for every approach. 1. AgentWorkflow (built-in) – declare a set of agents and let AgentWorkflow manage the hand-offs. Section Full Notebook 2. Orchestrator pattern (built-in) – an “orchestrator” agent chooses which sub-agent to call next; those sub-agents are exposed to it as tools . Section Full Notebook 3. Custom planner (DIY) – you write the LLM prompt (often XML / JSON) that plans the sequence yourself and imperatively invoke the agents in code. Section Full Notebook --- Pattern 1 – AgentWorkflow (i.e. linear “swarm” pattern) When to use – you want multi-agent behaviour out-of-the-box with almost no extra code, and you are happy with the default hand-off heuristics that ship with AgentWorkflow. AgentWorkflow is itself a Workflow pre-configured to understand agents, state and tool-calling. You supply an array of one or more agents, tell it which one should start, and it will: 1. Give the root agent the user message. 2. Execute whatever tools that agent selects. 3. Allow the agent to “handoff” control to another agent when it decides. 4. Repeat until an agent returns a final answer. NOTE: At any point, the current active agent can choose to return control back to the user. Below is the condensed version of the multi-agent report generation example. Three agents collaborate to research, write and review a report. (… indicates code omitted for brevity.) AgentWorkflow does all the orchestration, streaming events as it goes so you can keep users informed of progress. --- Pattern 2 – Orchestrator agent (sub-agents as tools) When to use – you want a single place that decides every step so you can inject custom logic, but you still prefer the declarative agent as tool experience over writing your own planner. In this pattern you still build specialist agents (ResearchAgent, WriteAgent, ReviewAgent), but you do not ask them to hand off to one another. Instead you expose each agent’s run method as a tool and give those tools to a new top-level agent – the Orchestrator . You can see the full example in the agents\ as\ tools notebook. Because the orchestrator is just another FunctionAgent you get streaming, tool-calling, and state management for free – yet you keep full control over how agents are called and the overall control flow (tools always return back to the orchestrator). --- Pattern 3 – Custom planner (DIY prompting + parsing) When to use – ultimate flexibility. You need to impose a very specific plan format, integrate with external schedulers, or gather additional metadata that the previous patterns cannot provide out-of-the-box. Here, the idea is that you write a prompt that instructs the LLM to output a structured plan (XML / JSON / YAML). Your own Python code parses that plan and imperatively executes it. The subordinate agents can be anything – FunctionAgents, RAG pipelines, or other services. Below is a minimal sketch of a workflow that can plan, execute a plan, and see if any further steps are needed. You can see the full example in the custom\ multi\ agent notebook. This approach means you own the orchestration loop, so you can insert whatever custom logic, caching or human-in-the-loop checks you require. --- Choosing a pattern Pattern Lines of code Flexibility Built-in streaming / events ------------------ ------------- ----------- --------------------------------------------- AgentWorkflow ⭐ – fewest ★★ Yes Orchestrator agent ⭐⭐ ★★★ Yes (via orchestrator) Custom planner ⭐⭐⭐ ★★★★★ Yes (via sub-agents). Top-level is up to you. If you are prototyping quickly, start with AgentWorkflow. Move to an Orchestrator agent when you need more control over the sequence. Reach for a Custom planner only when the first two patterns cannot express the flow you need. Next you will learn how to use structured output in single and multi-agent workflows

sourceText: By default, the AgentWorkflow is stateless between runs. This means that the agent will not have any memory of previous runs. To maintain state, we need to keep track of the previous state. In LlamaIndex, Workflows have a Context class that can be used to maintain state within and between runs. Since the AgentWorkflow is just a pre-built Workflow, we can also use it now. To maintain state between runs, we’ll create a new Context called ctx. We pass in our workflow to properly configure this Context object for the workflow that will use it. With our configured Context, we can pass it to our first run. Which gives us: And now if we run the workflow again to ask a follow-up question, it will remember that information: Which gives us: Maintaining state over longer periods The Context is serializable, so it can be saved to a database, file, etc. and loaded back in later. The JsonSerializer is a simple serializer that uses json.dumps and json.loads to serialize and deserialize the context. The JsonPickleSerializer is a serializer that uses pickle to serialize and deserialize the context. If you have objects in your context that are not serializable, you can use this serializer. We bring in our serializers as any other import: We can then serialize our context to a dictionary and save it to a file: We can deserialize it back into a Context object and ask questions just as before: You can see the full code of this example. This means you can set and retrieve variables from the context and use them in the tool, or to pass information between tools. AgentWorkflow uses a context variable called state that is available to every agent. You can rely on information in state being available without explicitly having to pass it in. To access the Context, the Context parameter should be the first parameter of the tool, as we’re doing here, in a tool that simply adds a name to the state: We can now create an agent that uses this tool. text: 在實際應用中，agents 可能需要較長時間才能執行。回饋用戶關於 agent 進度的資訊非常重要，串流（streaming）可以實現這一點。 AgentWorkflow 提供了一組預先建置的事件，您可以使用它們將輸出串流給用戶。讓我們看看如何操作。 提示 某些模型可能不支援串流 LLM 的輸出。雖然串流預設是開啟的，但如果您遇到錯誤，您可以將 FunctionAgent(..., streaming=False) 設定為停用串流。 首先，我們將介紹一個需要一些時間才能執行的新工具。在此例中，我們將使用一個名為 Tavily 的網路搜尋工具，它作為 llama-index-tools-tavily-research 套件提供。 終端機視窗 它需要一個 API 金鑰，我們將在我們的 .env 檔案中設定為 TAVILY API KEY 並使用 os.getenv 方法來檢索它。讓我們引入我們的匯入： 並初始化工具： 現在我們將使用該工具和我們先前初始化過的 LLM 來建立一個 agent。 在先前的範例中，我們使用 await 在 workflow.run 方法上獲取來自 agent 的最終回應。然而，如果我們不等待回應，我們會得到一個異步迭代器（asynchronous iterator），我們可以遍歷它以獲取事件的即時傳入。這個迭代器會回傳各種事件。我們將從一個 AgentStream 事件開始，它包含輸出中最新的「delta」（最接近的變更）。我們需要匯入該事件類型： 現在我們可以運行 workflow 並尋找該類型的事件來輸出： 如果您自己運行，您會看到輸出以區塊的形式到達，隨著 agent 運行，回傳類似這樣： AgentStream 只是 AgentWorkflow 在運行時發出的眾多事件之一。其他事件包括： - AgentInput：開始 agent 執行的完整訊息物件 - AgentOutput：來自 agent 的回應 - ToolCall：被呼叫的工具及其參數 - ToolCallResult：工具呼叫的結果 您可以在 此範例的完整程式碼 中看到我們過濾更多這些事件。 接下來，您將了解如何讓 human in the loop 提供回饋給您的 agents。
sourceText: In real-world use, agents can take a long time to run. Providing feedback to the user about the progress of the agent is critical, and streaming allows you to do that. AgentWorkflow provides a set of pre-built events that you can use to stream output to the user. Let’s take a look at how that’s done. Tip Some models might not support streaming LLM output. While streaming is enabled by default, if you encounter an error, you can always set FunctionAgent(..., streaming=False) to disable streaming. First, we’re going to introduce a new tool that takes some time to execute. In this case we’ll use a web search tool called Tavily, available as the llama-index-tools-tavily-research package. Terminal window It requires an API key, which we’re going to set in our .env file as TAVILY API KEY and retrieve using the os.getenv method. Let’s bring in our imports: And initialize the tool: Now we’ll create an agent using that tool and an LLM that we initialized just like we did previously. In previous examples, we’ve used await on the workflow.run method to get the final response from the agent. However, if we don’t await the response, we get an asynchronous iterator back that we can iterate over to get the events as they come in. This iterator will return all sorts of events. We’ll start with an AgentStream event, which contains the “delta” (the most recent change) to the output as it comes in. We’ll need to import that event type: And now we can run the workflow and look for events of that type to output: If you run this yourself, you will see the output arriving in chunks as the agent runs, returning something like this: AgentStream is just one of many events that AgentWorkflow emits as it runs. The others are: - AgentInput: the full message object that begins the agent’s execution - AgentOutput: the response from the agent - ToolCall: which tools were called and with what arguments - ToolCallResult: the result of a tool call You can see us filtering for more of these events in the full code of this example. Next you’ll learn about how to get a human in the loop to provide feedback to your agents.

sourceText: Most of the time you need results from an agent in a specific format. Agents results can return structured json in two ways: 1. output cls – a Pydantic model to use as a schema for the output 2. structured output fn – For more advanced use cases, supply a custom function that validates or rewrites the agent’s conversation into any model you want. title: 使用現有工具
text: 現在您已經建置了強大的 agent，我們希望您對它所能做的一切感到興奮。擴展 agent 功能的核心是可用的工具，我們有好消息：LlamaIndex 擁有數百個整合，包括 數十個現有的 agent 工具，您可以立即使用它們。我們將向您示範如何使用現有的工具，以及如何建立和貢獻您自己的工具。 使用現有工具 以我們的範例，我們將使用 Yahoo Finance tool。它提供了一套六個 agent 工具，用於查詢股票代號的各種資訊。 首先，我們需要安裝該工具： 終端機視窗 我們的依賴項與先前的範例相同，我們只需要新增 Yahoo Finance 工具： 為了示範如何將自訂工具與預建工具組合，我們將保留 add 和 multiply 函式，儘管在這裡我們不需要它們。我們將引入我們的工具： 工具列表只是一個 array，因此我們可以利用 Python 的 extend 方法將我們自己的工具加入其中： 我們將提出一個不同於上次的問題，這需要使用新的工具： 我們得到這個回應： （這有點作弊，因為我們的模型已經知道 NVIDIA 的代號。如果它是一家較不知名的公司，您需要新增一個搜尋工具，例如 Tavily，來找到代號。） 就是這樣！您現在可以在您的 agents 中使用任何預建的工具整合。 一如既往，您可以查看 the repo 以在一個地方看到這段程式碼。 建置和貢獻您自己的工具 我們很喜歡新的工具的開源貢獻！您可以查看 Yahoo finance tool 的程式碼看起來像什麼： - 一個擴展 BaseToolSpec 的 class - 一組任意的 Python functions - 一個映射了函式到工具 API 的 spec functions list 一旦您成功建立了一個工具，請遵循我們的 contributing guide 以獲取關於正確設定 metadata 和提交 pull request 的說明。 接下來我們將探討 如何在您的 agents 中維護 state。
sourceText: Now that you’ve built a capable agent, we hope you’re excited about all it can do. The core of expanding agent capabilities is the tools available, and we have good news: LlamaIndex has hundreds of integrations, including dozens of existing agent tools that you can use right away. We’ll show you how to use one of the existing tools, and also how to build and contribute your own. Using an existing tool For our example, we’re going to use the Yahoo Finance tool. It provides a set of six agent tools that look up a variety of information about stock ticker symbols. First we need to install the tool: Terminal window Our dependencies are the same as our previous example, we just need to add the Yahoo Finance tools: To show how you can combine custom tools with pre-built tools, we’re going to leave the add and multiply functions in place even though we don’t need them here. We’ll bring in our tools: A tool list is just an array, so we can use Python’s extend method to add our own tools to the mix: And we’ll ask a different question than last time, necessitating the use of the new tools: We get this response: (This is cheating a little bit, because our model already knew the ticker symbol for NVIDIA. If it were a less well-known corporation you would need to add a search tool like Tavily to find the ticker symbol.) And that’s it! You can now use any of the pre-built tool integrations in your agents. As always, you can check the repo to see this code all in one place. Building and contributing your own tools We love open source contributions of new tools! You can see an example of what the code of the Yahoo finance tool looks like: - A class that extends BaseToolSpec - A set of arbitrary Python functions - A spec functions list that maps the functions to the tool’s API Once you’ve got a tool working, follow our contributing guide for instructions on correctly setting metadata and submitting a pull request. Next we’ll look at how to maintain state in your agents.

text: 在 LlamaIndex 中，一個 agent 是一個半自主軟體，由 LLM 驅動，它會被賦予一個任務並執行一系列步驟來解決該任務。它會被給予一組工具，這些工具可以是任意函數，直到完整的 LlamaIndex query engines，並且它會選擇最適合的可用工具來完成每一步。當每一步完成後，agent 會判斷任務是否已完成，如果是，它會將結果回傳給使用者，否則它需要採取下一步，這時會回到開始。 在 LlamaIndex 中，你可以從頭開始 建構你自己的 agentic workflows，內容涵蓋在「Building Workflows」部分，或者你可以使用我們預先建置的 agentic workflows，例如 FunctionAgent（一個簡單的 function/tool calling agent）或 AgentWorkflow（一個能夠管理多個 agents 的 agent）。本教學涵蓋如何使用 FunctionAgent 建構一個 function calling agent。 要了解建構多個 agent 系統的各種方法，請前往 “Multi-agent systems”。 agent flow 開始使用 你可以在 agents 教學儲存庫 中找到所有這些程式碼。 為了避免衝突並保持環境乾淨，我們將建立一個新的 Python 虛擬環境。你可以使用任何虛擬環境管理器，但我們在這裡使用 poetry： 終端機視窗 然後我們將安裝 LlamaIndex 函式庫以及一些有用的其他依賴項： 終端機視窗 如果這些操作有任何問題，請查看我們的詳細 安裝指南。 OpenAI Key 我們的 agent 將由 OpenAI 的 gpt-4o-mini LLM 驅動，因此你需要一個 API key。取得金鑰後，你可以將其放入專案根目錄中的一個 .env 檔案中： 終端機視窗 如果你不想使用 OpenAI，你可以使用 任何其他 LLM，包括本地模型。Agents 需要具備能力的模型，因此較小的模型可能不太可靠。 引入依賴項 我們將從匯入 LlamaIndex 所需的組件開始，同時從我們的 .env 檔案中載入環境變數： 建立基本工具 對於這個簡單的範例，我們將建立兩個工具：一個知道如何將數字相乘，另一個知道如何將數字相加。 如你所見，這些是普通的 Python 函數。在決定使用哪個工具時，你的 agent 會使用工具的名稱、參數和 docstring 來判斷該工具的作用以及它是否適合當前的任務。因此，確保 docstring 具有描述性和實用性非常重要。它也會使用 type hints 來判斷預期的參數和回傳類型。 初始化 LLM gpt-4o-mini 將負責今天的運作： 你也可以選擇透過 API 存取的另一個流行模型，例如來自 Mistral、Claude from Anthropic 或 Gemini from Google。 初始化 agent 現在我們建立我們的 agent。它需要一個工具陣列、一個 LLM，以及一個 system prompt 來告訴它應該成為什麼樣的 agent。你的 system prompt 通常會比這個更詳細！ GPT-4o-mini 實際上足夠聰明，不需要工具來完成如此簡單的數學運算，這就是為什麼我們在 prompt 中指定它應該使用工具。 除了 FunctionAgent 之外，在 LlamaIndex 中還有其他 agents 可用，例如 ReActAgent 和 CodeActAgent，它們使用不同的 prompting 策略來執行工具。 提問現在我們可以要求 agent 進行一些數學運算： 請注意，這是異步程式碼。它可以在 notebook 環境中運行，但如果你想在一般的 Python 中運行它，你需要將它包裝成一個異步函式，如下所示： 這應該會給你類似以下的輸出： 提示 有些模型可能不支援串流 LLM 輸出。雖然預設開啟串流，但如果你遇到錯誤，你可以隨時設定 FunctionAgent(..., streaming=False) 來禁用串流。 請查看 repo 以查看最終程式碼應該是什麼樣子。 恭喜！你已經建構了最基本的 agent。接下來我們來學習如何使用 pre-built tools。
sourceText: In LlamaIndex, an agent is a semi-autonomous piece of software powered by an LLM that is given a task and executes a series of steps towards solving that task. It is given a set of tools, which can be anything from arbitrary functions up to full LlamaIndex query engines, and it selects the best available tool to complete each step. When each step is completed, the agent judges whether the task is now complete, in which case it returns a result to the user, or whether it needs to take another step, in which case it loops back to the start. In LlamaIndex, you can either build your own agentic workflows from scratch, covered in the “Building Workflows” section, or you can use our pre-built agentic workflows like FunctionAgent (a simple function/tool calling agent) or AgentWorkflow (an agent capable of managing multiple agents). This tutorial covers building a function calling agent using FunctionAgent. To learn about the various ways to build multi-agent systems, go to “Multi-agent systems”. agent flow Getting started You can find all of this code in the agents tutorial repo. To avoid conflicts and keep things clean, we’ll start a new Python virtual environment. You can use any virtual environment manager, but we’ll use poetry here: Terminal window And then we’ll install the LlamaIndex library and some other dependencies that will come in handy: Terminal window If any of this gives you trouble, check out our more detailed installation guide. OpenAI Key Our agent will be powered by OpenAI’s gpt-4o-mini LLM, so you’ll need an API key. Once you have your key, you can put it in a .env file in the root of your project: Terminal window If you don’t want to use OpenAI, you can use any other LLM including local models. Agents require capable models, so smaller models may be less reliable. Bring in dependencies We’ll start by importing the components of LlamaIndex we need, as well as loading the environment variables from our .env file: Create basic tools For this simple example we’ll be creating two tools: one that knows how to multiply numbers together, and one that knows how to add them. As you can see, these are regular Python functions. When deciding what tool to use, your agent will use the tool’s name, parameters, and docstring to determine what the tool does and whether it’s appropriate for the task at hand. So it’s important to make sure the docstrings are descriptive and helpful. It will also use the type hints to determine the expected parameters and return type. Initialize the LLM gpt-4o-mini is going to be doing the work today: You could also pick another popular model accessible via API, such as those from Mistral, Claude from Anthropic or Gemini from Google. Initialize the agent Now we create our agent. It needs an array of tools, an LLM, and a system prompt to tell it what kind of agent to be. Your system prompt would usually be more detailed than this! GPT-4o-mini is actually smart enough to not need tools to do such simple math, which is why we specified that it should use tools in the prompt. Beyond FunctionAgent, there are other agents available in LlamaIndex, such as ReActAgent and CodeActAgent, which use different prompting strategies to execute tools. Ask a question Now we can ask the agent to do some math: Note that this is asynchronous code. It will work in a notebook environment, but if you want to run it in regular Python you’ll need to wrap it an asynchronous function, like this: This should give you output similar to the following: Tip Some models might not support streaming LLM output. While streaming is enabled by default, if you encounter an error, you can always set FunctionAgent(..., streaming=False) to disable streaming. Check the repo to see what the final code should look like. Congratulations! You’ve built the most basic kind of agent. Next let’s learn how to use pre-built tools.

text: 概念 每次呼叫 LLM 都會產生一定的費用——例如，OpenAI 的 gpt-3.5-turbo 費用為每 1k tokens $0.002。建立索引和查詢的費用取決於 - 使用的 LLM 的類型 - 使用的資料結構類型 - 建立時使用的參數 - 查詢時使用的參數 每個索引的建立和查詢費用請參閱參考文件中的 TODO。在此期間，我們提供以下資訊： 1. 索引的成本結構的高階概述。 2. 一個您可以直接在 LlamaIndex 中使用的 token 預測器。 成本結構概述 沒有 LLM 呼叫的索引 以下索引在建立過程中不需要 LLM 呼叫（成本為 0）： - SummaryIndex - SimpleKeywordTableIndex - 使用 regex keyword extractor 從每個 document 中提取關鍵字 - RAKEKeywordTableIndex - 使用 RAKE keyword extractor 從每個 document 中提取關鍵字 有 LLM 呼叫的索引 以下索引在建構期間需要 LLM 呼叫： - TreeIndex - 使用 LLM 對文本進行層級摘要以建立樹狀結構 - KeywordTableIndex - 使用 LLM 從每個 document 中提取關鍵字 查詢時間 在查詢時間中，為了合成最終答案，總會有 $\ge 1$ 次 LLM 呼叫。有些索引在索引建立和查詢之間存在成本權衡。例如，SummaryIndex 可以免費建立，但對摘要索引（不進行過濾或 embedding 查找）進行查詢時，會呼叫 LLM {math}N 次。 以下是關於每個索引的一些備註： - SummaryIndex：預設需要 {math}N LLM 呼叫，其中 N 是 nodes 的數量。 - TreeIndex：預設需要 {math}\log (N) LLM 呼叫，其中 N 是葉子 nodes 的數量。 - 設定 child branch factor=2 會比預設的 child branch factor=1（多項式 vs 對數）更昂貴，因為對於每個父級 node，我們遍歷了 2 個子節點而不是僅 1 個。 - KeywordTableIndex：預設需要一個 LLM 呼叫來提取查詢關鍵字。 - 可以使用 index.as retriever(retriever mode="simple") 或 index.as retriever(retriever mode="rake") 在您的查詢文本上使用 regex/RAKE keyword extractors。 - VectorStoreIndex：預設每個查詢需要一次 LLM 呼叫。如果您增加 similarity top k 或 chunk size，或更改 response mode，則此數字會增加。 使用模式 LlamaIndex 提供 token predictors 來預測 LLM 和 embedding 呼叫的 token 使用量。這讓您在進行 1) 索引建構和 2) 索引查詢之前，估計您的成本，在任何相應的 LLM 呼叫發生之前。 Token 是使用 TokenCountingHandler 回調來計算的。請參閱 範例 notebook 以了解設置詳情。 使用 MockLLM 要預測 LLM 呼叫的 token 使用量，請匯入並實例化 MockLLM 如下所示。max tokens 參數用作「最壞情況」預測，其中每個 LLM 回應將包含確切該數量的 tokens。如果未指定 max tokens，它將僅預測提示詞。 然後您可以在索引建構和查詢期間使用此預測器。 使用 MockEmbedding 您也可以使用 MockEmbedding 預測 embedding 呼叫的 token 使用量。 使用模式 閱讀 完整使用模式 以獲取更多詳情！
sourceText: Concept Each call to an LLM will cost some amount of money - for instance, OpenAI’s gpt-3.5-turbo costs $0.002 / 1k tokens. The cost of building an index and querying depends on - the type of LLM used - the type of data structure used - parameters used during building - parameters used during querying The cost of building and querying each index is a TODO in the reference documentation. In the meantime, we provide the following information: 1. A high-level overview of the cost structure of the indices. 2. A token predictor that you can use directly within LlamaIndex! Overview of Cost Structure Indices with no LLM calls The following indices don’t require LLM calls at all during building (0 cost): - SummaryIndex - SimpleKeywordTableIndex - uses a regex keyword extractor to extract keywords from each document - RAKEKeywordTableIndex - uses a RAKE keyword extractor to extract keywords from each document Indices with LLM calls The following indices do require LLM calls during build time: - TreeIndex - use LLM to hierarchically summarize the text to build the tree - KeywordTableIndex - use LLM to extract keywords from each document Query Time There will always be = 1 LLM call during query time, in order to synthesize the final answer. Some indices contain cost tradeoffs between index building and querying. SummaryIndex, for instance, is free to build, but running a query over a summary index (without filtering or embedding lookups), will call the LLM {math}N times. Here are some notes regarding each of the indices: - SummaryIndex: by default requires {math}N LLM calls, where N is the number of nodes. - TreeIndex: by default requires {math}\log (N) LLM calls, where N is the number of leaf nodes. - Setting child branch factor=2 will be more expensive than the default child branch factor=1 (polynomial vs logarithmic), because we traverse 2 children instead of just 1 for each parent node. - KeywordTableIndex: by default requires an LLM call to extract query keywords. - Can do index.as retriever(retriever mode="simple") or index.as retriever(retriever mode="rake") to also use regex/RAKE keyword extractors on your query text. - VectorStoreIndex: by default, requires one LLM call per query. If you increase the similarity top k or chunk size, or change the response mode, then this number will increase. Usage Pattern LlamaIndex offers token predictors to predict token usage of LLM and embedding calls. This allows you to estimate your costs during 1) index construction, and 2) index querying, before any respective LLM calls are made. Tokens are counted using the TokenCountingHandler callback. See the example notebook for details on the setup. Using MockLLM To predict token usage of LLM calls, import and instantiate the MockLLM as shown below. The max tokens parameter is used as a “worst case” prediction, where each LLM response will contain exactly that number of tokens. If max tokens is not specified, then it will simply predict back the prompt. You can then use this predictor during both index construction and querying. Using MockEmbedding You may also predict the token usage of embedding calls with MockEmbedding. Usage Pattern Read about the full usage pattern for more details!

title: 評估
text: 評估和基準測試是 LLM 開發中的關鍵概念。為了提升 LLM 應用程式（RAG, agents）的效能，您必須有方法來衡量它。 LlamaIndex 提供關鍵模組來衡量生成結果的品質。我們也提供關鍵模組來衡量檢索品質。您可以在我們的 module guides 中了解 LlamaIndex 中評估是如何運作的。 回應評估 回應是否符合檢索的上下文？它是否也符合查詢？它是否符合參考答案或指南？以下是一個簡單的範例，用於評估單一回應的忠實度（Faithfulness），即回應是否與上下文一致，例如是否沒有產生幻覺： 回應包含回應本身以及生成該回應的來源；評估器會比較它們並判斷回應是否忠於來源。 您可以在我們的模組指南中了解更多關於 response evaluation 的資訊。 檢索評估 檢索到的來源是否與查詢相關？這是一個評估單一檢索的簡單範例： 這會比較為查詢檢索到的內容與預期應檢索的一組 nodes。 在現實中，您會希望評估一整批檢索結果；您可以在關於 retrieval evaluation 的模組指南中了解如何做到這一點。 相關概念 如果您正在呼叫託管的、遠端的 LLM，您可能會對 分析您的應用程式成本 感興趣。
sourceText: Evaluation and benchmarking are crucial concepts in LLM development. To improve the performance of an LLM app (RAG, agents), you must have a way to measure it. LlamaIndex offers key modules to measure the quality of generated results. We also offer key modules to measure retrieval quality. You can learn more about how evaluation works in LlamaIndex in our module guides. Response Evaluation Does the response match the retrieved context? Does it also match the query? Does it match the reference answer or guidelines? Here’s a simple example that evaluates a single response for Faithfulness, i.e. whether the response is aligned to the context, such as being free from hallucinations: The response contains both the response and the source from which the response was generated; the evaluator compares them and determines if the response is faithful to the source. You can learn more in our module guides about response evaluation. Retrieval Evaluation Are the retrieved sources relevant to the query? This is a simple example that evaluates a single retrieval: This compares what was retrieved for the query to a set of nodes that were expected to be retrieved. In reality you would want to evaluate a whole batch of retrievals; you can learn how do this in our module guide on retrieval evaluation. Related concepts You may be interested in analyzing the cost of your application if you are making calls to a hosted, remote LLM.
